items.north_star_item: §1 Temporally situated self S_t = {W,K,B,G,C,U,D,O} as one addressable object per t
covered_by: Shepherd arXiv:2605.10913 [V; deep read of code/blog, paper body unread]
ActiveGraph arXiv:2605.21997, github yoheinakajima/activegraph v1.12 [V; code + probe]
items.residual: Each of the eight components already exists as typed state somewhere. W = valid-time facts (Memvara valid_at, XTDB FOR VALID_TIME, Graphiti valid_at). K = transaction time (Memvara known_at, XTDB FOR SYSTEM_TIME). B = PoS world records with probability and observed/inferred tags, plus DeepRewind Assumption/Hypothesis nodes. G = PoS Goal, AER versioned plans, FlowState objective judgements. C = Trellis prompt_history ('exact messages the LLM saw'), AER retrieval context, Shepherd PromptSent. U = PoS epistemic gaps, Forecast-Dojo open_questions. D = AER verdict with alternatives_rejected, DeepRewind Commitment. O = PIS/PM-Bench intentions and PoS achievement gaps. Shepherd's process fork, or ActiveGraph's as-of projection (build_base_graph), restores everything held in agent state at any event. What is missing is one schema that types all eight together, and that is glue. No work shows that typing the 8-tuple changes behaviour beyond what the parts already do.
items.evidence: Shepherd: 'state(t) = fold(apply_effect, effects[0:t], initial_state)'; a scope fork copies the process, context and OverlayFS. ActiveGraph probe B: promote.build_base_graph(g,e) works as state_at(e). Verified ratings: PoS #10 yes and #11 yes; Memvara #2, #3 and #19 yes; Trellis #3 and #19 yes. Cap 20 (unified abstraction) is at most 'partial' in every digest.

items.north_star_item: §1/§17 Agent as a family of selves S_t1..S_now plus simulated future selves
covered_by: IDs for AI Systems arXiv:2406.12137 [L; lane mention via digest, not in dedup list]
items.residual: Per-step checkpoints with fork lineage materialize the historical family: LangGraph checkpoint tree, ActiveGraph (parent_run_id, forked_at_event_id), Shepherd commit graph. Imagined successors come from ITP policy-conditioned rollouts. Instance identity across reloads and branches has been proposed (IDs for AI Systems, unverified). Calling these 'selves' is vocabulary.
items.evidence: LangGraph docs: 'update_state does not roll back a thread. It creates a new checkpoint that branches from the specified point.' ITP verified #12 future_state_rollout = yes. Shepherd archives discarded worlds (DiscardSnapshot with parent_world_id).

items.north_star_item: §2 Past: events immutable, interpretation revisable; reconstruction, provenance, reinterpretation, no rewriting
covered_by: Corollary github gabe-santana/corollary [N; C, 386 tests run]
items.residual: Conceptually nothing is left. This is the textbook split between valid time and transaction time, plus invalidate-not-delete. Graphiti invalidates rather than deletes. Memvara distinguishes 'ended' (the world changed) from 'retired' (the record was wrong). Kumiho has immutable revisions with formal belief-revision properties. DeepRewind's docstring reads 'beliefs are never silently overwritten ... we add a revises/invalidates edge'. PROV has wasRevisionOf and wasInvalidatedBy. The only defects are implementation bugs: Graphiti MERGE+SET upserts and Memvara's in-place valid_to stamping.
items.evidence: XTDB docs: auditing needs data 'as we knew it at the time, _without_ subsequent corrections - this is the use case for FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF'. Temporal-memory lane verdict: 'textbook bitemporal practice'.

items.north_star_item: §2 Present: the boundary between committed history and open possibility; only the present self affects the committed world
items.residual: Shepherd's speculative scopes cannot escape effects ('Gate before escape, not reverse after'; ContainmentError if effects after a checkpoint were materialized). MemTX keeps recording an observation separate from committing a belief, and gates irreversible tool calls on the committed state. Datomic d/with gives speculative, uncommitted values. ITP's POIMDP makes 'observable stream = present' and 'imaginable stream = future' a software boundary. 'Control surface of temporal agency' is a new name for this.
items.evidence: Shepherd deep read: speculate/gate combinators, 'ContainmentError: If effects after checkpoint were materialized'. MemTX: action-safety invariants model-checked over 5.5M states. ITP docs: 'the POIMDP concept is expressed as a software boundary'.

Several systems that claim parts of it violate them, which says engineering discipline is the gap, not concept.

items.north_star_item: §5 Executable past self with strict epistemic cutoff knowledge(past_self_t) <= t; 'ask the former self' rather than reconstruct
covered_by: Shepherd fork (byte-identical prefix replay, ~95% KV reuse) [V]
Forecast-Dojo cutoff at search and scrape [V]
A Historical Corpus Is Not a Historical System arXiv:2609.12766 [U]
items.residual:
Every ingredient exists. The cutoff is a named, mature problem with methods, audits and documented failure modes. The project cannot claim it. Two things are left.
(a) End-to-end, leakage-audited enforcement over memory, tool caches, KV cache and model version in one runtime. This is engineering.
(b) An untested empirical question: does interrogating an executable past self beat retrieval over equally rich contemporaneous records (AER-grade)? docs/milestone-2-design.md §0 concedes the current benchmark cannot test this, because decisions are world-authored.
Adversarially, re-executing a stochastic LLM on a restored prefix is itself a reconstruction: AER calls this 'inference volatility'. The only faithful 'former self' is a deterministic or cached replay, and that just returns the logged answer. 'Asking' adds over 'reconstructing' only for questions that were never logged, and nobody has shown those matter.
items.evidence: ChronoMem: prompt-only rollback 0.9-2.8 F1 vs snapshot restore 31-38 F1 (secondary reader numbers). Epistemic-cutoff lane: 'The project therefore cannot claim the cutoff discipline, the past-self query, or knowledge of its failure modes as contributions.' Milestone-2 §0: 'Testing ... talking to an executable past-self that strong retrieval cannot reproduce ... needs a future experiment.'

items.north_star_item: §5 Questions a past self answers: why, what it believed, what it was uncertain about, which alternatives it had rejected, what information it was waiting for
covered_by: AER intent/inference + verdict.alternatives_rejected with rejected_by step + confidence [V]
FlowState D7 judgement with linked evidence [S]
items.residual: Every listed question has a contemporaneous record field that answers it without executing anything. Only questions nobody anticipated would need execution, and that falls under the §5 measurable_effect item.
items.evidence: AER verdict.json: confidence, evidence_chain, alternatives_rejected (with rejected_by step pointers). PoS: belief_update_history written at commit time, so 'they contain no hindsight' (verifier).

items.north_star_item: §6 Simulated future selves Ŝ^a_{t+Δ} = simulate(S_t, a, Δ), several per decision
covered_by: Future You arXiv:2405.12514, 2512.06106; Simulating Life Paths arXiv:2512.05397 [V]
Current Agents Fail to Leverage World Model arXiv:2601.03905 [V]
items.residual: The mechanism is covered. ITP-R alternates the agent's own policy action with a world-model step K times; Shepherd runs executed lookahead in speculative forks; prefix branching runs several candidate actions from identical states. None of these frames the rollout as the agent's own future self with changed objectives or policy. No work evaluates interrogating such a self. Human future-self studies show psychological effects and persuasion, not better decisions. The agent-side evidence is negative: agents rarely use world-model foresight and often misuse it. What is left is a framing plus a missing test.
items.evidence: Prospective lane: 'Not found: any agent that interrogates a simulated future version of itself (future policy, objectives or identity) and shows a measured decision benefit. This is the only unoccupied slice, and it has no supporting evidence either.' 2601.03905: simulation invoked in <1% of cases, misused ~15%, up to 5% performance loss.

items.north_star_item: §6 Q: 'What problems do you inherit from me?'
covered_by: SeerGuard arXiv:2607.15550 / MirrorGuard arXiv:2601.12822 [low; title discrepancy noted]
items.residual: This is predicted latent risk fed back into the current decision. SafePred aligns 'predicted future risks with current decisions' through step-level interventions and re-planning. SIMMER benchmarks latent failures with a world model. Saying it in the first person adds nothing.
items.evidence: Backward-optionality lane: 'SIMMER (2606.14574): foresight simulation cuts irreversible failures by up to 75%'.

items.north_star_item: §6 Q: 'Which decision of mine do you regret?'
items.evidence: Calibration Is Not Control: a prefix-only action-conditioned controller cuts regret from 0.506 to 0.110 on ALFWorld (abstract; units unverified). Shepherd: the selector returns {branch_turn, reason}.

items.north_star_item: §6 Q: 'What information do you wish I had collected?'
covered_by: DeepRewind TC gate / 'retain as contested' [V; code]
items.residual: This is value of information before commitment. DeepRewind blocks a commit when probe coverage is low and keeps researching. SafeCommit takes a 'low-side-effect probe' when the action is not safe in every retained world. FinalityBench finds that LLMs discover finality gating unprompted.
items.evidence: DeepRewind code: decide() returns not_commit if IRR·(1−TC) > τ. Backward lane: SafeCommit 'act only if safe in every retained world, otherwise take a low-side-effect probe or fallback'.

items.north_star_item: §6 Q: 'Which option do you wish I had preserved?'
covered_by: Relative reachability / Krakovna future tasks arXiv:1806.01186 [U]
items.residual: Option preservation from hypothetical future goals was formalized in 2018-2020 (unverified ids). Verified 2025-2026 agent versions exist: Heitzig & Potham do it by backward induction; LCPI homogenizes toward a common continuation.
items.evidence: Backward lane verdict: 'The project should drop backward requirements and option preservation as novelty claims.'

items.north_star_item: §6 Q: 'What must I do now for your future to remain reachable?'
items.residual: This is goal regression or backward chaining from a desired state, plus receding-horizon 'reason for future, act for now'.
items.evidence: Backward lane: 'LLM backward planning exists: BAR (2505.14079, planning starting from the terminal state)'. RAFA: 'plan a long-horizon trajectory, execute the first action, replan, with sqrt(T) regret'.

items.north_star_item: §7 Backward requirements: dated precondition chains derived from a desired future and sent back into present action
items.residual: The pieces exist: derivation (BAR, goal regression), persistence as typed time- and event-triggered obligations (PIS), and derivation links rechecked before acting (PlanFence, Corollary TTL). The backward lane's real gap is that obligations derived from feared or desired futures are consumed at decision time and never kept as timestamped, provenance-carrying state that is rechecked as events arrive. BAR feeding a PIS store with PlanFence links closes that mechanically. No evidence that it helps. The lane notes a 're-check prior commitments' prompt may close the gap too.
items.evidence: Backward lane Q2(1): 'None stores derived obligations ... as first-class, timestamped, provenance-carrying state that is re-checked as later events arrive.' PIS: 82.9% Set-F1 with lifecycle logic in code. PlanFence: 30/30 vs 0/30.

items.north_star_item: §8 Forecasts branch, not overwrite: prevented futures are not failed predictions
covered_by: Potential outcomes (Dickerman & Hernán [N]; Keogh & van Geloven; Boyer et al.)
Metaculus Conditional Pairs annulment + forecasting-tools ANNULLED [N]
Decision markets (Othman & Sandholm; Chen et al.; Oesterheld & Conitzer) [bibliography]
Reflexive Model-World Systems (Sorenson, GitHub preprint, not peer-reviewed) [N]
items.residual: The principle is established, almost word for word. Reflexive Model-World Systems: 'A successful prediction can therefore become observationally false because it was causally effective.' Scoring is covered by annulment and potential outcomes. Not found: a long-lived LLM agent that keeps averted forecasts as queryable objects (forecaster or policy version, cutoff, triggering intervention, status annulled/checked/unverifiable). That is schema and bookkeeping. The literature also turns against the claim: a deterministic agent that always intervenes violates positivity, so its 'prevented' labels cannot be verified without randomization, holdouts or a trusted simulator.
items.evidence: Performative lane verdict: 'What is left is narrow and largely engineering ... The benchmark should treat prevented as annulled rather than scored, unless the scenario supplies verifiable counterfactual ground truth.' Metaculus: the other conditional 'is Annulled ... It is not scored'.

items.north_star_item: §9 Reflexivity taxonomy: passive / policy-conditioned / intervention-aware / reflexive forecasts
items.evidence: Performative lane Q2 lists all four with sources. Calibration Is Not Control names the passive-forecast failure 'target error'.

items.north_star_item: §9 'An agent must know when observing a prediction changes the trajectory being predicted' (runtime detection and scoring of its own reflexive forecasts)
items.residual: An agent-side reflexivity detector, or a scored evaluation of one, is not found. The 2026 survey lists it as future work. Adversarially, for a single agent the only causal path from forecast to world is the agent's own action, so 'reflexive' collapses into policy-conditioned forecasting, which is covered. True reflexivity needs other actors reacting to a published forecast, which NORTH_STAR does not model. Self-scoring reflexive forecasts also creates manipulation incentives. The gap is narrow, possibly ill-posed here, and has no evidence of value.
items.evidence: Prospective lane: the survey 2608.23058 says 'existing evaluations do not yet establish reflexive effects'. Performative lane: 'no proper scoring rule makes reports fixed points for more than two outcomes'.

items.north_star_item: §10 Uncertainty grows with horizon: specific state near, scenario branches medium, distributions far

No digest work states a rule that switches representation by horizon. That rule is a design choice composed from existing parts, with no evidence it helps.
items.evidence: ITP verified #12 yes and #14 no. FutureSim #14 yes. Prospective lane: ForecastBench-Sim generates 'forecasting questions at arbitrary time horizons, paired intervention worlds'.

items.north_star_item: §11 Uncertainty about the past: certain / probable / disputed / unknown, and time coordinates with confidence intervals
covered_by: Memvara confidence, temporal_precision, Dispute, ended vs retired [N; C]

No digest work represents interval-valued, confidence-weighted event times ('between March 3 and March 8') with as-of semantics. Extending Memvara's temporal_precision to [earliest, latest, confidence] is a schema change.

items.north_star_item: §12 Identity continuity vs state continuity (objectives, model, tools, instructions, policies, values, role)
covered_by: OpenTelemetry GenAI semconv (gen_ai.agent.version, prompt.version, system_instructions, request.model) [N]
LangSmith assistant versioning + Context Hub commits [N]
LangGraph checkpoint metadata config keys [C; verifier probe]
items.residual: Recording which identity, policy, model or objective governed each step is standardized (OTel) and shipped (LangSmith, MLflow, Langfuse). Lineage of self-modification is routine (DGM, Autogenesis). Identity hysteresis is measured (Layered Mutability). The exchange 'that objective no longer governs me' is a revocation guard (2609.08258). Restoring a past self under its then-policy and then-model is pinning and engineering: ActiveGraph forks inherit the current Frame, and model aliases rotate. If the then-model can no longer be served, that is a hard limit no architecture removes.
items.evidence: Identity lane verdict: 'as infrastructure ... not novel'. Revoked but Still Authoritative: agents act on superseded policy, and a simple retrieval guard fixes much of it. FiscalQA Pro: as-of rule lookup 98.3% with plain versioned retrieval.
