items.north_star_item: EXPERIMENT.md §1 operative claim: detect that a later event changes an earlier decision's significance without contradicting any stored fact, trace it, reopen it, and remediate in the present
covered_by: DeepRewind [V; code + probe; headline numbers abstract-only]
items.evidence: Corollary probe (b): 'A later, unanticipated fact on a different key (cve:libfoo) left the decision IN.' DeepRewind probe: 'organic path ... monitor fired 0 times'. Benchmarks lane: 'failures come from not acting on evidence the agent already has, not from failing to reach the past'.

attack.overall_verdict: Almost nothing remains. Composed from verified prior work, the stack is MAGE/FlowState-style structured execution state + LangGraph / ActiveGraph / Shepherd checkpoint-fork-replay + PoS belief state + Graphiti / Memvara / XTDB bitemporal facts + COUNTERMEM / C3 counterfactual branches + ITP / Shepherd-speculate lookahead + DeepRewind / PlanFence / Corollary dependency-tracked reopening + FutureSim / Forecast-Dojo cutoff replay and predicted-vs-realized + Calibration Is Not Control / potential outcomes / Metaculus annulment for intervention-conditioned and prevented futures + relative reachability / AUP / SafeCommit / LCPI / DeepRewind for optionality + OTel / LangSmith / AER for identity and policy over time. That stack reproduces every NORTH_STAR section and invariant at the level of concept and mechanism. Of 47 items, none has a residual that is both a capability and attributable to temporal navigation. The leftovers are vocabulary, glue (one runtime enforcing all invariants including prospective objects, plus persisted averted-forecast and backward-requirement records), engineering fixes for documented cutoff leaks, and two untested empirical claims (executable past self vs retrieval over equally rich records; interrogating simulated future selves). The one real capability gap, detecting significance changes through implicit or undeclared links, is not specific to temporal architecture. Every measured comparison in the digests leans toward the null. The project should stop presenting NORTH_STAR as a new computational abstraction. If it continues, it should be a narrowly scoped empirical test, with a benchmark built by integration, against a baseline that includes dependency tracking, bitemporal / as-of memory, explicit belief state and AER-grade decision records. If that baseline matches the temporal contestant, the distinctive-architecture thesis should be killed (EXPERIMENT.md §13).

candidates.claim: C1 (NORTH_STAR §8, invariant 8; measurable effect). An LLM agent that calibrates itself from outcomes at inference time, through memory or reflection rather than retraining, will mis-learn when its own interventions suppress the outcomes it forecast. It records 'feared failure did not happen' as evidence that it was too pessimistic and weakens or drops safeguards. Keeping averted forecasts as annulled, branch-labelled records stops this. The claim is that the failure mode and the fix can be measured in LLM agents, not that the concept is new.
candidates.why_not_covered: Every LLM-agent self-calibration loop in the digests runs in a world the agent cannot influence. FutureSim (arXiv 2605.15188, verified): 'the world is fixed, so there is no intervention-aware forecasting and no prevented-futures preservation'. Forecast-Dojo (2609.28876, verified) lists 'the agent's actions are passive' as a limitation. EpiEvolve (2606.05513, verified) and Live-Evo (2602.02369, verified) forecast external events. ExACT (2410.02052, id not in corpus) stores expected-vs-actual reflections for web tasks. The clinical work that documents the error (Boeken et al. CLeaR 2024, 2403.00886, id unverified; Liley et al. 2010.11530, abstract not fetched; Lenert 2019 and Sperrin 2019) is about retraining statistical risk models, not LLM agents with memory. Calibration Is Not Control (2606.21399, verified) needs a resettable simulator and leaves 'deployment-time handling of prevented forecasts' open. The performative-lane query for 'forecasts trigger interventions agent prevented evaluation counterfactual LLM' returned 0 hits. The prospective lane reports that the 2026 forecasting-agent survey (2608.23058; it appears only in lane text and has no citation check) lists reflexive feedback as future work.
candidates.evidence: Counterexamples searched: Metaculus Conditional Pairs (annulment, non-arXiv), Reflexive Model-World Systems (non-peer-reviewed GitHub preprint whose §13.6 says 'successful prevention can erase the evidence of risk'), JANUS (2607.19913, verified, rewards forecasts by how useful they are to the decision), the Intervention Paradox (2602.03338, verified), ForecastBench-Sim (2606.18686, paired intervention worlds at environment level, the agent does not keep its averted forecasts) and Corollary's fault='none' rule (not counting world changes as source errors). All state or sidestep the principle. None runs an LLM agent's memory-based self-calibration in a world where the agent's own actions change the outcome, so none measures whether LLM reflection makes this error.
candidates.strongest_objection: (1) The concept is fully pre-empted: potential outcomes (Dickerman & Hernán 2020), Metaculus annulment, performative prediction (Perdomo 2020, 2002.06673, id unverified) and the clinical 'victims of their own success' results. Showing the error in LLMs would be a replication of a predicted consequence, and the fix is one status column that any checkpoint+RAG baseline can also log. (2) Positivity: a deterministic agent that always intervenes cannot verify its 'prevented' labels (decision-scoring-rule literature; Keogh & van Geloven), so the claim can only be tested in a simulated world with counterfactual ground truth. (3) An LLM that reflects in natural language may reason 'I intervened, so non-occurrence is not evidence' without help, in which case there is no effect to fix. (4) Neither smoke_v1 nor the EXPERIMENT.md event classes contain this situation, so the project's benchmark does not test it.

candidates.claim: C2 (the measurable form of NORTH_STAR §18, as EXPERIMENT.md §13 operationalizes it). On reopening and remediating decisions, a temporal-state agent's advantage grows with temporal lag and causal depth, and this growth is concentrated in the regime where valid time and knowledge time diverge (event classes C and D: delayed evidence, retroactive fact). The comparison is against a baseline that already has (a) single-clock as-of filtering over an append-only log, (b) an explicit current-state wrapper and (c) a dependency/TMS arm.
candidates.why_not_covered: No work in the digests measures how an advantage changes along lag or causal depth for decision reopening. Forecast-Dojo (2609.28876) states it has 'no variation in history length, causal depth or lag'. Memvara's own benchmark (non-arXiv, reproduced locally) finds the bitemporal gain confined to delayed-knowledge and correction questions (4 of 47 temporal questions, 92.0 vs 89.0 overall), but for fact QA, with no lag variation and no decisions. TGMS (2607.10265, id NOT in corpus, unverified) reports 0.897 vs 0.154 for vector-RAG on correction probes, again QA. MemStrata (2606.26511, verified id; numbers come from a list summary) compares only against similarity-only RAG.
candidates.evidence: Counterexamples checked. PoS (2610.01415) shows an advantage that grows with context length (LOCA 8K to 256K, +10.67 to +16.00 at 256K), but for a present-only belief state with no temporal machinery. StateMemBench (2608.19652, verified) attributes +15 to +32 points to explicit state structure. DreamBench-SWE (2608.20664, verified) finds verbatim event memory about equal to structured memory (82 vs 83 of 180). GitOfThoughts (2606.14470, verified) reports accuracy parity for a versioned, replayable substrate. Forecast-Dojo's carried belief notebook helps 6 of 12 models. None of these isolates lag or depth for decision reopening against the three arms above.
candidates.strongest_objection: This is an unrun experiment, not a distinct capability, and every piece of evidence in the digests predicts the null. Present-state structure (PoS, StateMemBench) already explains advantages that grow with length. Memvara's 8.5% share says the divergence regime is rare. DreamBench-SWE, GitOfThoughts and Forecast-Dojo all report parity. The current baseline also lacks two of the three arms. It explicitly may not use 'temporal fact graphs' (milestone-2 design §9), it has no explicit-state or dependency arm, and its 'dense' channel is lexical (amendment D1). A growing curve against today's baseline would therefore be confounded by construction. The claim survives only in this conditional, narrow form, and only as an open measurement.

candidates.claim: C3 (EXPERIMENT.md §1 steps 1 and 3; NORTH_STAR §4 Historian). The capability to detect, unprompted and without being told, that a later event changes the significance of an earlier decision when no recorded premise is retracted or superseded and no defeater was declared at decision time. In other words, the dependency was implicit and has to be inferred when the event arrives.
candidates.why_not_covered: Mechanisms that reopen decisions need an explicit link. Corollary (non-arXiv, probe in deep-9): a later fact on a different key leaves the decision IN, and defeaters (unless=) exist only in the programmatic API, not in the LLM contract. Graphiti/Zep invalidates only on fact contradiction. In Memvara 'derives' links exist but 'Nothing in the engine writes one today', and nothing propagates. DeepRewind (2609.36344, verified): in the probe, organic contradictions never fired rollback, and the switching study wires the contradiction directly to the target. PlanFence (2609.03340) needs recorded derivation links. The benchmarks lane found no benchmark that scores per-decision reopen recall and precision with negative controls on executed decisions.
candidates.evidence: Closest coverage: STALE (2605.06527, verified) has 'implicit conflict', where a later observation invalidates an earlier memory without explicit negation. TWIST (2609.28575, verified) has unprompted tension detection with hard negatives. Impact Is Not Invalidation (2609.25130, list summary) re-checks claims in a software world. TRACE (2609.33517, id unverified) has memories that are 'inadmissible for action'.
candidates.strongest_objection: (1) As a construct it is covered piecewise (STALE, TWIST, Impact Is Not Invalidation, MerchantBench, VibeLifeBench), so what remains is integration in one software world, which the benchmarks lane judged to be integration rather than a new test. (2) More damaging: nothing ties this capability to temporal navigation. Finding an unrecorded dependency is semantic relevance detection over history, which retrieval plus an LLM already does (TWIST: flat RAG detects 0.76 to 0.97 of contradictions). STALE, KWBench (2604.15760) and MEMTRACK show the failure is acting on evidence the agent already has, not reaching the past. An addressable time dimension does not create links nobody recorded. It is a real gap in benchmarks, not a distinct NORTH_STAR capability.

candidates.claim: C4 (NORTH_STAR §5: 'It asks the former self'). For decisions the agent itself made, querying a re-instantiated past self that is cut off cleanly at decision time improves reconsideration (historical-state fidelity and reopening or remediation outcomes) over a present self that reads the same stored decision record.
candidates.why_not_covered: milestone-2 design §0 states that the current benchmark cannot test this, because decisions are world-authored and there is no decision-time agent state. No work in the digests measures replica-versus-record on consequential, agent-made decisions in a long-lived agent.
candidates.evidence: Covered parts. Self-Blinding (2601.14553, verified): querying a blinded replica beats instructing the model to ignore information (bias domain). ChronoMem (2607.27773, verified; numbers from a secondary reader): snapshot restore scores 31 to 38 F1, prompt-only 0.9 to 2.8, RAG-only rollback 19.4 to 28.9, on post-exposure QA. Hindsight Bias in Clinical Temporal Reasoning (2609.13454, verified): 'temporal masking reduces bias without lowering accuracy'. Shepherd (2605.10913, verified) supports fork at turn t plus inject, the mechanism for questioning a past self. ContextEcho (2605.24279, verified) uses snapshot-then-probe forks. Causal Agent Replay (2606.08275, verified) and C3 (2603.06859, verified) re-decide from a past state with an intervention.
candidates.strongest_objection: (1) The mechanism is commodity (Shepherd, ContextEcho, CAR, C3). The direction of the fidelity effect is already shown in three domains (Self-Blinding, ChronoMem, clinical temporal masking), so the experiment would confirm an expected result. (2) Inference volatility (AER, 2603.21692, non-identifiability argument): a re-invoked past self produces a fresh sample, not what the agent actually thought then. 'Why did you decide X' is answered faithfully only by a contemporaneous record, so 'ask, don't reconstruct' adds counterfactual re-decision, which CAR and C3 already do, and not authentic testimony. (3) Leakage through KV state (2608.15939) and parameters (2601.13717) undermines 'strict cutoff' unless the world is synthetic. (4) For remediation the fix is usually the same whether the decision was wrong then or the world changed, so the expected effect on the primary metrics is small. The only thing that survives is 'nobody ran this exact experiment', which is not distinctness.

candidates.claim: C5 (NORTH_STAR §6, §14). An agent that instantiates simulated future versions of itself (its own future knowledge, policy or objectives, not just future world states) and questions them for regrets, wished-for information and options to preserve makes measurably better present decisions.
candidates.why_not_covered: The prospective lane reports: 'Not found: any agent that interrogates a simulated future version of itself (future policy, objectives or identity) and shows a measured decision benefit.' Future-self work exists only for humans.
candidates.evidence: Human studies: Future You (2405.12514, verified) and Simulating Life Paths (2512.05397, verified) measure psychological effects and persuasion-driven shifts, and the latter 'assessed decision intentions rather than implemented behaviors'. Agent side: 'Current Agents Fail to Leverage World Model as Tool for Foresight' (2601.03905, verified) finds agents invoke simulation in under 1% of cases and misuse rollouts about 15% of the time.
candidates.strongest_objection: The questions break down into covered quantities. 'Which option do you wish I had preserved' is option preservation: relative reachability (1806.01186, id unverified), AUP (1902.09725, id unverified), Heitzig & Potham (2508.00159, verified). 'What information do you wish I had collected' is information-buying across plausible futures (SafeCommit 2608.04289, verified: a low-side-effect probe targeting the blocking worlds). 'Which decision do you regret' and feared-future constraints are covered by SafePred (2602.01725), JANUS (2607.19913), SIMMER (2606.14574) and FLARE (2601.22311). 'Simulate, then act from the present' is RAFA (2309.17382, id unverified). The 'self' framing adds a persona prompt, not computation. The only evidence about such interfaces is negative (agents do not use simulators; for humans the effect is persuasion). What remains is terminology.

candidates.claim: C6 (NORTH_STAR §7 and §15 loop). At decision time the agent derives watch conditions (signposts or defeaters) from simulated desired or feared futures. It persists them with provenance and checks later events against them. This raises reopen recall at matched precision compared with rediscovering relevance by retrieval when the event arrives.
candidates.why_not_covered: Backward-optionality lane residual: in every LLM work found, feared futures are 'used once, at decision time'. None stores derived obligations or conditions as timestamped, provenance-carrying state that is re-checked when later events arrive. DAPP signposts could not be confirmed in fetched sources. Corollary's defeaters cannot be emitted by the LLM.
candidates.evidence: Counterexamples found. FlowState (2609.34565) has a stored conditional plan, 'reconsider if B becomes cheaper', which PSA re-discloses when the trigger occurs (a motivating example, not separately evaluated). ChronosBench (2601.09382, verified) has the agent write trigger conditions from dialog history and re-engage when they are met (85.19%). DeepRewind (2609.36344) registers a trigger for each accepted commitment and counts linked PlanStep probes (contradiction-trigger coverage, TC). PlanFence keeps derivation links that are re-checked before protected actions.
candidates.strongest_objection: Persisting reopen conditions and re-checking them is covered (ChronosBench evaluated; FlowState and DeepRewind implemented). The only new element is where the conditions come from, simulation instead of the user or a generic contradiction check, and a baseline gets this from a prompt to write 'revisit if' notes into its decision records. By design it catches only anticipated changes, which declared defeaters already handle. The hard case, unanticipated significance changes (C3), is exactly what it cannot cover. It is a prompt-policy variant, not a distinct capability.

candidates.claim: C7 (NORTH_STAR §5, §12, invariant 3). An agent-facing, leakage-audited state_at(t) over the agent's whole decision-time state (beliefs, plans, assumptions, uncertainty, and the policy, objective and identity in force), used by the agent itself to decide whether to reopen, as opposed to fact-level as-of memory or developer-facing traces.
candidates.why_not_covered: The belief lane found no system that versions the whole decision-time state rather than facts, and no agent that queries its own past state to decide on reopening. The partial systems leak. In the ActiveGraph probes (2605.21997, verified), forks inherited a post-cutoff tool observation and the current Frame. Memvara's generic as_of applies later endings. Graphiti leaks invalid_at. Corollary's TrustLedger at= leaks later outcomes. LangGraph replay reads the current Store. Trellis (2606.29823, verified) has as-of only for training data, and its agent is stateless. AER (2603.21692) is never read by the agent.
candidates.evidence: Shepherd (2605.10913) forks the whole process, context and filesystem at turn t, which restores any in-process belief or policy state at a cutoff. The As-Of Information-Set Pinning pattern (non-arXiv) pins model, corpus and data per decision. 2609.12766 (id NOT in corpus, unverified) formalizes historical state as (D_t, theta_t, M_<i). For policy and identity: OTel GenAI, MLflow, Langfuse and LangSmith record versions; Shepherd's CRO reopens the first past step a policy edit touches; Arike 2505.02709 (verified) scores failure to divest after a goal switch; Revoked-but-Still-Authoritative (2609.08258, verified) shows a simple guard fixes most acting on a superseded policy.
candidates.strongest_objection: Every ingredient exists, and Shepherd's fork already gives a whole-state past self with a clean cutoff in sandboxable worlds. What remains is putting a leakage-tested API in front of the agent, which the epistemic-cutoff lane calls 'a systems-integration and benchmark claim, not a conceptual one'. The policy-attribution part is solved as data (FiscalQA Pro 2608.09393: 98.3% with versioned retrieval) and partly as mechanism (CRO, the revocation guard). With no evidence that agent-facing access changes decisions, this is engineering.

candidates.claim: C8 (NORTH_STAR §11). Representing uncertainty about when past events happened (interval-valued or probabilistic valid time, for example 'stopped between March 3 and 8'), and using it to decide which earlier decisions fall inside the window a retroactive fact affects, improves reopening precision and recall on retroactive-fact events.
candidates.why_not_covered: No work in the digests represents indeterminate valid time in agent memory. Graphiti renders a null valid_at as 'date unknown' (verify/graphiti.md). Memvara stores point valid_from and valid_to. PoS attaches probabilities to records but has no time fields. A grep of notes, verify and synth for indeterminacy or temporal-uncertainty terms found nothing else.
candidates.evidence: The absence comes from the digests and raw notes. No lane searched for this topic.
candidates.strongest_objection: Absence here is not evidence of non-coverage, because the sweep never searched for it, and the classical temporal-database literature on indeterminate valid time is a likely counterexample. That literature is outside the digests, so I cannot cite it and it is unverified. The expected effect is also tiny: Memvara puts the whole delayed-knowledge and correction regime at about 9% of temporal questions, and interval-uncertain cases are a subset of that. An LLM can also carry 'between March 3 and 8' as text and reason about the overlap without a structured representation. The claim of non-coverage cannot be established from these materials.

steelman.verdict:
No capability, abstraction or mechanism in NORTH_STAR.md survives as distinct from the 2025-2026 and classical prior art in the digests. The covered material, by item:

- **"Never overwrite time, fork it" and the Chronicle:** event sourcing (OpenHands SDK, ActiveGraph), Shepherd, AgentGit, Dolt/lakeFS and W3C PROV.
- **The Historian's revisable interpretations:** Graphiti, Kumiho, Memvara (ended vs retired), DeepRewind.
- **Bitemporal known-then vs true-then:** XTDB, Datomic, Memvara, TOKI.
- **Strict cutoff and past-self reconstruction:** ChronoMem, Shepherd fork, Self-Blinding, and the look-ahead-bias literature with its documented failure modes.
- **Forks with provenance and counterfactual branches:** ActiveGraph, Shepherd, C3, Causal Agent Replay.
- **Future rollout:** ITP, RAP, WebDreamer, WMA.
- **Backward requirements and option preservation:** goal regression, BAR, relative reachability, AUP, SafePred, SafeCommit, DeepRewind's gate.
- **Intervention-aware and reflexive forecast taxonomy:** potential outcomes, performative prediction, Calibration Is Not Control.
- **Prevented futures:** Metaculus conditional annulment, clinical "victims of their own success".
- **Predicted vs realized:** FutureSim, EpiEvolve, Live-Evo, WALL-E 2.0.
- **Identity and policy over time:** OTel GenAI, MLflow, LangSmith, AER, Shepherd's CRO.

The "unified temporal abstraction" is integration: ActiveGraph plus Trellis plus a planner covers most of it, and every lane judged unification to be engineering unless an experiment shows it helps.

Two narrow, empirical, untested effect claims survive.

**C1.** In a world where the agent's own interventions change outcomes, an LLM agent that calibrates itself from outcomes through memory or reflection may mistake successful prevention for wrong prediction, and annulled, branch-labelled forecast records may fix that.
- Every LLM self-calibration study in the digests runs in a world the agent cannot influence (FutureSim, Forecast-Dojo, EpiEvolve, Live-Evo).
- The concept is pre-empted. Only the LLM demonstration is open, and it can be tested only where counterfactual ground truth exists, i.e. a simulated world.
- The current benchmark does not test it at all.

**C2.** A temporal-state advantage may grow with lag and causal depth, concentrated where valid time and knowledge time diverge (event classes C and D: delayed evidence, retroactive fact).
- This holds only against a baseline that also has single-clock as-of filtering, an explicit current-state wrapper and a dependency/TMS arm.
- No work in the digests measures such a curve for decision reopening.
- All available evidence predicts the null: Memvara's 8.5% share, DreamBench-SWE and GitOfThoughts parity, Forecast-Dojo's 6 of 12 models, and PoS and StateMemBench attributing gains to present-state structure.
- The current baseline cannot rule out the confound. It may not use temporal fact graphs, its "dense" channel is lexical (D1), and it has no explicit-state or dependency arm.

Neither surviving claim is a capability claim about "time as an addressable dimension of state". Both are measurements that could come out negative.

**Strongest non-survivor:** C3, unprompted detection of significance changes with no recorded premise. It is a real benchmark gap, but nothing ties it to temporal navigation; it is semantic relevance detection. The design doc's §0 already concedes that past-self dialogue (C4) is untested, and C4 fails anyway: the mechanism is commodity, three prior works already show the direction of the fidelity effect, and AER's non-identifiability argument means a re-invoked "former self" is a fresh sample, not testimony.

**Practical consequences:**
- The project should treat NORTH_STAR as a set of hypotheses to test against strengthened baselines, not as a novel architecture.
- If it wants a residual of its own, it needs a scenario family that EXPERIMENT.md does not yet contain: reflexive forecasts with simulator ground truth (C1), and lag- and depth-graded class C and D events run with the three extra baseline arms (C2).

**Caveats:**
- Several citations are unverified, as labelled in each candidate (TGMS, 2609.12766, ExACT, Boeken, Liley, Perdomo, Krakovna, AUP, RAFA, and the 2608.23058 survey, which appears only in lane text).
- WebSearch was exhausted and arXiv was blocked, so 2026 work that uses the project's own vocabulary may have been missed.
- No files in /home/user/temporal-agent were modified.

concepts.definition: Producing a probability distribution over a future outcome Y given the information set H_t. The NORTH_STAR §9 taxonomy distinguishes a passive forecast P(Y | H_t, status-quo policy), a policy- or action-conditioned forecast P(Y^a | H_t), and a reflexive or performative forecast, where publishing the forecast changes the distribution of Y. It predicts only; it does not choose actions.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: LLM forecasting agents and harnesses: FutureSim arXiv 2605.15188 [V, deep read: date-gated replay, append-only PredictionHistory with get_prediction_as_of, daily predicted-vs-truth Brier feedback]; Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V, deep read]; EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [V]; Live-Evo 2602.02369 [V]; ForecastBench 2409.19839 and FutureX 2508.11987 [V, bundled entry]. Action-conditioned and causal forecasting: Dickerman & Hernán 2020, doi 10.1007/s10654-020-00659-8 [NA]; Keogh & van Geloven 2024 / Boyer et al. 2025 [U]. Performative forecasting: Perdomo et al. arXiv 2002.06673 [U]; Oesterheld et al. arXiv 2305.17601 [U]. Agent oversight: Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]. Legend: [V] arXiv id and title verified in the local corpus; [U] arXiv id not in the local corpus (unverified); [NA] non-arXiv, checked through a repo or GitHub; [TD] id in the corpus but title differs; [LN] cited only in a lane note's corpus abstract; [M] mandatory digest, code read but paper body unread; [3P] third-party figure.
concepts.what_north_star_adds: Three things: (1) every forecast is tagged with branch identity, assumptions, generating policy and horizon (§2); (2) the four-way passive/policy-conditioned/intervention-aware/reflexive classification (§9); (3) forecasts are represented more coarsely as the horizon grows (§10).
concepts.residual: None at the level of concept. The taxonomy is the potential-outcomes and performative-prediction split. FutureSim already ships forecast histories that are as-of queryable and fed back to the agent. Calibration Is Not Control shows that better calibration of a passive forecast leaves control regret unchanged, which undercuts calibration as a value claim. The only gap the sweep found is bookkeeping: an agent's own self-averted forecasts kept as labelled objects (see prevented_future).

concepts.definition: Generating a set of internally coherent alternative futures, usually driven by exogenous uncertainties rather than by the agent's candidate actions. A strategy is stress-tested across the set, and the conditions under which it fails are identified. The output is an ensemble plus failure regions, not a single prediction.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: Decision making under deep uncertainty (DMDU) and robust decision making (RDM): EMA workbench, github.com/quaquel/EMAworkbench [NA; scenario discovery and directed search over levers]. US COVID-19 Scenario Modeling Hub (Howerton et al. 2023, Nat Commun 14:7260) [NA], which scores a projection only where its scenario assumptions held. Agent and benchmark level: FORESIGHT-9 2608.29372 [V], nine counterfactual worldlines branching from one information boundary; ForecastBench-Sim 2606.18686 [V], with paired intervention worlds. Dynamic adaptive policy pathways (signposts and tipping points, Haasnoot 2013) are UNVERIFIED: no fetched source confirmed them.
concepts.what_north_star_adds: Simulated scenarios become branches in the agent's own temporal graph and keep provenance (§3, §10, invariant 5). They sit alongside past states rather than in a separate analysis tool.
concepts.residual: Persisting a scenario ensemble across the agent's life and re-weighting it as evidence arrives is what DAPP signposts do (unverified in our sources). For LLM agents it was not found. It is a modest engineering integration, not a new capability. FORESIGHT-9 found that a fixed equal-weight policy beat 31 of 36 adaptive runs, a warning that adaptive scenario machinery does not automatically pay off.

concepts.definition: Predicting a trajectory of future states ŝ_{t+1..t+K}, given the current state and a candidate action or action sequence, so that candidate actions can be compared before one is committed. The rollout can be imagined (from a model) or executed (in a resettable copy of the environment).
concepts.canonical_prior_art: Imagined rollouts: RAP 2305.14992 [U]; WebDreamer 2411.06559 [U; code read: num_of_sim=3, steps=2, simulations not persisted]; WMA 2410.13232 [U; aims to avoid irreversible mistakes such as buying non-refundable tickets]; Imagine-then-Plan (ITP) 2601.08955 [M; one greedy K-step foresight per step, adaptive K]; Dyna-Think 2506.00320 [V]. Executed rollouts: prefix branching in Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]; C3 2603.06859 [V]; Causal Agent Replay 2606.08275 [LN].
concepts.what_north_star_adds: §6 defines Ŝ^a_{t+Δ} = simulate(S_t, a, Δ). The simulated object is the agent's whole situated state {W,K,B,G,C,U,D,O}, not only the environment observation.
concepts.residual: None for environment rollout: §6's simulate is this operation. The only untested part is rolling out the agent's own future memory, policy and objectives as part of the state. ITP-R comes closest: it alternates the policy's own actions with world-model steps. Nothing measured a benefit from self-state rollout, and 'Current Agents Fail to Leverage World Model as Tool for Foresight' 2601.03905 [V] reports agents invoke simulation in under 1% of cases, misuse about 15% of rollouts, and lose up to 5%.

concepts.definition: A transition model T(s, a) → s' (with a reward model if needed), learned or prompted, that provides the dynamics for rollout and planning. In LLM agents it is usually text in, text out. It is the component; rollout and planning are uses of it.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: RAP 2305.14992 [U] (LLM used as world model plus MCTS); WMA 2410.13232 [U]; WebEvolver / WebWorld / Qwen-AgentWorld 2504.21024 / 2602.14721 / 2606.24597 [TD]; WALL-E 2.0 2504.15785 [V], which repairs the model from the gap between predicted and actual trajectories; the ITP world model is a LoRA trained on (state, action) → next state pairs [M]; SIMMER 2606.14574 [V], a symbolic world model for latent failures; SafePred 2602.01725 [V].
concepts.what_north_star_adds: It implies a self-model: a model of how the agent's own beliefs, goals and obligations will evolve, so that a 'future self' can be instantiated (§1, §6, §12).
concepts.residual: An agent self-model used for decisions is unevaluated anywhere we found. That is an absence of evidence, not evidence of value. The 2601.03905 [V] negative result and the Forecast-Dojo notebook result (6 of 12 models improved) give a low prior.

concepts.definition: Choosing an action sequence that reaches a goal by searching over model-predicted futures, with values backed up from imagined outcomes to the present choice. It covers tree search, value propagation and limiting commitment.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: RAP (MCTS) 2305.14992 [U]; LATS 2310.04406 [U]; ExACT R-MCTS 2410.02052 [U; it stores expected-vs-actual reflections with task provenance]; Agent Q 2408.07199 and Tree-GRPO [TD bundle]; FLARE 2601.22311 [V; 'explicit lookahead, value propagation, and limited commitment ... allowing downstream outcomes to influence early decisions'].
concepts.what_north_star_adds: The §15 loop (forecast → instantiate future selves → receive requirements → act) names the outputs of planning 'requirements and warnings' and attributes them to future selves.
concepts.residual: None at the level of mechanism. Planning is the standard computation behind 'future sends requirements backward'.

concepts.definition: At each step, optimise over a horizon H with the model, execute only the first action, observe, update the model or posterior, and re-plan from the new present. Derived requirements are recomputed at every step rather than stored.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: RAFA, 'Reason for Future, Act for Now' 2309.17382 [U; code README read]: plan a long-horizon trajectory, take its initial action, store the feedback, re-plan, with √T regret. LLMPC 2501.02486 [LN; prompting techniques viewed 'through the lens of model predictive control'].
concepts.what_north_star_adds: §15 adds 'compare predicted futures vs realized future → calibrate' and frames the loop as a 'temporal control loop' rather than as memory.
concepts.residual: None. §15 is receding-horizon control with posterior updating, which is what RAFA does. MPC also undercuts the case for persisting derived obligations: if re-planning from the present is cheap and the planner sees the relevant state, the plan is simply recomputed (see backward_obligations).

concepts.definition: Starting from a desired (or feared) terminal condition and working backward to the subgoals and preconditions that must hold earlier, ideally with latest-start dates. The result is a dated chain of present obligations. NORTH_STAR §7's T+90 → T+20 example is this.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: Classical goal regression, still active: 2511.11095 [LN]. LLM backward planning: BAR 2505.14079 [V] ('planning starting from the terminal state'); Goal-Mem 2605.12213 [LN] (backward chaining). Backward induction over goal distributions: Heitzig & Potham 2508.00159 [V]. From a feared future to a present constraint: SafePred 2602.01725 [V]; JANUS 2607.19913 [V]; SIMMER 2606.14574 [V]; WMA [U]. PoS 2610.01415 [M] derives single-level 'achievement gaps' from the goal specification (rated partial).
concepts.what_north_star_adds: Requirements derived from simulated future selves, and from feared as well as desired states, kept as obligations O_t inside the temporal state.
concepts.residual: Thin. The only part not found is keeping the derived chain as timestamped, provenance-carrying state that is re-checked as events arrive. That is prospective memory plus truth maintenance (see backward_obligations), and the baseline's rolling summary already tracks 'open, parked or blocked work and what it is waiting for'.

concepts.definition: There are four distinct senses. (a) Learning-theoretic regret bounds on cumulative loss against the best policy. (b) Decision-analytic minimax regret across a scenario ensemble (RDM). (c) Measured counterfactual control regret: the value of the chosen action against the oracle action on same-prefix branches. (d) Anticipated or hindsight regret elicited by a prompt ('which decision do you regret?'), which is a pre-mortem.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: (a) RAFA 2309.17382 [U] (√T); Plaut et al. 2502.14043 [V] (sublinear regret with irreversible costs via asking for help). (b) RDM via EMA workbench [NA]. (c) Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]: control regret 0.506 → 0.110 on ALFWorld with a prefix-only action-conditioned controller; recalibration 'leaves control regret unchanged'. (d) BTF-2 2604.26106 [LN]: better forecasters differ 'primarily in [their] pre-mortem analysis'; this is correlational. Reflexive Model-World Systems [NA, not peer-reviewed]: 'observed regret may be endogenous to the policy that produced or prevented it'.
concepts.what_north_star_adds: A future self that reports regret (§6) as an input to the present decision.
concepts.residual: None. Sense (d) is role-prompted pre-mortem; sense (c) requires counterfactual branch values, which come either from simulation (SafeCommit / RDM) or from positivity in reality (see prevented_future). Hindsight regret about one's own interventions is exactly where positivity fails.

concepts.definition: Holding an intention ('do X when cue C occurs, or at time T') across a delay while doing other work, then executing it at the right cue or time. This includes updating or cancelling intentions. The intentions are usually given by a user rather than derived.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: PM-Bench 2607.12385 [M; code verified]: heartbeat-proactive scores 65.1% macro Set-F1, the TODO ledger 62.8%, the baseline 60.0%, and the best hidden-channel hit rate is 16.7%. Prospective Intention Store (PIS) 2609.01272 [V]: 82.9% Set-F1, and 70.1% against at most 54.4% for retrospective memory. Cluster in lane notes: TriggerBench 2606.23459 [LN] ('PM decays sharply as context length scales'); BudgetPM 2609.37125; 'Memory That Looks Forward' 2609.22091 (dated or trigger-conditioned ledger); 'Delivery, Not Storage' 2607.20972 (trigger conditions evaluated deterministically by the harness); 'Did You Forget What I Asked?' 2603.23530 (a salience reminder restores compliance to 90–100%). ChronosBench 2601.09382 [V]: the agent 'autonomously formulates trigger conditions based on dialog history'.
concepts.what_north_star_adds: O_t as part of the situated self. Obligations are derived from simulated futures rather than given, and carry provenance back to the branch and assumptions that produced them.
concepts.residual: Very thin. ChronosBench already has agent-formulated triggers. DeepRewind 2609.36344 [V] registers a trigger per commitment and runs a monitor. FlowState 2609.34565 [M] has a motivating example of a conditional plan ('reconsider if B becomes cheaper') that is re-evaluated when it triggers; that example is unverified as a measured result. Corollary [NA] provides retraction cascades. The one new element is that the source of derivation is simulation, and nothing shows simulation-derived obligations beat dialog- or dependency-derived ones.

concepts.definition: An interactive dialogue with a simulated future version of a person (or agent), conditioned on a projected future state, used to change present attitudes or choices. It is distinct from a rollout because the interface is conversational and framed around identity.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: Future You 2405.12514 (found in a corpus listing; n=344, anxiety −0.68 vs +0.21 for control, p=0.001, from a third-party wiki note [3P]): lower anxiety, higher future-self continuity. Future You multimodal 2512.06106 (N=92; continuity, well-being and motivation up, with no difference between modalities). Simulating Life Paths 2512.05397 [V] (N=192): one-sided avatars shift choices toward the option presented, a system-generated third option gets adopted, and its limitations section says 'we assessed decision intentions rather than implemented behaviors'. AI-Powered Episodic Future Thinking 2503.16484 [LN]: usability study only.
concepts.what_north_star_adds: The agent's own executable future selves, queried for regrets, requirements and options to preserve (§6, §14).
concepts.residual: Unoccupied for agents, and unsupported by any evidence. The human evidence is psychological or persuasive, not about decision quality. See future_self_ux.

concepts.definition: Choosing present actions that keep the set of reachable good futures large, typically by penalising lost reachability or attainable value relative to a counterfactual baseline (inaction or stepwise). Variants gate commitments on estimated reversibility, or act only when the action is safe in every plausible world.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: Relative reachability / 'Avoiding Side Effects By Considering Future Tasks' 1806.01186 [U; DeepMind README read]; AUP 1902.09725 [U; README read]; Heitzig & Potham 2508.00159 [V]; SafeCommit 2608.04289 [V] (act only if safe in every retained world, otherwise probe or fall back); LCPI 2609.36741 [V] (homogenize so that every remaining model admits an acceptable continuation; Last Identifiable Margin; a sham control eliminates the gain); DeepRewind 2609.36344 [V] (gate on IRR·(1−TC), then rollback); FinalityBench 2609.04706 [V] (a finality gate reaches 85.4%, and LLMs discover gating without being told).
concepts.what_north_star_adds: §13 makes I(a) a first-class temporal variable, and frames 'preserve options' as a request from future selves.
concepts.residual: None in mechanism. Untested: checking retrospectively whether an already-executed action destroyed an option that a later event made valuable. That is an evaluation design (a FinalityBench-style twin pair applied after the fact), not a new capability.

concepts.definition: A forecast whose subject depends on the action it triggers. The forecast of the no-action outcome is a potential outcome Y^{a0}; if the agent intervenes, Y^{a0} goes unobserved. The forecast is then annulled, not falsified.
concepts.canonical_prior_art: Dickerman & Hernán 2020 [NA]; Metaculus Conditional Pairs (an unrealised conditional 'is Annulled ... It is not scored') and the ConditionalQuestion/ANNULLED model in forecasting-tools [NA]; decision markets and decision scoring rules (Chen, Kash et al. 2011; Oesterheld & Conitzer 2020) [NA, from a bibliography]; counterfactual oracle, Armstrong 1711.05541 [U]; Boeken et al. 2403.00886 [U]; Liley et al. 2010.11530 [U]; van Amsterdam et al. 2312.01210 [U]; Perdomo 2002.06673 [U]; Oesterheld et al. 2305.17601 [U]; Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]; Intervention Paradox 2602.03338 [V].
concepts.what_north_star_adds: §8 and invariant 8: prevented futures are preserved as counterfactuals rather than scored as errors.
concepts.residual: Bookkeeping only, plus a failure-mode study. See prevented_future.

future.backward_obligations:
QUESTION 1. Is there a residual capability in "deriving present obligations or option-preserving actions by reasoning backward from simulated future states"?

Answer: no residual capability. At most there is one narrow empirical hypothesis, and the current harness cannot test it.

To compare the prior art precisely, I split the claim into five parts:
- (D) the source of derivation: what kind of simulated future the obligation comes from;
- (R) the representation of the derived obligation or option condition;
- (P) persistence with provenance across events;
- (T) trigger re-evaluation when later events arrive;
- (A) the resulting action: a new obligation, an option-preserving act, or reopening an already-executed decision.

ITP 2601.08955 [M, code read]
- D: one greedy K-step imagined trajectory, with K chosen adaptively (by prompt in ITP-I, by a learned head with a −λK cost in ITP-R).
- R: free text pasted into the prompt.
- P: none. The foresight is dropped from the history (runner.py:262-271) and never compared with the outcome.
- T: none. A: the next action only.
- Lesson: large within-episode gains came from the cheapest possible lookahead. ALFWorld overall, ITP-I vs RAP: 35.71/41.43/37.86 vs 27.86/28.57/22.86 on Qwen2.5-7B/Qwen3-8B/Llama-3.1-8B.
- The prospective benefit is not robust: RAP beats ITP-I on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen, 27.14 vs 19.86.
- The released code has an evaluation regex bug and possible train/eval split overlap.
- Consequence: any future-side contestant must be compared against "baseline + an ITP-I-style imagine step per event at an equal token budget". Otherwise a win cannot be attributed to persistence or to addressable time.

RAP / LATS / WebDreamer / WMA [all U; repos read]
- D: several imagined branches, scored and searched (MCTS in RAP and LATS; WebDreamer evaluate_simulation with num_of_sim=3, steps=2). WMA explicitly targets irreversible mistakes such as buying a non-refundable ticket.
- R: search-tree nodes. P: within the episode only; WebDreamer's released modules never persist simulations. T: none.
- A: choosing an action, or vetoing one when the feared future is irreversible.
- This already covers both "option-preserving action derived from a simulated feared future" and "multiple futures", at decision time.

RAFA 2309.17382 [U] / LLMPC 2501.02486 [LN]
- Receding horizon: plan over a long horizon, act on the first step, store feedback, re-plan (√T regret).
- Derived requirements are recomputed from the new present at every step instead of being stored.
- This is the strongest argument against persistence. When re-planning is cheap and the planner sees the relevant state, recomputation reproduces whatever a stored obligation would say, and it also picks up conditions that were not anticipated at derivation time, which a stored list cannot do.

Relative reachability 1806.01186 [U] / AUP 1902.09725 [U] / Krakovna future-tasks reward / Heitzig 2508.00159 [V]
- D: a distribution over hypothetical future goals, against an inaction or stepwise counterfactual baseline.
- A: a penalty that preserves reachability of, or attainable value for, those goals.
- This is "option-preserving action from imagined futures", formalised and implemented in 2018–2020. It is recomputed each step, not persisted.

Feared-future constraints for LLM agents
- SafePred 2602.01725 [V]: 'aligning predicted future risks with current decisions'; step-level interventions plus task-level re-planning; >97.6% safety.
- JANUS 2607.19913 [V]: anticipation plus adjudication; forecasts are rewarded for decision utility.
- SIMMER 2606.14574 [V]: foresight simulation cuts latent failures by up to 72% and irreversible cases by up to 75%.
- SafeCommit 2608.04289 [V]: calibrated set of retained plausible worlds; act only if safe in all of them, otherwise take a low-side-effect probe or a fallback.
- LCPI 2609.36741 [V]: homogenize so all remaining models admit a common continuation; the Last Identifiable Margin is the feasibility boundary.
- DeepRewind 2609.36344 [V, deep read]: reversibility-gated commit (IRR·(1−TC)) and, importantly, a registered trigger per accepted commitment, a monitor run every iteration, and dependency-aware rollback.
- DeepRewind therefore already persists a derived reopen-condition across iterations. Two caveats: its trigger comes from dependencies, not from a simulated future; and in the released code organic contradictions never fire the rollback. A probe confirmed it fires only in the synthetic switching study.
- All the others consume the feared future at decision time.

DMDU/RDM (EMA workbench [NA]) and dynamic adaptive policy pathways
- RDM's scenario discovery derives the conditions under which a strategy fails, i.e. requirements from an ensemble of futures.
- DAPP signposts and triggers are, conceptually, the very thing the project would claim: derived obligations kept with a monitored trigger and a tipping point. They are UNVERIFIED in our sources (no fetched text confirms Haasnoot 2013).
- If the concept is accepted from the domain, the persistent-signpost idea is established policy-analysis practice. Even without accepting it, it cannot be presented as an AI novelty without first checking DAPP.

PM-Bench 2607.12385 [M] / PIS 2609.01272 [V] / TriggerBench 2606.23459 [LN] / ChronosBench 2601.09382 [V]
- These cover P and T for given or dialog-derived intentions.
- PM-Bench: periodic re-checking (heartbeat-proactive) is best at 65.1% macro Set-F1, against 60.0% for the baseline. Hidden-channel cues stay at 16.7%.
- PIS: a typed store with lifecycle logic in code reaches 82.9%, and beats retrospective memory 70.1% vs at most 54.4%.
- TriggerBench: prospective memory degrades as context grows.
- ChronosBench: the agent formulates its own trigger conditions, so even "derived rather than given" is not untouched.

What persistence of derived obligations would add over recomputation. Model the stored obligation as o = (condition c, action a, deadline d, derivation time t0, generating branch b, assumptions A_b). Persistence then offers five things:
1. Survival across context loss and restarts. The protocol makes this relevant: under amendment A4 the contestant process restarts from persisted state after a timeout or crash.
2. Firing on a deadline or clock without re-simulating. This is the latest-start dates of §7.
3. Retraction when A_b is invalidated (truth maintenance).
4. Auditing whether o was justified given what was known at t0 (hindsight-free).
5. Stability: less flip-flopping between re-plans. FutureSim measures forecast movement with avg_submission_tv_to_prev and reports anchoring through a third-party summary only.

Would a re-check prompt over a stored list match it? Case by case:
- Short list, conditions checkable in natural language: yes, essentially. That is PM-Bench's TODO ledger or heartbeat, and the gains are modest.
- The repo's baseline already is this null arm:
  - its rolling summary is instructed to keep "open, parked or blocked work and what it is waiting for" and "decisions in force with their stated reasons and assumptions" (src/baseline/memory.py SUMMARY_TASK);
  - its per-event notes are indexed and retrieved;
  - the standing maintainer guidance says "record what could matter later, including what might become relevant if circumstances change" (src/contestant_runtime/protocol.py).
- Long list: the re-check prompt degrades (TriggerBench; 'Did You Forget What I Asked?' 2603.23530 [LN] shows compliance drops under load and a salience reminder restores it). The documented fix is a typed store with triggers evaluated in code (PIS; 'Delivery, Not Storage' 2607.20972 [LN]), not temporal navigation.
- Retraction when assumptions change: a dependency graph handles it (Corollary [NA] JTMS retraction cascades; DeepRewind; MemTX 2607.23929 [V]; PlanFence 2609.03340 [V], where in 30 live workflows a freshness-only executor used the stale plan every time and PlanFence completed all 30). A prompt that carries the assumption text approximates it, less reliably.
- Auditing at t0: the event log plus A1's read_at/diff already let any contestant reconstruct what was known at t0.
- Conditions not anticipated at t0: neither a stored list nor persistence helps. Re-simulating from the new present (MPC) is required, and that is prior art.

So the persisted obligation store equals "a typed prospective-memory store plus TMS dependency links". A re-check prompt matches it for small lists; typed triggers plus dependencies match it at scale. Neither requires time-addressability.

The only residual hypothesis I can state honestly is "future-mediated relevance". Sometimes a later event bears on a past decision only through a simulated future: the event makes branch B likely, B needs option X, and past decision D removed X. There is no lexical, entity or causal link in the record. The hypothesis is that an agent which keeps weighted simulated branches with attached obligations, and re-weights them on each event, detects such reopenings with higher recall, or at lower cost at long lag, than (i) the baseline, (ii) the baseline plus a per-event ITP-I-style imagine step, and (iii) the baseline plus a PIS-style typed obligation store with depends_on links, all at equal model and token budgets.

The prior for this hypothesis is low:
- 2601.03905 [V]: agents rarely and poorly use foresight.
- Forecast-Dojo [V]: a carried belief notebook improved Brier for only 6 of 12 models (mean delta about +0.002, i.e. slightly worse).
- FinalityBench [V]: plain LLMs discover gating unprompted.

The current harness cannot test it at all:
- smoke_v1's events are a fixed stream that does not react to the agent (amendment A1: agent edits are not part of the world timeline).
- The decisions are authored by the world.
- The only scored actions are ReopenAction and NoteAction (src/harness/agent.py). An agent cannot make a forward commitment whose consequences unfold.

Testing it would need a protocol amendment with agent-made decisions and a contingent world. The scenarios would have to be authored and frozen before any future-side contestant exists (CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 6). Even then, writing scenarios whose relevance is only future-mediated risks tuning the benchmark toward the temporal contestant, unless such cases come up naturally at a pre-registered rate.
future.itp_and_planning_comparison:
Comparison along the five parts defined in backward_obligations: D (source of derivation), R (representation), P (persistence across events), T (trigger re-evaluation), A (resulting action). Legend: [V] arXiv id and title verified in the local corpus; [U] arXiv id not in the local corpus (unverified); [NA] non-arXiv, checked through a repo or GitHub; [M] mandatory digest, code read but paper body unread; [LN] cited only in a lane note's corpus abstract.

| Prior art | D | R | P | T | A | What it pre-empts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ITP 2601.08955 [M] | 1 greedy imagined trajectory, adaptive K | prompt text | no; dropped after each step | no | next action | "simulate and interrogate futures, act from the present" |
| RAP / LATS / WebDreamer / WMA [U] | several imagined branches, scored or searched | search tree | episode only | no | select or veto an action, incl. irreversible-harm avoidance (WMA) | multiple futures; feared-future veto |
| RAFA [U] / LLMPC [LN] | long-horizon plan | memory buffer of feedback | feedback only | implicit, by re-planning each step | first action | the §15 loop; makes stored requirements redundant when re-planning is cheap |
| Relative reachability / AUP [U], Heitzig [V] | distribution over future goals vs a counterfactual baseline | penalty term | no | no | option-preserving action | §13 option preservation |
| SafePred / JANUS / SIMMER [V]; DreamGuard / ARTIS [LN]; SeerGuard [title differs] | feared delayed future | guardrail verdict, re-plan | no | no | block or re-plan | "future sends warnings backward" |
| SafeCommit [V] | retained plausible worlds | conformal certificate | no | no | act, probe, or fallback | robust option-preserving choice |
| LCPI [V] | candidate fault models | Last Identifiable Margin boundary | no | no | distinguish or homogenize | tipping-point logic |
| DeepRewind [V] | 1-step world-model prediction of a commit | typed epistemic graph | yes, within a run | yes; per-commitment trigger plus monitor | gate a commitment; roll back later | the derived reopen trigger. Organic firing absent in released code |
| RDM / EMA [NA]; DAPP [unverified] | ensemble of futures | failure regions; signposts | yes (DAPP) | yes (DAPP) | adaptive pathway | persisted signposts, if DAPP is admitted |
| PM-Bench / PIS / TriggerBench / ChronosBench | given or dialog-derived intentions | ledger or typed store | yes | yes | execute when due | the P and T machinery |

Reading the table: every part already exists. D is covered by ITP, RAP, WMA, SafePred and SafeCommit. P and T are covered by PM-Bench, PIS, DeepRewind and DAPP. A is covered by RAFA, AUP and SafeCommit. What is missing is one system that combines D (from a simulated future) with P and T, and acts by reopening executed decisions. That combination is an integration whose value is an empirical question, and the evidence so far points against it:
- 2601.03905 [V]: agents misuse foresight.
- Forecast-Dojo [V]: a carried belief notebook improved 6 of 12 models.
- Calibration Is Not Control [V]: prediction quality does not translate into control value.
- FinalityBench [V]: LLMs find gating unprompted.
- ITP: its own gains come from the cheapest variant, with no persistence.

Ablation any future-side claim needs, all arms at equal model and budget:
1. The current baseline. Its summary already tracks "open, parked or blocked work and what it is waiting for".
2. Baseline plus an ITP-I-style "imagine consequences" step per event.
3. Baseline plus a PIS-style typed obligation store with code triggers and depends_on links.
4. Baseline plus a DeepRewind-style dependency monitor.
5. The persisted-branch temporal contestant.

The temporal contestant earns a claim only if it beats max(2, 3, 4) on reopening recall and precision at matched cost.
future.prevented_future:
QUESTION 2. A forecast leads to an intervention, so the forecast outcome never happens. Is this already handled cleanly, and what is left for agents?

The concept is handled cleanly by existing work. What is left for agents is bookkeeping, one failure-mode study, and evaluation design. The positivity problem has no agent-specific solution.

1. The formal treatment is settled. The forecast's target is the potential outcome Y^{a0} under a named strategy a0 (no intervention): Dickerman & Hernán 2020 [NA]; Keogh & van Geloven 2024 and Boyer et al. 2025 [U], with IPW estimators of counterfactual calibration, AUC and Brier. When the agent takes a1, Y^{a0} is missing, not falsified. Scoring practice: annul the branch that was not realised.
- Metaculus Conditional Pairs: 'Annulled ... It is not scored'. forecasting-tools ships a ConditionalQuestion model with an ANNULLED status that LLM bots already use [NA].
- Decision markets void conditionals on actions not taken [NA].
- Public health scores a scenario projection only where its scenario held: Howerton 2023 [NA].

Reflexive cases, where publishing the forecast itself changes the outcome:
- performative prediction, Perdomo 2002.06673 [U];
- fixed-point scoring, Oesterheld et al. 2305.17601 [U]: no proper scoring rule makes optimal reports fixed points for more than two outcomes;
- counterfactual oracle with random erasure, Armstrong 1711.05541 [U].

Clinical work states the 'victim of its own success' problem directly:
- Boeken et al. 2403.00886 [U]: 'naive retraining ... underestimates the risk, due to effective workings of the previous model'. They give an identification result for the risk under the no-alarm policy.
- Liley et al. 2010.11530 [U]; Lenert 2019; Sperrin 2019.
- van Amsterdam et al. 2312.01210 [U; secondary summary]: requiring calibration both before and after deployment makes a model useless for decisions.
- Reflexive Model-World Systems [NA, not peer-reviewed] states NORTH_STAR §8 almost word for word: 'a dashboard that reports only mismatch ... would punish causal success'.

LLM agents:
- Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]: the decision object is the intervention advantage E[U | do(a), prefix] − E[U | continue, prefix], evaluated by same-prefix branching. Recalibration 'leaves control regret unchanged'.
- Intervention Paradox 2602.03338 [V]: a critic with AUROC 0.94 caused a 26 pp collapse (disruption-recovery tradeoff).

NORTH_STAR §8 is therefore correct but not new. Its wording 'Future A remains a valid prevented future' overclaims: the correct status is 'annulled / unverified', not 'valid'.

2. The positivity problem is the real obstacle, and NORTH_STAR does not address it. Take a deterministic policy π(H) = intervene iff f(H) > τ.
- For every history with f(H) > τ, P(A = a0 | H) = 0, so E[Y^{a0} | H] is not identified from the agent's own data. That is exactly the high-risk region where the forecast matters.
- 'Successful prevention' and 'false alarm followed by a harmless intervention' are then observationally identical.
- NORTH_STAR guards only against the first error, prevention mistaken for failed prediction. It leaves open the symmetric, self-serving error: failed prediction relabelled as prevention.
- That error is incentive-compatible for a self-scoring agent: forecast doom, intervene, claim credit (cf. the Oesterheld manipulation result).
- So a stored 'prevented' label must default to unverifiable and earn no calibration credit.
- The §15 loop step 'compare predicted vs realized → calibrate' is also invalid for any forecast that triggered an action.

Remedies (none is agent-specific):
- (a) Randomised withholding: counterfactual-oracle erasure; untreated holdouts, e.g. the OptHoldoutSize package [via Liley bibliography]; Chen & Kash: the decision rule 'must sometimes randomize'. Acceptable only for low-stakes warnings.
- (b) A resettable simulator or fork: same-prefix branching (Calibration Is Not Control); process and filesystem forks such as Shepherd 2605.10913 [V] or ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V]. Software worlds are unusually favourable here: when the feared outcome is computable (a test that would fail), the counterfactual can be executed in a sandbox. Any contestant, including the baseline, can already do this with A1 read_at plus A2 run_command in its own workspace. If the simulator is the same world model that issued the forecast, the check is circular.
- (c) Delayed external evidence that later reveals the counterfactual. This matches the protocol's pattern C. It requires the forecast to be stored with its cutoff, which FutureSim's PredictionHistory and Metaculus resolution already do.
- (d) Identification under assumptions (Boeken), which still needs exchangeability or positivity somewhere.

3. What is genuinely left for agents:
- (i) Bookkeeping. A long-lived agent keeping averted forecasts as typed records (forecaster or policy version, evidence cutoff, triggering intervention, status annulled / counterfactually checked / unverifiable). No LLM-agent implementation was found, but a checkpoint+RAG baseline can log the same record at negligible cost. Engineering, not capability.
- (ii) A failure-mode study, which I think is the most valuable concrete item. Self-evolving outcome-feedback memories may learn to under-warn after their own successful interventions:
  - Live-Evo 2602.02369 [V] down-weights 'misleading or stale experiences';
  - EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [V] reflects on delayed labels;
  - ExACT [U] stores expected-vs-actual reflections.
  
  A warning that prompted a successful intervention looks 'misleading' to all of them. This is Boeken's retraining bias moved into agent memory. Nothing in the digests demonstrates it for LLM agents, and the fixes are the standard causal remedies above.
- (iii) Evaluation design. A benchmark can score 'prevented' claims, because the evaluator controls the world and so has positivity: twin runs with and without the intervention, as in FinalityBench's twin pairs 2609.04706 [V] and ForecastBench-Sim's paired intervention worlds 2606.18686 [V]. That needs a world that reacts to agent actions. smoke_v1's event stream does not react to the agent, so this benchmark cannot instantiate a prevented future at all.

Bottom line: causal inference, conditional-forecast annulment, performative prediction, counterfactual oracles and clinical prediction-under-intervention already handle the concept cleanly. Agents add no new conceptual problem. Positivity makes 'prevented' unverifiable for a deterministic intervener unless it randomises or has a trusted simulator.
future.future_self_ux:
QUESTION 3. What evidence shows that interrogating a simulated future self improves decisions, and is an executable LLM copy needed?

Evidence on humans (all human-facing; none measures decision quality):
- Future You 2405.12514 (n=344; anxiety −0.68 vs +0.21 for control, p=0.001; the numbers come from a third-party wiki note) showed lower anxiety and higher future-self continuity.
- Future You multimodal 2512.06106 (N=92) found gains in continuity, well-being and motivation, with no difference between text, voice and avatar.
- Simulating Life Paths 2512.05397 [V] (N=192) found decision shifts:
  - one-sided avatars pushed people toward the option they presented;
  - a system-generated third option got adopted;
  - its limitations section says it 'assessed decision intentions rather than implemented behaviors'.
- AI-Powered Episodic Future Thinking 2503.16484 [cited only in a lane note's corpus abstract] is a usability study only.

So the measured effects are affective, and they show persuasion. Persuasion argues against this kind of interface as a tool for knowing: a simulated future self is a framing channel that can steer choices in whatever direction the simulation leans.

Evidence on agents:
- Nothing in the digests interrogates a simulated future version of the agent itself (its future policy, objectives or memory) and measures a benefit to decisions.
- The nearest results are mixed:
  - ITP's single pasted foresight helps on ALFWorld but loses to RAP on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen [mandatory digest, code read].
  - SIMMER foresight cuts latent failures by up to 72% [V].
  - WiA-LLM 2509.04791 forecasts game-state changes at 74.2%.
  - Prospection-Guided Retrieval 2605.14177 gets about 3x recall; that helps retrieval, not decisions.
  - BTF-2 2604.26106 finds that better forecasters differ mainly in their pre-mortems; the link is correlational.
  - 2601.03905 [V]: agents invoke simulation under 1% of the time, misuse it about 15% of the time, and lose up to 5% performance.
  - Forecast-Dojo [V]: a carried belief notebook helped 6 of 12 models.
- Agent work offers no positive evidence and some negative evidence.

Is an executable LLM copy needed? Not on current evidence, and probably not in principle.
- For a stateless model, a 'future self' is the same weights given a context that describes the projected state Ŝ_{t+Δ}. It has no information the present lacks.
- It can only add three things:
  1. Computation spent on rolling the world forward. That is world-model rollout, as in ITP-R, which alternates policy actions and world-model steps, or WebDreamer.
  2. A forked copy of the agent's accumulated memory to run forward. Forking memory or a process is a commodity: Shepherd 2605.10913 [V] forks the agent process and its filesystem, and ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V] forks at an event.
  3. Isolation from the present's deliberation, which may reduce anchoring or simply add variance.
- The 'self' framing adds nothing beyond role prompting. NORTH_STAR §6's questions ('which decision do you regret', 'what must I do now') are a pre-mortem.
- The decisive ablation compares two arms with the same model and token budget:
  - (a) one prompt: 'imagine state at T+Δ; list regrets, requirements and options to preserve';
  - (b) a role-separated copy with forked memory, driven by a world model through the horizon, then interrogated.
- If (b) does not beat (a), the executable copy is unnecessary.
- Given the agent evidence above, building future-self machinery before that ablation, and before a benchmark where the agent makes its own forward-looking decisions, would be building ahead of evidence.
- The current milestone's own boundary already excludes multiplicity: docs/milestone-2-design.md §0 says results are not a test of past-self dialogue or temporal multiplicity.
future.verdict:
The future side of NORTH_STAR does not contain a residual capability that is distinct from prior art. The project should drop it as a novelty claim.

Each component already exists:
- Forecasting: FutureSim, Forecast-Dojo, potential outcomes.
- Scenario simulation: robust decision making (RDM) and FORESIGHT-9.
- Action-conditioned rollout and world models: RAP, WebDreamer, WMA, ITP, Dyna-Think.
- Planning: RAP, LATS, FLARE.
- Model-predictive control: RAFA, LLMPC.
- Goal regression: BAR, Goal-Mem, classical regression.
- Option preservation: relative reachability, AUP, SafeCommit, LCPI, DeepRewind.
- Feared-future constraints: SafePred, JANUS, SIMMER.
- Regret: RAFA, Plaut et al., Calibration Is Not Control.
- Prospective memory: PM-Bench, PIS, TriggerBench, ChronosBench.
- Prevented-future scoring: Metaculus annulment, decision markets, counterfactual oracle, Boeken, Calibration Is Not Control.

The NORTH_STAR §15 loop is receding-horizon control plus calibration, and §8 is conditional-forecast annulment.

What remains is three narrow, non-architectural items:
1. **A low-prior empirical hypothesis, "future-mediated relevance".** A persisted store of weighted simulated branches with attached obligations might catch reopenings that are linked only through a simulated future. It would have to beat three cheaper arms: the baseline plus an ITP-I-style imagine step, a PIS-style typed obligation store with depends_on links, and a DeepRewind-style dependency monitor. A re-check prompt over a stored list, which the repo baseline's summary and notes already approximate, matches persistence when the list is short. Typed triggers plus truth-maintenance dependencies match it at scale. Neither needs time to be addressable.
2. **A failure-mode study.** Outcome-feedback memories (Live-Evo, EpiEvolve, ExACT-style) may learn to under-warn after their own successful interventions. The fixes are standard causal ones.
3. **Bookkeeping and evaluation design.** Averted-forecast records should default to the status "unverifiable", because a deterministic agent that always intervenes violates positivity. They can be scored only by an evaluator that controls the world with twin runs (FinalityBench, ForecastBench-Sim style).

None of the three can be tested with the current harness. smoke_v1 is an event stream that does not react to the agent, its decisions are authored by the world, and agents can only reopen or note. Testing any of them would need a protocol v0.3 with decisions the agent makes and a world that reacts to them. That protocol must be authored and frozen before any future-side contestant exists.

The executable future-self copy has no supporting evidence for agents. Human studies show affective and persuasive effects, not better decisions, and agent foresight results are mixed to negative. It should not be built unless a matched-budget pre-mortem-prompt ablation fails first.

Recommendations:
- Keep the future side out of Tesseract scope.
- Cite this prior art.
- Correct NORTH_STAR §8 from "valid prevented future" to "annulled or unverified counterfactual".
- Add positivity as a known limit on the §15 "compare predicted vs realized" step.

Caveats:
- Many foundational IDs are unverified in the local corpus: RAP, LATS, WebDreamer, WMA, RAFA, relative reachability, AUP, Perdomo, Armstrong, Boeken, Liley, van Amsterdam.
- DAPP signposts are unverified in any source.
- Several items are cited only in lane notes: LLMPC, Goal-Mem, TriggerBench, DreamGuard.
- Paper bodies were unread for ITP, PM-Bench, DeepRewind and Calibration Is Not Control. Their ratings rest on code and abstracts.

Files consulted: /home/user/temporal-agent/NORTH_STAR.md, EXPERIMENT.md, docs/milestone-2-design.md, docs/protocol-amendments.md, src/baseline/memory.py, src/contestant_runtime/protocol.py, src/harness/agent.py, world/events/smoke_v1/events.jsonl, plus the scratchpad files lit/synth/digest_mandatory.md, lit/synth/digest_sweep.md, and lit/notes/sweep-{backward-optionality,prospective-forecast,performative-prevented,counterfactual-worldmodel}.md.

comparison.benchmark: MemoryArena (arXiv:2602.16313; github.com/ZexueHe/MemoryArena @6cd9de14). Citation verified: code read, abstract mirrored verbatim; paper tables unverified
comparison.what_it_measures: Memory used across chains of interdependent subtasks in four domains: bundled shopping, group travel, progressive web search and formal reasoning. Memory is pluggable through add_chunk/wrap_user_prompt. Metrics are SR, PS, SPS and passrate. Tasks average about 57 action steps (search extract).
comparison.overlap_with_smoke_v1: Both evaluate a long-lived agent across sessions against a strong-memory baseline set: long-context, BM25, embedding RAG, Mem0/Mem0-graph, Letta, MIRIX, MemoRAG and ReasoningBank.
comparison.gap: Dependencies run strictly forward. No implemented task requires noticing that later information invalidates an earlier decision; the travel prompt that allows revision is dead code. Feedback modes inject ground truth rather than test whether the agent notices. There is no fidelity scoring and no remediation.
comparison.reusable_for: A no-regression check that a temporal contestant does not lose on ordinary forward-dependency memory. Gives within-benchmark comparability with the reported MAGE and FlowState numbers, though those used other backbones. Does not test reopening.
comparison.license_or_access: Code is public with no top-level LICENSE, so run locally and do not redistribute. Leakage risk: runners hold ground truth (travel reset returns answers; shopping observations carry target_products). wrap_user_prompt is called only at subtask start, so tool-style temporal queries need runner changes. Default judges are gpt-4o/gpt-4.1, i.e. cross-provider.

comparison.benchmark: MAGE evaluation (arXiv:2606.06090). Verified abstract (MSR page); mechanism and results from search extracts
comparison.what_it_measures: MAGE's results on MemoryArena with Qwen3.6-27B/ReAct: +7.8 to +20.4 pp SR over long-context, RAG and agent-memory baselines. Ablation: Revise contributes -4.0 to -5.2 pp. The 55.1% token reduction has an unverified comparator.
comparison.overlap_with_smoke_v1: Revise reopens an earlier committed boundary when a later check shows it was wrong, and keeps the flawed branch. That is the reopen move, applied to the agent's own state.
comparison.gap: It works within one task, on the agent's own subtask summaries, and is triggered by a validator. Its hint channel H deliberately injects hindsight. It has no world-authored artifacts, no true-then/known-then separation, no forward remediation, and no evaluation that isolates reopening.
comparison.reusable_for: A design for a baseline arm (path-structured memory with a validator), and an external reference number on MemoryArena. Not a benchmark to adapt to.
comparison.license_or_access: Paper only; no code found (github.com/microsoft/MAGE is an unrelated project). arXiv text was reachable only through search extracts.

comparison.benchmark: FlowState evaluation (arXiv:2609.34565). Abstract and metadata verified; method and results from search extracts only
comparison.what_it_measures: A MemoryArena subset (shopping, travel, formal reasoning) and τ³-Bench airline/retail, with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Reported gains: +4.55 pp SR on MemoryArena and +13.95 pp on τ³, with 43.2% and 40.6% fewer tokens.
comparison.overlap_with_smoke_v1: The motivating example (hotel decision D7 reopened with linked evidence when B's price drops, giving D8) has the same structure as smoke_v1's premise.
comparison.gap: The verifier notes the D7/D8 behaviour was never evaluated in isolation; the metrics are aggregate. Decisions are the agent's own judgements. There is no epistemic cutoff and no code remediation.
comparison.reusable_for: A design for a typed decision/evidence-graph baseline arm, needed to avoid confounding structure with time. τ³ is usable as a no-regression check.
comparison.license_or_access: Code not released ('at an appropriate time'). Method text unverified.

comparison.benchmark: PM-Bench (arXiv:2607.12385; github.com/genglinliu/PMBench @e1093c4). Code verified; paper body unread
comparison.what_it_measures: Prospective memory: carrying out deferred intentions at the right cue or time while busy with other work. One synthetic week of 80 steps with 83 intentions (57 event-based, 26 time-based), 11 explicit updates, hidden state channels and lures. Scored by micro Set-F1. Best macro result is 65.1% (heartbeat-proactive); best single run is 79.1%.
comparison.overlap_with_smoke_v1: smoke_v1's parked-work reconsideration (TCK-0107 blocked on the SDK in evt-0003, unblocked by the SDK 1.4.0 bump in evt-0008) is an event-cued deferred intention.

There is no reopening of executed decisions, no fidelity scoring and no remediation. The follow-up PIS (2609.01272, digest abstract only) reaches 82.9% with a typed intention store driven by code.

comparison.benchmark: STALE (arXiv:2605.06527). Verified in the abstract corpus; the 67.8% figure comes from a sibling WebSearch extract
comparison.what_it_measures: 400 conflict scenarios and 1,200 queries, with contexts up to 150K tokens. Probes: State Resolution, Premise Resistance, and Implicit Policy Adaptation (IPA, acting on updated state without a prompt). 'Implicit Conflict' means a later observation invalidates memory without negating it. Best model: 55.2%. A prototype scores 91% on SR but 32% on IPA. In 67.8% of failed IPA cases the updated evidence was visible to the model.

comparison.gap: Covers facts and preferences in conversational memory, probed by queries. Nothing is reopened, no executed decision is remediated, and over-intervention is not priced.
comparison.reusable_for: IPA as an external measure of 'notice and act'. Its 67.8% finding is direct evidence that the bottleneck is acting on evidence, not reaching the past. StateAuditor (2608.01619) already reports on it (+5.0 pts).
comparison.license_or_access: Code and data availability is not recorded in the digests; verify before planning.

comparison.what_it_measures: 234 multi-session scenarios in which facts, constraints and decisions are revised. Scenarios are symbolic event programs replayed deterministically into ground truth. Grading checks whether answers use the current or a superseded value. A state wrapper adds +32 to +67 pts; a length- and cost-matched control attributes +15 to +32 to state structure.
comparison.overlap_with_smoke_v1: Its construction is the project's: a deterministic event program yields ground truth, decisions get revised, and drift is scored.
comparison.gap: Revisions are explicit operations in the program and only answers are graded. There is no unprompted reopening and no remediation.
comparison.reusable_for: An external test for an explicit current-state or decision-register baseline arm. Its matched-control result is the strongest prior that structure, not time, carries the gains.

comparison.what_it_measures: 64 scenarios across 8 domains, 1,879 rounds and 365 dynamic updates. Hidden full ground truth; multi-channel sessions, workspace files and staged updates; multiple-choice and shell-based executable checks. Tests multi-source conflict, dynamic belief revision and implicit personalization.
comparison.overlap_with_smoke_v1: The closest existing harness: hidden truth, staged updates that invalidate earlier conclusions, workspace files and executable checks.

Adapting needs five changes: retarget updates at decision artifacts, replace probes with the no-hint trigger protocol, add negative controls, add three-way probes, and score remediation by tests. It is also usable as-is for prompted belief revision.
comparison.license_or_access: The abstract says code is available, but the URL was not captured and the license is unknown.

comparison.benchmark: FutureSim (arXiv:2605.15188; github.com/OpenForecaster/futuresim @908322f). Verified; code read; ablation numbers unverified
comparison.what_it_measures: Chronological replay of Jan-Mar 2026 news with date-capped search and hidden ground truth. Agents submit and revise distributions daily and get Brier feedback.
