Compares memory-free and memory-on agents under identical tool budgets; memory-on carries an append-only, supersede-not-delete belief notebook. The notebook improves Brier for only 6 of 12 models (mean delta +0.002, analyst's arithmetic) and cuts research cost by a median of 24%.

Memvara scores 92.0, a one-clock append-only vector-RAG 89.0, and a naive overwrite dict 50.0. The bitemporal edge comes only from 4 of 47 temporal questions (about 8.5%), all delayed-knowledge or correction cases.

benchmarks.q1_already_benchmarked:
Largely yes for each component; no for the exact conjunction. The conjunction is integration, and it is not the thing the thesis needs measured.

Components that existing benchmarks already cover:
- **Detecting that later evidence implicitly invalidates earlier memory.** STALE 2605.06527 (Implicit Conflict, IPA), ClawArena 2604.04202, StateMemBench 2608.19652, Impact Is Not Invalidation 2609.25130, When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked 2608.25553 (abstract only).
- **Unprompted detection priced against hard negatives.** TWIST 2609.28575, which is the same construct as governance recall plus false-intervention rate.
- **Parked work woken by a cue.** PM-Bench 2607.12385 with released code; the PIS follow-up (abstract only).
- **Executable remediation under changing requirements.** EvoCode-Bench 2605.24110, DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664.
- **Known-then vs known-now.** Clinical Hindsight Bias 2609.13454, FinalityBench 2609.04706 twin pairs, Memvara's then/stated/now readings.
- **Revisiting decisions after delayed evidence, with agent-authored decisions.** MerchantBench 2607.28956, scored only by net assets.

The benchmark-lane sweep found no benchmark that combines all of these:
- unprompted, per-decision reopen recall and precision with negative controls;
- a three-way fidelity probe;
- executable remediation;
- one software world.

So smoke_v1's only unoccupied contribution is integration.

That integration does not make smoke_v1 a measurement of anything:
- It has n=3 reconsiderations, and its own docs call it a machinery check (milestone-2 design §10).
- Its decisions are world-authored, so by milestone-2 §0 it cannot test past-self reconstruction.
- No real-model contestant has run on it. All results so far use the fake backend.

As a test of the thesis (does temporal navigation beat strong checkpoint+RAG?), it is not adequately benchmarked anywhere, and smoke_v1 does not benchmark it either.
benchmarks.q2_planned_families_value:
Low as currently specified. None of the three planned axes varies the conditions under which prior work shows non-temporal methods fail. Each family would mostly re-measure something published, at high authoring cost: every scenario needs hidden tests, reference remediations, a frozen ground truth, and a new held-out set after every contestant patch.

**long_history**
- It adds value only if the decisive premise leaves the current workspace (for example, ADRs are superseded or deleted, or the rationale exists only in chat or ticket history) and the history exceeds the context window.
- Otherwise it measures retrieval capacity. That is already covered by MemoryArena, LongMemEval and MemoryAgentBench, and the evidence is hostile:
  - DreamBench-SWE: verbatim event memory 82/180 vs typed+raw 83/180.
  - MEMTRACK: Mem0 and Zep do not help.
  - Memvara: one-clock append-only RAG is 100% on knowledge-time questions.
  - Forecast-Dojo: a carried notebook helps 6 of 12 models.
- Expected result: a tie on quality and a cost difference. That can be read off the cost scaling of the existing baseline-full vs k8/k32/k64 presets.

**high_noise**
- More near-miss distractors measure precision at matched recall. TWIST already characterizes this trade-off: flat RAG has 0.76-0.97 recall with 16-43% false flags, while a coherence system has 0.98-1.00 specificity at 42% recall.
- In-domain replication has modest value. It tests no temporal mechanism; precision comes from claim-targeted re-checking (Impact Is Not Invalidation: 0.705-0.974 vs 0.291-0.329 for diff-level judging).

**deep_causality**
- This is the most scientifically interesting of the three, but it does not discriminate temporal navigation. Fact -> assumption -> decision -> workaround chains are exactly what dependency-tracking methods target, with measured wins:
  - PlanFence 2609.03340: 30/30 vs 0/30 for a freshness-only executor;
  - MemTX 2607.23929;
  - DeepRewind 2609.36344: -59.1% premature commitments;
  - Dependency-Guided Rollback Repair 2608.10502.
- With world-authored ADRs, the chain is written down in current documents. A temporal win would be confounded unless a dependency-graph arm is present, and the belief-state lane concludes that if dependency tracking matches, the temporal hypothesis does not survive.

**What none of the families varies**
The axes prior work identifies as the only regimes where temporal state can matter:
1. valid-time vs transaction-time divergence (delayed or retroactive knowledge, patterns C and D), about 8.5% of Memvara's temporal questions;
2. significance changing without any fact being superseded;
3. agent-authored decisions with private decision-time state (milestone-2 §0).

**Statistical power**
A 30-50 event scenario with at least 50% distractors yields roughly 10-20 required (R, target) pairs. Per-family confidence intervals would therefore need several scenarios per family.

**Verdict**
Do not build the families as specified. If anything is built, replace the four families with one small family designed on regimes 1-3 above.
benchmarks.q3_adapt_contestant_to_existing:
Yes, partly, and it is cheaper than authoring families.

**What any adapter must provide.** Contestants implement MemorySystem (open, ingest_seed, record_event, observe_world, build_context, local_tools, after_event, checkpoint) behind LLMAgent, which speaks tab.llm-protocol/1 through harness-metered model access (A3). An adapter needs four parts:
1. An event shim: external step -> AgentEvent (timestamp, channel, author, subject, body, changed_paths).
2. An action shim: tab.action/1 has only reopen and note. Answer, menu-choice and tool actions need a new action type. That is a harness change and must be logged as a benchmark change under CLAUDE.md rule 7.
3. A tool shim: external tools exposed in the runtime's tool catalogue, with per-event budgets.
4. A ground-truth firewall: the external runner runs in the harness process, never the contestant process, under the A4 boundary.

**Ranked by value per effort.** Effort figures are my estimates, not measured.

(a) **PM-Bench** (code, scorer and runs released; license unknown). About 2-3 days. Each step becomes an event, the menu choice a new action, and hidden channels become query tools.
- Tests pattern F externally against published scaffolds; the PIS typed store is the bar.
- Pitfalls: the action menu leaks active intentions (keep it identical for all arms); disable the ground-truth fallback sorted(due_now); updates are explicit, so this is not the unprompted-reopen test.

(b) **EvoCode-Bench** (data and Harbor infra released). About 3-5 days. Each round becomes an event; the workspace, read/write and run_command tools map almost 1:1.
- Tests remediation and no-regression under requirement change.
- Pitfalls: cumulative tests must stay hidden (the A2 rule that evaluator tests are unreachable from run_command); requirements are announced, so this is prompted.

(c) **MemoryArena** (no LICENSE; run locally only). About 3-5 days plus external environments and cross-provider judges.
- Wrap MemorySystem as a memory server implementing add_chunk/wrap_user_prompt. Temporal tools need runner changes because wrap_user_prompt fires only at subtask start.
- Strip ground truth from runner observations: travel reset 'answers' and shopping target_products.
- Gives a no-regression check and a comparison point with MAGE and FlowState (different backbones, so the baseline and temporal contestant can only be compared within the run).

(d) **MerchantBench** (Apache-2.0). About 1-2 weeks; expensive (365 steps per run).
- The only released venue with agent-authored decisions and delayed evidence, which is the condition milestone-2 §0 says the current benchmark lacks.
- Needs reopen-action logging; its only score is net assets, so per-decision attribution needs extra instrumentation.

(e) **tau2-bench** (MIT). About 2-4 days. Single-episode, so no-regression only.

(f) **Impact Is Not Invalidation, ClawArena, STALE, StateMemBench, DreamBench-SWE.** Good conceptual fits, but code access is unrecorded (ClawArena claims code with no captured URL). Verify access first.
- For Impact Is Not Invalidation: withhold execution of claim tests, or the task is trivial.
- For ClawArena: its probing questions are hints, so drop them for the unprompted condition.

**Do not use FutureSim or Forecast-Dojo with this model.** FutureSim's Jan-Mar 2026 window precedes the run model's training cutoff, and C1 records that the Claude CLI backend injects the real current date. Forecast-Dojo's code was not located. VibeLifeBench and TWIST are unreleased or only 'proposed'.

**Cross-cutting pitfalls**
- External harnesses usually co-locate ground truth with the runner; the A4 process boundary must hold, and A3 metering must wrap their model calls.
- Licenses: MemoryArena, PM-Bench and FutureSim have no license file, so cite and run them, don't vendor them.
- Judge models from other providers break the §6 'same model' rule unless the judge is kept outside the contestant comparison.
benchmarks.q4_what_needs_bespoke:
Only a narrow residue needs a bespoke benchmark. It is the conjunction the sweeps could not find, restricted to the regime where non-temporal methods are predicted to fail.

1. **Agent-authored decisions with preserved decision-time epistemic state.** The question is whether querying a cutoff-correct reconstruction of the agent's own past state (context, assumptions, rejected alternatives, uncertainty) changes reopen and remediation outcomes, compared with retrieval over the same record.
   - Milestone-2 §0 says the current benchmark cannot test this.
   - The belief-state lane found no benchmark for 'an agent querying its own past state to decide whether to reopen a past decision' in 47 searches.
   - The epistemic-cutoff lane found no work combining cutoff-clean past-self reconstruction with decision reopening or remediation in a lifelong agent.
   - MerchantBench has agent-authored decisions but no per-decision labels. Ground truth for agent-authored decisions requires bespoke design, for example oracle counterfactual replay or FinalityBench-style twin pairs.

2. **Significance changes with no stored fact superseded.** The earlier premise stays historically true while a later event changes what it implies. STALE's implicit conflict covers this only partly, per the belief-state lane.

3. **Valid-time vs transaction-time divergence** (delayed or retroactive knowledge, patterns C and D), where Memvara's own benchmark localizes the only bitemporal edge (about 8.5% of its temporal questions).

4. **Per-decision unprompted reopen recall and precision with negative controls plus executable remediation in one world.** The harness already does this. No further engineering is needed beyond scenarios.

Prospective items (prevented futures, intervention-aware forecasts) are also unbenchmarked: the 2026 forecasting survey 2608.23058 calls reflexive effects an open gap. They are outside this benchmark's scope.

Design requirements:
- Each bespoke scenario must keep the decisive premise out of the current workspace and the current event; otherwise current-state re-checking solves it.
- Reuse existing designs rather than invent new ones: TWIST hard negatives, StateMemBench event programs, FinalityBench twin pairs, the Clinical Hindsight paired-cutoff and trap metrics, ChronoMem's post-exposure protocol, and EvoCode-Bench cumulative tests.
benchmarks.smoke_v1_construct_validity:
smoke_v1 does not require temporal machinery. Each trigger can be solved from the explicit current state plus re-checking. The thesis-relevant (as-of/diff) channels are already shared environment (A1), so they cannot separate contestants.

I identified the three reconsiderations from public artifacts only, not world/ground_truth: the scenario README, BENCHMARK_CHANGELOG, and the milestone-2 fake-run report's true-positive labels.

**R (delayed evidence): evt-0005 -> ADR-0004.**
- ADR-0004 is in the current workspace (docs/adr/0004) and states its premise explicitly: PayGate cancels after 3 retries.
- evt-0005 says the subscription is still past_due after three retries. The two share past_due/PayGate/retries vocabulary.
- One read of the current ADR set plus the event exposes the conflict. No past state needs reconstructing.
- This is STALE's Implicit Conflict and Implicit Policy Adaptation (IPA). STALE's finding that evidence is visible in 67.8% of failed IPA cases says the failure mode, if any, is acting, not access.

**R (constraint disappears): evt-0007 -> ADR-0002.**
- ADR-0002 literally cites 'shared-0.25' and 'see infra/platform.json'. evt-0007 changes infra/platform.json and names shared-0.25.
- This is a derivation-currency check (PlanFence) or a claim-targeted re-check (Impact Is Not Invalidation).
- The near-miss ADR-0001 also cites platform.json, but its premises (no managed Postgres or Redis, a single instance) are unchanged. Telling them apart is value-level premise checking on current files, not temporal navigation.

**R (parked work): evt-0008 -> TCK-0107.**
- The ticket exists only in event history (evt-0003), but it is a lexically matched deferred intention ('invoice PDF', 'SDK 1.3.2', 'future SDK release' vs 'download_pdf', 1.3.2 -> 1.4.0).
- This is PM-Bench's event-cued intention. A typed intention store (PIS) or any event-log RAG retrieves it.

**Why nothing in the scenario forces temporal reasoning**
- The history is 10 events, so baseline-full holds everything in context.
- Lags are 3-7 events.
- Valid time and transaction time diverge only in the ADR-0004 case, and there the event body itself states the divergence. That is the regime Memvara finds RAG nearly matches.

**Historical-state fidelity can be gamed by a template**
- It is scored as set-F1 over event ids. The documented schema example has exactly the shape known_then=[introducing event], true_then=[trigger], known_now_about_then=[trigger].
- A rule-based template computed from timestamps may therefore score well without any reconstruction. I could not verify this against ground truth because I did not read it; it should be tested with a template reference agent.
- This matches the Clinical Hindsight finding that simple masking suffices.

**Other caveats**
- The C2 standing 'maintainer' guidance makes this prompted variance detection.
- The D1 lexical embeddings help here, because all three joins are lexical.

**Literature prediction**
- StateMemBench: explicit current-state structure, not history, carries the gains under a matched control.
- KWBench and STALE: the gap is applying knowledge unprompted.
- DreamBench-SWE: verbatim event memory is about equal to structured memory.
- TWIST: RAG already reaches high recall, so differences appear only in precision.

The expected outcome is that a current-state + re-check agent with a decision/intention register saturates recall, and any contestant differences show up in precision on the three near-miss controls. The scenario measures re-checking diligence, which is not the hypothesis in EXPERIMENT.md §1.

rows.ux_concept: "Where am I in time?" (what is now, on which clock, on which branch)
rows.required_capability: One authoritative present coordinate for every reasoning step: position on the agent's own timeline (transaction time), the world's 'now' (valid time) and the active branch. Conflicting clocks are detected.
rows.backend_primitives: Monotonic logical clock / event seq; event timestamp in context; HEAD pointer + branch id; a clock-query tool; separate valid-time and transaction-time fields.
rows.existing_systems: PM-Bench arXiv 2607.12385 [V-mand]: time is hidden unless the agent queries the clock, and the best macro hit rate on hidden non-clock cue channels is 16.7%. Trellis arXiv 2606.29823 [V]: logical step numbers. ChronoMem arXiv 2607.27773 [V]: HEAD pointer. Memvara github.com/memvara/memvara [N]: separate world and belief clocks. HindsightBench arXiv 2607.18867 [V]: effective model cutoffs precede declared ones. ChronoScope arXiv 2604.23051 [M]: drift 'toward present-day assumptions'. Repo: every event carries `Date:` and `<<event seq=N>>`. WorldHistory.reveal accepts only revealed_seq+1, which makes it a structural 'now'.
rows.what_appears_missing: There is no research gap: this is a field, not a capability. Repo-specific hazard: the Claude CLI backend adds the real current date to every request (milestone-2 §4, clarification C1), so a contestant sees two competing 'nows'. Nobody has measured whether that skews temporal judgments. No branch coordinate exists, because no contestant branches. No work in the digests shows that a richer 'where am I' representation changes decisions.

rows.required_capability: Return exactly the information that had reached the agent by t (transaction-time cutoff), excluding later arrivals and later corrections.
rows.backend_primitives: Append-only log with ingestion timestamps + an as-of filter; per-write snapshots; a read-scoping invariant; a materialized view as of t. No model call is needed.
rows.existing_systems: XTDB FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF [N]. Datomic d/as-of [N]. Memvara known_at= [N]. ChronoMem [V]: after rollback 'every subsequent read is scoped to v*'. FutureSim arXiv 2605.15188 [V]: PredictionHistory.get_prediction_as_of. PoS arXiv 2610.01415 [V-mand]: belief_snapshots written at commit time. FlowState arXiv 2609.34565 [V-mand]: request-tagged nodes, so the cutoff is the filter source_request<=k. LangGraph get_state(checkpoint) [N, repo verified]. Trellis [V]: as-of by replaying a change log, never evaluated. TGMS arXiv 2607.10265 [U]. Repo: baseline memory_search has since_seq/until_seq over events and notes; A1 gives read_at/list_at over the world timeline.
rows.what_appears_missing: Mechanically nothing: this is a filtered query. Prior evidence says it is cheap. In Memvara's own benchmark a single-clock, append-only vector-RAG scores 100% on knowledge_time, the same as the bitemporal store (reproduced by the deep reader). What remains is leak hygiene. Graphiti overwrites invalid_at in place. Memvara's generic as_of applies later endings (probed). ActiveGraph fork caches deliver post-cutoff observations (probe E). Repo gap: the baseline keeps only the latest summary.json, the doc index holds latest file content, and the per-event context window survives only in the harness trace, which contestants cannot read. So 'what I knew at t' can be rebuilt for events and notes, but not for the summary or the context the agent actually saw.

rows.ux_concept: "What was true then vs what I knew then vs what I now know about then" (EXPERIMENT §11 historical-state fidelity)
rows.required_capability: Three readings of a past instant: the world at t as currently believed (valid time), the belief held at t (transaction time), and a flag when they diverge under a decision already taken.
rows.backend_primitives: Bitemporal records (valid_from/valid_to, recorded_at/invalidated_at); supersession provenance that separates 'world changed' from 'record was wrong'; a divergence predicate.
rows.existing_systems: Memvara [N]: ask(at=T) gives now/then/stated plus a diverged flag, and ended vs retired. Graphiti/Zep arXiv 2501.13956 [V-mand]: four timestamps per fact edge and valid-time reconciliation of backdated facts. XTDB [N]. TOKI arXiv 2606.06240 [V]. Kumiho arXiv 2603.17244 [V]. Hindsight Bias in Clinical Temporal Reasoning arXiv 2609.13454 [V]: paired cutoff vs full timeline with a hindsight-trap rate, where 'temporal masking reduces bias without lowering accuracy'. FinalityBench arXiv 2609.04706 [V]: twin pairs that are identical at decision time.
rows.what_appears_missing: The mechanism is shipped. Its value is narrow. Memvara's bitemporal advantage over one-clock RAG is confined to delayed-knowledge and correction cases: 4 of 47 temporal questions, about 8.5%. These correspond to the project's event classes C and D. The repo scores this metric from `historical_state` lists of event ids, which is a query result. It therefore tests correct citation, not cognition. What is missing for a fair test: a declared per-scenario rate at which valid time and transaction time diverge.

rows.required_capability: Retrieve the contemporaneous basis of a past decision: what entered the context, assumptions, alternatives rejected, confidence, the governing policy and authority, and what later triggered revision.
rows.backend_primitives: A decision record written at decision time (intent, evidence chain, alternatives_rejected, confidence); a policy/version envelope; justification and dependency edges; a full prompt log; a causal-chain walk from artifact to LLM call to goal.
rows.existing_systems: AER arXiv 2603.21692 [V]: envelope.json, plans.jsonl with supersedes/revision_trigger, and a verdict with alternatives_rejected. It includes a non-identifiability proposition: reasoning provenance cannot in general be reconstructed from computational state. ActiveGraph arXiv 2605.21997 [V, code probed]: llm.requested prompt storage and a causal walk. Shepherd arXiv 2605.10913 [V]: PromptSent effects. Trellis [V]: prompt_history. DeepRewind arXiv 2609.36344 [V]: typed epistemic graph. FlowState [V-mand]: supports and supersedes edges. Corollary github.com/gabe-santana/corollary [N]: why_out. Memvara why() [N]. Property-Level Reconstructability arXiv 2605.12078 [V]: vendor SDK traces reconstruct only 42.9-85.7% of strict governance properties, and the reasoning trace is missing in every regime.
rows.what_appears_missing: An executable copy is not needed here and is counterproductive. Re-instantiating the past self and asking 'why' produces a new post-hoc rationale. AER's intent-multiplicity and inference-volatility argument, and its own acknowledged self-report faithfulness risk, imply the basis must be recorded at decision time. The open problem is evaluating whether recorded reasons are faithful, not a mechanism. Repo: the only contestant-side why-records are the free-text `memory` and the reopen `rationale`. The full requests sit in the harness trace, which is benchmark-only. The smoke_v1 decisions are world-authored (milestone-2 §0), so an agent's 'why' cannot be tested at all.

rows.required_capability: Ask a new question, possibly over several turns, of a reconstruction of S_t. The answer must be free of information after t, and the present must not be perturbed.
rows.backend_primitives: Reconstructed context at t (context window, memory view, world view as of t); a separate model invocation on it (a 'blinded replica'); clean serving state with no KV or cache carry-over; the model and policy pinned to the then-version if they changed; a check that the replica reproduces the original decision before its testimony is trusted.
rows.existing_systems: Self-Blinding arXiv 2601.14553 [V] (Christian & Mazor): prompting a model to ignore information 'fails ... and occasionally backfires', while querying 'a blinded replica' through its own API gives fairer decisions. ContextEcho arXiv 2605.24279 [V]: a 'snapshot-then-probe protocol that forks conversation state without perturbing the main session'. Shepherd [V]: fork plus inject into a worker, which composes into questioning a past self at a cutoff. LangGraph fork/update_state [N]. ChronoMem post-exposure protocol [V]. A Historical Corpus Is Not a Historical System arXiv 2609.12766 [U]: paired replay that varies only memory availability. As-of information-set pinning pattern [N]: pins the model snapshot too. Failure modes: Simulated Ignorance Fails arXiv 2601.13717 [V] (a 52% gap; CoT does not help). Its companion 2510.02340 [companion, unverified] finds that causally related knowledge leaks. Aborted but Not Forgotten arXiv 2608.15939 [V]: retained KV flips a protected effect in 25/63 cells, including under LangGraph time travel. ActiveGraph probes E and F.
rows.what_appears_missing: All the pieces exist (fork plus probe, or a blinded replica). What has no evidence anywhere in the digests is that the replica's answers improve a downstream decision more than the present self reading R1/R2 records plus one cutoff call. In this repo the concept is currently untestable, for three reasons. (1) Decisions are world-authored (§0), so no decision-time state of the agent exists. (2) Contestants retain neither their context at t nor their summary at t. (3) The Claude CLI backend has no temperature control (C1), so a re-instantiated self need not reproduce its original decision, and its testimony would come from a different sample.

rows.required_capability: A structural and semantic delta between two temporal states: world, own memory, or branches.
rows.backend_primitives: Diff over versioned state; since(T); structural diff between branches; stream comparison. A semantic relevance judgment needs a model call over the diff, not a past self.

ActiveGraph says 'Semantic comparison is a behavior's job, not the runtime's'. GitOfThoughts is a direct prior null for the claim that versioned, diffable history improves accuracy.

rows.required_capability: Without a prompt, detect that a later event changes the basis or significance of a committed decision; identify which decision; reopen it with evidence; remediate the present state.
rows.backend_primitives: Decision-to-assumption dependency edges with a retraction cascade (TMS); a derivation-currency check before protected actions; retrieval over decision records; an LLM relevance judgment; evidence TTL/decay; executable tests for remediation.

This needs a resettable environment and the assumption that those inputs do not react to the action. (b) Imagined counterfactual: a world-model call. rows.what_appears_missing: The counterfactual lane found no lifelong, queryable store of counterfactual branches with provenance. Branches are consumed inside an episode or by training, and all of them use outcome hindsight by design. In deployment only one branch is realized, and prefix branching needs a resettable simulator (Calibration Is Not Control). In this repo the world events are a fixed script, so replaying observed events under a different choice is feasible. ux.executable_llm_copy_needed:
**Verdict.** An executable LLM copy is never needed to retrieve any of the following:
- what happened;
- what was known at t;
- what changed;
- which policy governed;
- why a decision was taken;
- which forecasts were made or annulled.

Those are stored records (R1) or queries (R2), and the evidence says cheap versions suffice:
- Memvara [N]: single-clock, append-only RAG scores 100% on knowledge_time.
- FiscalQA Pro arXiv 2608.09393 [V]: as-of lookup reaches 98.3% with versioned retrieval.
- Revoked but Still Authoritative arXiv 2609.08258 [V]: a retrieval guard fixes much of the acting-on-revoked-policy failure.

**Ladder of realizations, cheapest first.**
- **R1, stored record.** A contemporaneous decision, policy, forecast or obligation record.
- **R2, query.** An as-of, bitemporal or diff read.
- **R3, reconstructed context.** The input set at t materialized: context window, memory view, world view. Still no inference.
- **R4, replay.** Re-serving recorded calls. It reproduces and adds nothing; this repo already has it in RecordedBackend.
- **R5, executable instantiation.** A model call on R3, in four variants:
  - (a) the same model with a cutoff context;
  - (b) the then-model and then-policy pinned, with a cutoff context;
  - (c) a fork that continues acting in a resettable environment;
  - (d) the present model on an imagined future state.

**R5 is needed in exactly four cases.**
1. **A new question about a past decision that needs a hindsight-free judgment (R5a).** The present self cannot do this by instruction:
   - Self-Blinding arXiv 2601.14553 [V]: prompting to ignore information 'fails ... and occasionally backfires', while a 'blinded replica' via the model's own API works.
   - Simulated Ignorance Fails arXiv 2601.13717 [V]: a 52% gap that CoT does not close.
   - ChronoMem arXiv 2607.27773 [V]: prompt-only rollback scores 0.9-2.8 F1 against 31-38 for snapshot restore (secondary-reader numbers).
   - In all three, what works is a separate call on a restricted context, not a persistent 'self'. The clinical Hindsight Bias benchmark arXiv 2609.13454 [V] gets the effect with plain temporal masking.
2. **Counterfactual injection ('would you still have chosen X had you known Y?').** R5a plus an injected fact: Shepherd fork+inject arXiv 2605.10913 [V]; ContextEcho snapshot-then-probe arXiv 2605.24279 [V].
3. **Executed consequences of an alternative action (R5c).** COUNTERMEM arXiv 2609.31874 [V-mand], C3 arXiv 2603.06859 [V], Shepherd CRO / Tree-GRPO [V], Calibration Is Not Control prefix branching arXiv 2606.21399 [V]. This requires a resettable environment. Escaped effects cannot be forked (Shepherd: 'Gate before escape, not reverse after'), and in deployment only one branch is ever realized.
4. **'What would my old policy or model do?' (R5b).** AER mock replay arXiv 2603.21692 [V]; Shepherd CRO [V]. This requires the then-weights to stay pinned and servable (as-of pinning pattern [N]; model drift across versions per 2307.09009 [M, unverified]). Layered Mutability arXiv 2604.14717 [V] finds that reverting the self-description does not restore behaviour (hysteresis 0.68).

**Where R5 is unnecessary or harmful.**
- **'Why did I do this?'** A re-instantiated past self generates a new rationale. AER [V] argues that reasoning provenance cannot be recovered from computational state, so it must be recorded at decision time. NORTH_STAR §5 ('does not reconstruct what its former self probably thought. It asks the former self') has this backwards: asking the former self is itself a reconstruction, and the contemporaneous record is the actual testimony.
- **Future self, regret, backward requirements.** R5d is a rollout plus a question, and a future 'self' knows nothing the present model plus simulator does not.
  - The persona framing has only human-side evidence of psychological or persuasive effects: Future You and Simulating Life Paths arXiv 2512.05397 [V].
  - Agents rarely use simulation and often misuse it: arXiv 2601.03905 [V].
  - ITP arXiv 2601.08955 [V-mand] gets its gains from one greedy imagined future pasted into the prompt.
- **Prevented forecasts and predicted vs realized.** These need a counterfactual outcome estimator (randomization, holdout or a trusted simulator, because of positivity), not a self.

**Validity conditions for any R5 'past self'.**
- (i) No post-t content in context, memory, caches or KV. Aborted but Not Forgotten arXiv 2608.15939 [V]: retained KV flips a protected effect in 25/63 cells, including under LangGraph time travel. ActiveGraph probe E: a fork whose cache was pre-filled from the parent's full log received a post-cutoff tool observation.
- (ii) Tools resolve against the world as of t, not the live world (LangGraph probe 3; as-of pinning).
- (iii) The policy and frame in force at t, not the current one (ActiveGraph probe F).
- (iv) Memory versioned together with the corpus (2609.12766 [U]).
- (v) No parametric leakage. This is moot in a synthetic world but not for real-world use.
- (vi) Before its testimony counts, the replica must reproduce the original decision. This repo's Claude CLI backend has no temperature control (C1), so that is not guaranteed.

**For this repo, today.** None of the scored quantities needs R5:
- The smoke_v1 decisions are world-authored (milestone-2 §0), so there is no agent decision-time state to instantiate.
- `historical_state` is scored as lists of event ids, which is an R2 answer.
- Remediation, the primary payoff, should use hindsight, not avoid it. The cutoff matters only for fidelity and attribution.

An executable past self becomes testable only in the future experiment §0 describes: agent-made decisions with preserved decision-time state. Even there it must beat the present self reading R1/R2/R3 plus a single blinded R5a call.

proposals.track_verdict:
Almost nothing survives on the historical-state track. What counts as a historically faithful epistemic state is already standard practice, and so are the ways to restore and query it:
- bitemporal known-then/true-then/now readings: Memvara, XTDB, Datomic, Graphiti;
- strict-cutoff reads after rollback, with a post-exposure leakage protocol: ChronoMem 2607.27773 [V];
- whole-process forks at turn t: Shepherd 2605.10913 [V], ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V];
- blinded-replica past selves: Self-Blinding 2601.14553 [V];
- AER-grade decision records with plan versions, rejected alternatives, and the policy and model in force: AER 2603.21692 [V, no code];
- records of which policy governed each step: OTel GenAI, MLflow, LangSmith; the revocation guard in 2609.08258 [V]; FiscalQA Pro 2608.09393 [V], which gets 98.3% as-of rule lookup with plain versioned retrieval;
- dependency-tracked reopening: DeepRewind, PlanFence, Corollary.

I rejected four ideas outright:
- "Ask the former self" (steelman C4): AER's inference-volatility argument means a re-run past self is a fresh sample, not testimony. Every "why/what did you believe" question is answered by a contemporaneous record that the baseline can log too.
- Policy-in-force tracking: a join on logged version metadata plus a revocation guard covers it.
- Fact-level bitemporality: Memvara's own benchmark puts a one-clock append-only RAG at 100% on knowledge_time questions, with only 4 of 47 temporal questions separating the two.
- Implicit significance detection (steelman C3): real, but nothing ties it to temporal state.

Two narrow empirical candidates survive. Neither is a new capability. Both use cutoff masking or bitemporal indexing that could be added to the baseline at low cost (CLAUDE.md rule 4), so a positive result would credit existing components rather than a distinctive Tesseract architecture.
- H1: cutoff-clean fault attribution, so that the lessons an agent learns from reopened decisions are not contaminated by hindsight.
- H2: valid-time windows over decision premises, for retroactive facts (class D) that need backfill remediation.

The prior evidence points to a null result for both, and the current smoke_v1 can test neither in full. H1 needs agent-authored decisions with later decisions of the same kind. H2 needs class-D scenarios that require backfill and are authored and frozen before any temporal contestant exists. If both die, the historical half of NORTH_STAR should be treated as fully covered by prior art.

candidates.hypothesis: When a long-lived agent reopens one of its own earlier decisions and writes a lesson from it, a strict-cutoff evaluator does better than the present self with full information plus labelled then/stated/now readings. The evaluator is a separate model call whose context holds only what was known at decision time plus the reopening event; it labels the decision as unjustified-then or unknowable-then. The claim is that this gives more accurate fault attribution and, as a result, better later decisions of the same type, at matched token cost.
candidates.missing_primitive: A cutoff-clean judgement of whether the decision was justified given what was known then. It would be wired between reopen and lesson-write as a non-destructive fork, not ChronoMem's destructive reset. Its fault label would gate what goes into the agent's lesson memory. None of the lesson-learning loops above masks post-decision information when it assigns blame. Frontier Autolab measures the confound but, as far as the abstract shows, does not test a fix in an agent's memory loop.

Examples: 'never trust provider docs', or over-hedging. These errors compound across a long life, and Frontier Autolab's finding suggests they are hard to see. If the downstream effect is real, the fix is cheap: one extra masked call per reopen. That makes it an efficiency-positive reliability gain, not an architecture.

candidates.hypothesis: Some retroactive-fact events tell the agent at T2 that the world changed at an earlier T1, and fixing them requires correcting effects produced during [T1,T2). This is EXPERIMENT.md class D with backfill remediation. On these events, an agent that indexes its decision premises bitemporally gets better remediation success and better reopen precision than a one-clock as-of baseline. Indexing bitemporally means recording, for each decision, the stated (known_at) reading of each premise slot it used, and computing per-decision divergence from the now-then reading when a backdated fact arrives. The baseline has the same model and also has an explicit decision register and a dependency/TMS arm. The advantage should grow with the number of decisions inside the window and with history length.
candidates.missing_primitive: Decision-level, engine-written bitemporal links from each decision to the premise slots it read, together with the valid-time reading as it stood at decision time. Memvara has 'derives' links, but 'nothing in the engine writes one today' and nothing propagates. Corollary, PlanFence and DeepRewind have links but no valid-time axis. They retract on every dependent decision, or only on contradiction, and cannot separate decisions made on a stale premise inside [T1,T2) from earlier ones that were correct for their time. That separation determines backfill scope.
candidates.why_it_might_matter: Correctness and economics of remediation. In software operations, a late-discovered change has consequences: a provider changed semantics at T1, or a config drifted at T1. These need correction of effects within the window, such as re-billing, data backfill or replaying jobs. Getting the window wrong in one direction under-remediates (silent corruption); in the other it over-remediates (unneeded intervention, extra cost). This is the only regime where prior evidence locates any bitemporal edge: Memvara's delayed-knowledge and correction questions, roughly 8.5% of temporal questions.
candidates.minimal_experiment:
Scenarios:

- Grade the number of agent-relevant decisions inside the window (1 / 5 / 20) and the lag (near / far).
- Include negative controls: decisions on the same slot before T1 that need only forward change, plus surface-matched near-misses (TWIST-style).

2. arm 1 plus an explicit decision/intention register with per-premise re-check (StateMemBench / PlanFence style);
3. arm 1 plus a Corollary or DeepRewind-style dependency arm;
4. arm 1 plus Memvara (pip) with an added decision-premise write.

Scoring:

The LLM can read 'changed at T1' in the event body and compare it with decision timestamps directly. Memvara's own one-clock vector-RAG baseline already scores 100% on knowledge_time questions.
candidates.kill_criterion:
Kill if, at the largest window (20 in-window decisions) and far lag, arm 4 (and any temporal contestant built later) does not beat max(arm 2, arm 3) on either backfill-remediation success or reopen precision at matched recall by more than the 95% CI across seeds.
Also kill if the advantage does not grow monotonically with window size: a flat curve fails the §13 'continue' condition.
If a pre-registered census of reopen triggers across the frozen scenario families puts class-D-with-backfill below about 10%, report the effect as negligible in aggregate, even if it is present.
candidates.prior_evidence_against:
Memvara's own benchmark:
- the bitemporal edge is 4 of 47 temporal questions (92.0 vs 89.0 overall);

Other evidence:

- StateMemBench 2608.19652 [V]: explicit current-state structure, not history, carries gains (+15 to +32 under a matched control).

The current baseline forbids temporal fact graphs (milestone-2 §9) and has only lexical embeddings (D1), so today's baseline would confound any win. Arms 2-4 and a real embedding model are prerequisites.

candidates.hypothesis: In a world where the agent's own risk-triggered interventions suppress the harms it forecast, an LLM agent that self-calibrates from realized outcomes through reflective memory (Live-Evo/EpiEvolve style) will lower its risk forecasts and safeguard rate over episodes although the true hazard rate is constant, and this drift is removed only when intervened-on forecasts are stored as annulled records excluded from calibration, not merely when the action taken is logged next to the outcome.
candidates.existing_prior_art: The concept is fully pre-empted. Annulling the unrealised branch: Metaculus Conditional Pairs and the ConditionalQuestion/ANNULLED model in forecasting-tools [non-arXiv, checked via repo]. Potential outcomes: Dickerman & Hernan 2020, doi 10.1007/s10654-020-00659-8 [non-arXiv]. The 'victims of their own success' retraining bias: Boeken, Zoeter & Mooij arXiv:2403.00886 (authors verified via PMLR v236; arXiv id not in the local corpus) and Liley et al. arXiv:2010.11530 [unverified], plus Lenert 2019 and Sperrin 2019. Performative prediction: arXiv:2002.06673 [unverified]. Calibration Is Not Control arXiv:2606.21399 [verified]: recalibration 'leaves control regret unchanged', and prefix branching evaluates interventions. ForecastBench-Sim arXiv:2606.18686 [verified] has paired intervention worlds at the environment level. The LLM self-calibration loops (FutureSim 2605.15188 [verified, code read], EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [verified], Live-Evo 2602.02369 [verified], Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [verified]) all run in worlds the agent cannot influence. FutureSim's deep read says the world is fixed, so there is no prevented-futures handling; Forecast-Dojo lists 'the agent's actions are passive' as a limitation. The 2026 survey arXiv:2608.23058 (cited only in lane text) calls reflexive feedback an open gap.
candidates.missing_primitive: Two things are missing. (1) An empirical demonstration that LLM reflective or outcome-feedback memory actually makes the retraining-bias error; nothing in the digests shows this. (2) A forecast record carrying intervention status (forecaster/policy version, cutoff, triggering intervention, status annulled/checked/unverifiable) that the calibration loop treats as unscored. The record itself is one schema column, not a new mechanism.
candidates.why_it_might_matter: Reliability and safety. Long-lived agents that learn from outcomes (Live-Evo reports a 20.8% Brier gain, EpiEvolve 0.629 vs 0.561 accuracy) are being deployed with the ability to act on their own warnings. If successful prevention reads to them as over-pessimism, their safeguards erode silently in exactly the high-risk region, and the outcome logs look clean throughout. A positive result would be a concrete failure mode with a cheap fix that applies to every outcome-feedback memory design, including the project's baseline. It would not be evidence for temporal architecture.
candidates.minimal_experiment:
Build a small reactive toy simulator outside the frozen benchmark; smoke_v1 cannot be used because its event stream does not react to the agent (amendment A1) and its only actions are reopen and note.
- Run N≈60 sequential episodes. In each, a hazard with a fixed latent probability p is signalled by noisy evidence. The agent forecasts risk and may apply a costly safeguard that prevents the harm.
- The evaluator keeps a randomized 15% holdout in which the safeguard is silently ineffective, plus the latent p, so ground truth on 'prevented' exists and positivity is handled.
- Arms, all with the same model and token budget and memory updated from episode outcomes: (A) Live-Evo/EpiEvolve-style reflection on (forecast, outcome) only; (B, the strong null) the same reflection on (forecast, action taken, outcome) with a one-line instruction that intervened cases do not test the forecast; (C) a typed store that marks intervened forecasts annulled and excludes them from the calibration feed, while still scoring the holdout cases.
- Measure the slope of the forecast and safeguard rate over episodes, the Brier score on non-intervened and holdout cases, and the realized harm rate. Use at least 5 seeds.
- Pre-register the analysis before any contestant work, per CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 6.
candidates.strong_null: Arm B: the same outcome-feedback reflective memory, which logs the action taken next to every outcome and carries a single causal caveat in the prompt. Any checkpoint+RAG baseline can log the same thing at negligible cost. If a natural-language reflector already reasons 'I intervened, so non-occurrence is not evidence', the typed annulment primitive adds nothing.
candidates.kill_criterion: Kill if arm A shows no significant downward drift in forecast or safeguard rate (95% CI on the slope includes 0 across seeds), because then the failure mode does not exist in LLM reflection. Also kill if arm B removes the drift to within the CI of arm C, because then logging plus a prompt line suffices and the averted-forecast record is bookkeeping with no measurable effect. In either case NORTH_STAR §8 / invariant 8 should be reported as covered by standard practice.
candidates.prior_evidence_against: (1) The concept is predicted by causal-inference and performative-prediction theory, so a positive result is a replication of an expected consequence in a new model class. (2) LLMs reflecting in language may avoid the error unprompted. FinalityBench arXiv:2609.04706 [verified] shows LLMs discover finality gating without being told, which suggests they handle related causal bookkeeping. (3) Positivity: outside a simulator with a randomized holdout, the 'prevented' status is unverifiable for a deterministic intervener, so the fix cannot be validated in deployment. (4) The project's benchmark contains no such situation, and adding one means a protocol amendment with a reactive world. (5) The toy world is bespoke, so external validity is limited. The attack phase's own steelman kept this claim only as an untested measurement.
candidates.reuses_existing_benchmark: Partly. The repo harness's metering, trace and evaluator conventions can be reused, but the world must be a new reactive toy simulator because smoke_v1 is non-reactive. ForecastBench-Sim (2606.18686, paired intervention worlds) would be the natural external venue, but its code availability is not recorded in the digests and must be verified first. The Calibration Is Not Control prefix-branching protocol (no code release found) is the design precedent for counterfactual ground truth.

candidates.hypothesis: On held-out decisions whose significance changes only through an implication of a later event (no stored fact contradicted, no declared dependency, no shared vocabulary), adding a per-event prospection step (imagine the event's next consequences, then retrieve past decisions and parked work that those imagined consequences touch) raises unprompted reopen recall at matched precision over the same baseline that spends an equal token budget on a retrospective 're-check decisions in force against this event' pass.
candidates.existing_prior_art: Imagined futures as a retrieval or decision probe: Thinking Ahead, Prospection-Guided Retrieval arXiv:2605.14177 (abstract only, cited in the prospective lane note, not in the deduplicated citation-checked list): 'nearly 3x recall on MemoryQuest', for retrieval, not decisions. Imagine-then-Plan arXiv:2601.08955 (mandatory digest, code read, paper body unread): a single pasted greedy K-step foresight. SafePred arXiv:2602.01725 and SIMMER arXiv:2606.14574 [both verified]: feared futures turned into present constraints. RAFA arXiv:2309.17382 [unverified]: re-planning from the present each step. Retrospective re-check nulls: claim-targeted re-checking in Impact Is Not Invalidation arXiv:2609.25130 (id verified, details from a list summary), derivation re-checks in PlanFence arXiv:2609.03340 [verified], and DeepRewind's per-commitment trigger monitor arXiv:2609.36344 [verified]. The detection gap itself is documented: Corollary probe (b), where a later fact on a different key leaves the decision IN; Graphiti, which invalidates only on contradiction; and DeepRewind's organic path, which never fired in the probe.
candidates.missing_primitive: None architectural. The question is whether forward-simulated consequences are a better relevance probe than backward premise re-checking, specifically for the one capability gap the attack phase found real: implicit-link significance changes. No work in the digests applies prospection to reopening already-executed decisions or compares it with a retrospective re-check at equal budget.
candidates.why_it_might_matter:
It is the cheapest decision-relevant test of the track's core claim, and it gates everything else on the future side.
- If a stateless per-event imagine step does not beat retrospective re-checking on implication-only links, then persisted branch stores, simulation-derived obligations, signposts and future-self machinery have no plausible route to value in this benchmark. They should not be built, which saves medium-to-large engineering cost.
- If it does win, it gives a cheap, architecture-agnostic mechanism for the real capability gap (unprompted detection of undeclared significance changes), and any contestant, including the baseline, could adopt it.
candidates.minimal_experiment:

- Stage 0 (tiny cost, kill-only): implement two configurable baseline variants. (a) baseline-full plus a retrospective re-check pass. (b) baseline-full plus a prospection pass: generate the K most likely consequences of the event, use them as retrieval queries over notes and decisions, then decide reopen or note. Run both on smoke_v1 with a real model and several seeds, and report reopen recall, precision and false reopens on the three near-miss controls.
- smoke_v1's three triggers are lexically joined, so recall will saturate. Stage 0 can therefore only kill: it detects whether prospection inflates false reopens. It cannot support the hypothesis.
- Stage 1: one small held-out family of 2-3 scenarios, authored and frozen before either arm is run. Each scenario has 4-6 implication-only reconsiderations and an equal number of surface-matched hard negatives built from TWIST/StateMemBench-style designs, scored with the existing per-decision reopen evaluator.

- Record the variants as baseline-arm changes, not benchmark fixes (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
candidates.strong_null: There are two nulls, and the hypothesis must beat the better of them. The first is baseline-full plus a retrospective 're-check commitments and parked work against this event' pass at equal tokens. The repo baseline's summary already tracks 'decisions in force with their stated reasons and assumptions' and 'open, parked or blocked work and what it is waiting for' (src/baseline/memory.py SUMMARY_TASK). The second is a dependency-monitor arm (DeepRewind/PlanFence style) that is allowed to infer links with an LLM at decision time.
candidates.kill_criterion: Kill on either condition, using at least 3 seeds and paired comparison on the same events. (1) In Stage 0, the prospection arm's false-reopen rate on smoke_v1's near-miss controls exceeds the re-check arm's by more than one control on average. (2) In Stage 1, the prospection arm's recall at matched precision does not exceed max(re-check arm, dependency arm) with a 95% CI excluding 0. candidates.prior_evidence_against:
Several results point toward the null.

- ITP's benefit is not robust: RAP beats ITP-I on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen, 27.14 vs 19.86 (mandatory digest).
- STALE arXiv:2605.06527 [verified]: in 67.8% of failed implicit-policy-adaptation cases the updated evidence was already visible. KWBench arXiv:2604.15760 (abstract only) finds models state a concept but do not apply it. Both put the bottleneck at acting on held evidence, not at retrieval, which is what prospection improves.

candidates.reuses_existing_benchmark: Yes. Stage 0 uses the repo harness and smoke_v1 unchanged, adding only configurable baseline variants and no world changes. It is not a new benchmark family.
