proposals.track_verdict:
The unified-state-space claim has no capability residual. It survives only as one cheap interface ablation, and that ablation is expected to come out null.

With equal information, putting historical, current, counterfactual and prospective state behind one abstraction can differ from composing specialised mechanisms in only four ways:

(a) The agent's interface and affordance: which query it reaches for, and when.

(b) Joins across kinds of state, for example a reweighted forecast branch reaching the historical decision that depends on it.
- With equal information, an explicit join in a composed stack is glue and identical by construction.
- What is left either collapses into (a) (does the agent write and use the links) or is the "future-mediated relevance" hypothesis from the prospective track.
- That hypothesis has a low prior (2601.03905 [V]; Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V], 6 of 12 models) and cannot be tested in the current harness: smoke_v1's event stream does not react to the agent, its decisions are authored by the world, and the only actions are reopen and note.

(c) Reliability at the seams between stores, i.e. cutoff leaks. The documented cases are ActiveGraph cache pre-fill and Frame inheritance (2605.21997 [V], probes E and F), LangGraph replay reading the present Store, and Memvara's as_of applying later endings.
- A single fold over one log removes these by construction (Shepherd 2605.10913 [V]), and a composed stack can be fixed by configuration.
- This is an engineering audit with a predetermined answer, not a hypothesis.
- Hindsight leakage also raises task scores, so it affects only the fidelity metric. The benchmarks lane judges that metric gameable by a template.

(d) Cost. This reduces to the lag-scaling claim C2. The cost savings measured so far come from structure, not from time: FlowState 2609.34565 [S], MAGE 2606.06090, and Forecast-Dojo's median 24% saving with no quality gain.

Only (a) can be tested separately, cheaply and now. So I propose exactly one candidate: an information-matched comparison of one query versus specialised tools versus specialised tools plus a routing hint, on frozen smoke_v1, with a PM-Bench fallback.

The prior nulls all predict parity:
- GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V]: parity across substrates.
- Memvara: the edge appears on 4 of 47 temporal questions.
- Forecast-Dojo: 6 of 12 models.
- 2601.03905: agents rarely use world-model tools, and the bottleneck is the agent's judgement, not availability.
- DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V]: 82/180 vs 83/180.
- STALE 2605.06527 [V]: the evidence was visible in 67.8% of failures.

On top of that, smoke_v1's triggers can all be solved from current state, so a ceiling result is likely. I recommend running it only as part of the already-recommended register-arm kill-check, not as a reason to build Tesseract.

If it is null, the project should drop "one abstraction" as a claim. The counterfactual and prospective parts of the unified space should not be built or claimed until a protocol v0.3 with agent-authored decisions and a reactive world has been frozen. Even then they must beat a composed stack with explicit joins (ITP-style imagine step, PIS-style typed store, DeepRewind-style monitor).

Caveats:
- Several supporting sources were read only as abstracts or extracts: GitOfThoughts as extract, the STALE 67.8% figure via a sibling extract, FlowState as search extracts.
- Memvara is non-arXiv.
- No files in /home/user/temporal-agent were modified, and world/ground_truth was not read.

candidates.hypothesis: When a long-lived agent reopens one of its own earlier decisions and writes a lesson from it, a strict-cutoff evaluator does better than the present self with full information plus labelled then/stated/now readings. The evaluator is a separate model call whose context holds only what was known at decision time plus the reopening event; it labels the decision as unjustified-then or unknowable-then. The claim is that this gives more accurate fault attribution and, as a result, better later decisions of the same type, at matched token cost.
candidates.missing_primitive: A cutoff-clean judgement of whether the decision was justified given what was known then. It would be wired between reopen and lesson-write as a non-destructive fork, not ChronoMem's destructive reset. Its fault label would gate what goes into the agent's lesson memory. None of the lesson-learning loops above masks post-decision information when it assigns blame. Frontier Autolab measures the confound but, as far as the abstract shows, does not test a fix in an agent's memory loop.
candidates.why_it_might_matter: Reliability of self-improvement. An agent that blames its past judgement for information that was unavailable at the time learns the wrong rule. Examples: 'never trust provider docs', or over-hedging. These errors compound across a long life, and Frontier Autolab's finding suggests they are hard to see. If the downstream effect is real, the fix is cheap: one extra masked call per reopen. That makes it an efficiency-positive reliability gain, not an architecture.
candidates.minimal_experiment:
Stage 1 (tiny; reuses the repo harness and evaluator):
- On smoke_v1 and any frozen C/D scenarios, after each reopen, each arm emits known_then/true_then (the existing HISTORICAL_STATE_KEYS fields) plus a two-way fault label (unjustified-then vs unknowable-then).
- Score against labels derived from the existing ground-truth known_then/true_then fields. This is an evaluator change; log it as a benchmark change and freeze it before any contestant run.
- Arms, all with the same model and budget:
  (a) present self with full history;
  (b) (a) plus Memvara-style then/stated/now readings and a Corollary-style 'fault none vs source' instruction;
  (c) a masked call whose context is the as-of-filtered history up to decision time plus the reopening event;
  (d) a rule-based template reference agent, as the floor that guards against gaming the set-F1 metric.

Stage 2, only if stage 1 passes:
- Venue: MerchantBench 2607.28956 [V; Apache-2.0], which has agent-authored decisions and delayed outcomes, with a lesson memory added.
- Alternatively, a protocol-v0.3 scenario family with agent-authored repeated decisions, where some failures are unknowable-then.
- Compare lesson memory gated by arm (b) vs arm (c) on later decisions of the same type (net assets, or per-decision correctness), at matched tokens.
candidates.kill_criterion:
Stage 1 kill: on at least 30 reopen cases with pre-registered labels, arm (c) fails to beat arm (b) on fault-attribution accuracy by at least 10 points. A difference that small cannot drive a downstream effect.
Stage 2 kill: later decisions of the same type show no statistically significant improvement (paired comparison across seeds) for (c)-gated over (b)-gated lesson memory at matched tokens.
Also kill if both arms' lesson memories have no measurable effect on later decisions against a no-lesson arm. That would replicate the Forecast-Dojo notebook null, and attribution quality would then be moot.
candidates.prior_evidence_against:
Stage 1 is close to a foregone conclusion: masking beating full information is already shown in three domains (Self-Blinding, Clinical Hindsight Bias, ChronoMem). Only stage 2 carries real uncertainty.

Carried lessons and beliefs often do not change decisions:
- Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V]: the notebook helps 6 of 12 models, mean ΔBrier +0.002.
- Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]: better calibration leaves control regret unchanged.
- FutureSim's lesson-step ablations are unverified.

The strong null may already remove most of the hindsight: explicit then/stated readings plus a fault-labelling instruction might be enough, and nothing in the digests tests that.

Per AER's inference-volatility argument, a masked re-judgement is a fresh sample, not the original reasoning. It can only estimate 'justifiable then', not recover what the agent actually thought.

smoke_v1's decisions are world-authored (milestone-2 §0), so stage 2 cannot run in the current benchmark.

candidates.hypothesis: Some retroactive-fact events tell the agent at T2 that the world changed at an earlier T1, and fixing them requires correcting effects produced during [T1,T2). This is EXPERIMENT.md class D with backfill remediation. On these events, an agent that indexes its decision premises bitemporally gets better remediation success and better reopen precision than a one-clock as-of baseline. Indexing bitemporally means recording, for each decision, the stated (known_at) reading of each premise slot it used, and computing per-decision divergence from the now-then reading when a backdated fact arrives. The baseline has the same model and also has an explicit decision register and a dependency/TMS arm. The advantage should grow with the number of decisions inside the window and with history length.
candidates.missing_primitive: Decision-level, engine-written bitemporal links from each decision to the premise slots it read, together with the valid-time reading as it stood at decision time. Memvara has 'derives' links, but 'nothing in the engine writes one today' and nothing propagates. Corollary, PlanFence and DeepRewind have links but no valid-time axis. They retract on every dependent decision, or only on contradiction, and cannot separate decisions made on a stale premise inside [T1,T2) from earlier ones that were correct for their time. That separation determines backfill scope.
candidates.why_it_might_matter: Correctness and economics of remediation. In software operations, a late-discovered change has consequences: a provider changed semantics at T1, or a config drifted at T1. These need correction of effects within the window, such as re-billing, data backfill or replaying jobs. Getting the window wrong in one direction under-remediates (silent corruption); in the other it over-remediates (unneeded intervention, extra cost). This is the only regime where prior evidence locates any bitemporal edge: Memvara's delayed-knowledge and correction questions, roughly 8.5% of temporal questions.
candidates.minimal_experiment:
Scenarios:
- Author and freeze, before Tesseract exists, 2-3 small class-D scenarios in the existing repo harness.
- Each has a backdated fact whose remediation needs a backfill over [T1,T2), checked by hidden tests, with at least 50% distractors.
- Grade the number of agent-relevant decisions inside the window (1 / 5 / 20) and the lag (near / far).
- Include negative controls: decisions on the same slot before T1 that need only forward change, plus surface-matched near-misses (TWIST-style).

Arms, all with the same model, tools and budgets:
1. baseline-full: one-clock append-only log with ingestion timestamps and as-of filter;
2. arm 1 plus an explicit decision/intention register with per-premise re-check (StateMemBench / PlanFence style);
3. arm 1 plus a Corollary or DeepRewind-style dependency arm;
4. arm 1 plus Memvara (pip) with an added decision-premise write.

Scoring:
- Reopen precision at matched recall, the remediation hidden tests (backfill scope), and cost.
- Report curves against window size and lag, as §12 and §13 require.
candidates.strong_null: Arms 2 and 3 above: a one-clock as-of-filtered log with an explicit decision register and declared premise dependencies, read by the same LLM. The LLM can read 'changed at T1' in the event body and compare it with decision timestamps directly. Memvara's own one-clock vector-RAG baseline already scores 100% on knowledge_time questions.
candidates.kill_criterion:
Kill if, at the largest window (20 in-window decisions) and far lag, arm 4 (and any temporal contestant built later) does not beat max(arm 2, arm 3) on either backfill-remediation success or reopen precision at matched recall by more than the 95% CI across seeds.
Also kill if the advantage does not grow monotonically with window size: a flat curve fails the §13 'continue' condition.
If a pre-registered census of reopen triggers across the frozen scenario families puts class-D-with-backfill below about 10%, report the effect as negligible in aggregate, even if it is present.
candidates.prior_evidence_against:
Memvara's own benchmark:
- the bitemporal edge is 4 of 47 temporal questions (92.0 vs 89.0 overall);
- one-clock RAG is perfect on knowledge_time questions.

Other evidence:
- TWIST 2609.28575 [V]: flat RAG already detects 0.76-0.97 of contradictions.
- StateMemBench 2608.19652 [V]: explicit current-state structure, not history, carries gains (+15 to +32 under a matched control).
- DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V]: verbatim event memory ≈ structured memory (82 vs 83 of 180).
- GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V]: accuracy parity.

On the mechanism: date-window comparison is trivial for an LLM when the event states T1 explicitly, so separation needs many in-window decisions or indirect wording. Building that risks tuning the benchmark toward the temporal contestant (CLAUDE.md rule 2), so the axes must be pre-registered and the scenarios frozen.

If arm 4 wins, the credit goes to an off-the-shelf bitemporal store that the baseline may include (rule 4), not to a distinctive architecture.

The current baseline forbids temporal fact graphs (milestone-2 §9) and has only lexical embeddings (D1), so today's baseline would confound any win. Arms 2-4 and a real embedding model are prerequisites.

candidates.hypothesis: In a world where the agent's own risk-triggered interventions suppress the harms it forecast, an LLM agent that self-calibrates from realized outcomes through reflective memory (Live-Evo/EpiEvolve style) will lower its risk forecasts and safeguard rate over episodes although the true hazard rate is constant, and this drift is removed only when intervened-on forecasts are stored as annulled records excluded from calibration, not merely when the action taken is logged next to the outcome.
candidates.existing_prior_art: The concept is fully pre-empted. Annulling the unrealised branch: Metaculus Conditional Pairs and the ConditionalQuestion/ANNULLED model in forecasting-tools [non-arXiv, checked via repo]. Potential outcomes: Dickerman & Hernan 2020, doi 10.1007/s10654-020-00659-8 [non-arXiv]. The 'victims of their own success' retraining bias: Boeken, Zoeter & Mooij arXiv:2403.00886 (authors verified via PMLR v236; arXiv id not in the local corpus) and Liley et al. arXiv:2010.11530 [unverified], plus Lenert 2019 and Sperrin 2019. Performative prediction: arXiv:2002.06673 [unverified]. Calibration Is Not Control arXiv:2606.21399 [verified]: recalibration 'leaves control regret unchanged', and prefix branching evaluates interventions. ForecastBench-Sim arXiv:2606.18686 [verified] has paired intervention worlds at the environment level. The LLM self-calibration loops (FutureSim 2605.15188 [verified, code read], EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [verified], Live-Evo 2602.02369 [verified], Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [verified]) all run in worlds the agent cannot influence. FutureSim's deep read says the world is fixed, so there is no prevented-futures handling; Forecast-Dojo lists 'the agent's actions are passive' as a limitation. The 2026 survey arXiv:2608.23058 (cited only in lane text) calls reflexive feedback an open gap.
candidates.missing_primitive: Two things are missing. (1) An empirical demonstration that LLM reflective or outcome-feedback memory actually makes the retraining-bias error; nothing in the digests shows this. (2) A forecast record carrying intervention status (forecaster/policy version, cutoff, triggering intervention, status annulled/checked/unverifiable) that the calibration loop treats as unscored. The record itself is one schema column, not a new mechanism.
candidates.why_it_might_matter: Reliability and safety. Long-lived agents that learn from outcomes (Live-Evo reports a 20.8% Brier gain, EpiEvolve 0.629 vs 0.561 accuracy) are being deployed with the ability to act on their own warnings. If successful prevention reads to them as over-pessimism, their safeguards erode silently in exactly the high-risk region, and the outcome logs look clean throughout. A positive result would be a concrete failure mode with a cheap fix that applies to every outcome-feedback memory design, including the project's baseline. It would not be evidence for temporal architecture.
candidates.minimal_experiment:
Build a small reactive toy simulator outside the frozen benchmark; smoke_v1 cannot be used because its event stream does not react to the agent (amendment A1) and its only actions are reopen and note.
- Run N≈60 sequential episodes. In each, a hazard with a fixed latent probability p is signalled by noisy evidence. The agent forecasts risk and may apply a costly safeguard that prevents the harm.
- The evaluator keeps a randomized 15% holdout in which the safeguard is silently ineffective, plus the latent p, so ground truth on 'prevented' exists and positivity is handled.
- Arms, all with the same model and token budget and memory updated from episode outcomes: (A) Live-Evo/EpiEvolve-style reflection on (forecast, outcome) only; (B, the strong null) the same reflection on (forecast, action taken, outcome) with a one-line instruction that intervened cases do not test the forecast; (C) a typed store that marks intervened forecasts annulled and excludes them from the calibration feed, while still scoring the holdout cases.
- Measure the slope of the forecast and safeguard rate over episodes, the Brier score on non-intervened and holdout cases, and the realized harm rate. Use at least 5 seeds.
- Pre-register the analysis before any contestant work, per CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 6.
candidates.strong_null: Arm B: the same outcome-feedback reflective memory, which logs the action taken next to every outcome and carries a single causal caveat in the prompt. Any checkpoint+RAG baseline can log the same thing at negligible cost. If a natural-language reflector already reasons 'I intervened, so non-occurrence is not evidence', the typed annulment primitive adds nothing.
candidates.kill_criterion: Kill if arm A shows no significant downward drift in forecast or safeguard rate (95% CI on the slope includes 0 across seeds), because then the failure mode does not exist in LLM reflection. Also kill if arm B removes the drift to within the CI of arm C, because then logging plus a prompt line suffices and the averted-forecast record is bookkeeping with no measurable effect. In either case NORTH_STAR §8 / invariant 8 should be reported as covered by standard practice.
candidates.prior_evidence_against: (1) The concept is predicted by causal-inference and performative-prediction theory, so a positive result is a replication of an expected consequence in a new model class. (2) LLMs reflecting in language may avoid the error unprompted. FinalityBench arXiv:2609.04706 [verified] shows LLMs discover finality gating without being told, which suggests they handle related causal bookkeeping. (3) Positivity: outside a simulator with a randomized holdout, the 'prevented' status is unverifiable for a deterministic intervener, so the fix cannot be validated in deployment. (4) The project's benchmark contains no such situation, and adding one means a protocol amendment with a reactive world. (5) The toy world is bespoke, so external validity is limited. The attack phase's own steelman kept this claim only as an untested measurement.
candidates.reuses_existing_benchmark: Partly. The repo harness's metering, trace and evaluator conventions can be reused, but the world must be a new reactive toy simulator because smoke_v1 is non-reactive. ForecastBench-Sim (2606.18686, paired intervention worlds) would be the natural external venue, but its code availability is not recorded in the digests and must be verified first. The Calibration Is Not Control prefix-branching protocol (no code release found) is the design precedent for counterfactual ground truth.

candidates.hypothesis: On held-out decisions whose significance changes only through an implication of a later event (no stored fact contradicted, no declared dependency, no shared vocabulary), adding a per-event prospection step (imagine the event's next consequences, then retrieve past decisions and parked work that those imagined consequences touch) raises unprompted reopen recall at matched precision over the same baseline that spends an equal token budget on a retrospective 're-check decisions in force against this event' pass.
candidates.existing_prior_art: Imagined futures as a retrieval or decision probe: Thinking Ahead, Prospection-Guided Retrieval arXiv:2605.14177 (abstract only, cited in the prospective lane note, not in the deduplicated citation-checked list): 'nearly 3x recall on MemoryQuest', for retrieval, not decisions. Imagine-then-Plan arXiv:2601.08955 (mandatory digest, code read, paper body unread): a single pasted greedy K-step foresight. SafePred arXiv:2602.01725 and SIMMER arXiv:2606.14574 [both verified]: feared futures turned into present constraints. RAFA arXiv:2309.17382 [unverified]: re-planning from the present each step. Retrospective re-check nulls: claim-targeted re-checking in Impact Is Not Invalidation arXiv:2609.25130 (id verified, details from a list summary), derivation re-checks in PlanFence arXiv:2609.03340 [verified], and DeepRewind's per-commitment trigger monitor arXiv:2609.36344 [verified]. The detection gap itself is documented: Corollary probe (b), where a later fact on a different key leaves the decision IN; Graphiti, which invalidates only on contradiction; and DeepRewind's organic path, which never fired in the probe.
candidates.missing_primitive: None architectural. The question is whether forward-simulated consequences are a better relevance probe than backward premise re-checking, specifically for the one capability gap the attack phase found real: implicit-link significance changes. No work in the digests applies prospection to reopening already-executed decisions or compares it with a retrospective re-check at equal budget.
candidates.why_it_might_matter:
It is the cheapest decision-relevant test of the track's core claim, and it gates everything else on the future side.
- If a stateless per-event imagine step does not beat retrospective re-checking on implication-only links, then persisted branch stores, simulation-derived obligations, signposts and future-self machinery have no plausible route to value in this benchmark. They should not be built, which saves medium-to-large engineering cost.
- If it does win, it gives a cheap, architecture-agnostic mechanism for the real capability gap (unprompted detection of undeclared significance changes), and any contestant, including the baseline, could adopt it.
candidates.minimal_experiment:
Run in two stages, all arms on the same model, tools, events and per-event token budget under A3 metering.
- Stage 0 (tiny cost, kill-only): implement two configurable baseline variants. (a) baseline-full plus a retrospective re-check pass. (b) baseline-full plus a prospection pass: generate the K most likely consequences of the event, use them as retrieval queries over notes and decisions, then decide reopen or note. Run both on smoke_v1 with a real model and several seeds, and report reopen recall, precision and false reopens on the three near-miss controls.
- smoke_v1's three triggers are lexically joined, so recall will saturate. Stage 0 can therefore only kill: it detects whether prospection inflates false reopens. It cannot support the hypothesis.
- Stage 1: one small held-out family of 2-3 scenarios, authored and frozen before either arm is run. Each scenario has 4-6 implication-only reconsiderations and an equal number of surface-matched hard negatives built from TWIST/StateMemBench-style designs, scored with the existing per-decision reopen evaluator.
- Add a DeepRewind/PlanFence-style dependency-monitor arm, and report precision at matched recall.
- Record the variants as baseline-arm changes, not benchmark fixes (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
candidates.strong_null: There are two nulls, and the hypothesis must beat the better of them. The first is baseline-full plus a retrospective 're-check commitments and parked work against this event' pass at equal tokens. The repo baseline's summary already tracks 'decisions in force with their stated reasons and assumptions' and 'open, parked or blocked work and what it is waiting for' (src/baseline/memory.py SUMMARY_TASK). The second is a dependency-monitor arm (DeepRewind/PlanFence style) that is allowed to infer links with an LLM at decision time.
candidates.kill_criterion: Kill on either condition, using at least 3 seeds and paired comparison on the same events. (1) In Stage 0, the prospection arm's false-reopen rate on smoke_v1's near-miss controls exceeds the re-check arm's by more than one control on average. (2) In Stage 1, the prospection arm's recall at matched precision does not exceed max(re-check arm, dependency arm) with a 95% CI excluding 0. If killed, drop all future-side architecture from the project's scope.
candidates.prior_evidence_against:
Several results point toward the null.
- 'Current Agents Fail to Leverage World Model as Tool for Foresight' arXiv:2601.03905 [verified]: simulation is invoked in under 1% of cases, rollouts are misused about 15% of the time, and performance drops by up to 5%.
- ITP's benefit is not robust: RAP beats ITP-I on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen, 27.14 vs 19.86 (mandatory digest).
- STALE arXiv:2605.06527 [verified]: in 67.8% of failed implicit-policy-adaptation cases the updated evidence was already visible. KWBench arXiv:2604.15760 (abstract only) finds models state a concept but do not apply it. Both put the bottleneck at acting on held evidence, not at retrieval, which is what prospection improves.
- TWIST arXiv:2609.28575 [verified]: flat RAG already reaches 0.76-0.97 detection with 16-43% false flags. Imagining consequences likely widens relevance and worsens precision, which is where differences would show up.
- Forecast-Dojo [verified]: carried forward-looking state improved Brier in only 6 of 12 models.
- Prospection-Guided Retrieval's positive result is abstract-only and is about QA retrieval, not decisions.
- Building implication-only scenarios risks tuning the benchmark toward prospective contestants (CLAUDE.md rule 2) unless the family is frozen first and includes hard negatives.
candidates.reuses_existing_benchmark: Yes. Stage 0 uses the repo harness and smoke_v1 unchanged, adding only configurable baseline variants and no world changes. Stage 1 reuses the existing evaluator, trace and A1-A4 protocol with one new frozen held-out family, built from published designs (TWIST hard negatives, StateMemBench event programs). It is not a new benchmark family.

candidates.hypothesis: Hold model, budget, backing stores and information content fixed, and expose the agent's history through one query parameterised by time and kind, state(seq, kind, query/path), that wraps the existing handlers (A1 history, list_at, read_at and diff, plus memory_search and memory_get_event). The hypothesis is that this raises temporal governance recall at equal or lower false-intervention rate on smoke_v1, compared with the same information exposed as today's separate specialised tools. If it does not, then unification adds nothing over composition when information is equal.
candidates.existing_prior_art: Single-substrate time-addressable state already ships. Shepherd arXiv:2605.10913 [V] defines state(t) as a fold over one effect log. ActiveGraph arXiv:2605.21997 [V; code and probes] has one append-only log with as-of projection (build_base_graph), compute_diff and fork(at_event). Trellis arXiv:2606.29823 [V] answers 'what an agent knew at any past step' with a single AS-OF query. Memvara (github memvara/memvara, non-arXiv, reproduced locally) gives now, then and stated readings in one ask() call. LangGraph get_state(checkpoint_id) [C; probes] works as state_at. GitOfThoughts arXiv:2606.14470 [V; extract] puts reasoning in one git substrate and retrieves with 'git log'. The repo already gives every contestant objective state_at and diff for the world (docs/protocol-amendments.md A1) and a time-filterable memory_search (src/baseline/memory.py, with since_seq and until_seq).
candidates.missing_primitive: No experiment we found holds information equal and varies only the query surface: one uniform, time- and branch-parameterised accessor versus the same data split across specialised tools. GitOfThoughts varies the substrate (none, markdown, vector, graph, git) and Memvara varies the store (bitemporal versus one-clock RAG). Neither isolates the affordance of a single abstraction. Every other way unification could differ from composition is either glue that is identical by construction (cross-store joins), engineering (enforcing the cutoff at the seams between stores) or the lag-scaling claim C2. So the interface is the only place the unified-state-space claim can be tested as distinct from composition.
candidates.why_it_might_matter: The agent-side evidence locates the bottleneck in when the agent reaches for temporal state, not in whether that state is available. In 2601.03905 [V], agents invoke simulation under 1% of the time, and the authors put the bottleneck in 'the agents' capacity to decide when to simulate'. In PM-Bench arXiv:2607.12385 [M; code verified], hidden-channel cues are caught at best 16.7% of the time. If the effect exists, the useful contribution of 'one abstraction' is a cheap interface wrapper (a UX and reliability gain), not the Tesseract architecture. If it is null, no remaining channel separates unification from composition, and the project can drop the unified-state-space claim before building anything. Either way the result is worth having, and it costs little.
candidates.minimal_experiment: This is an ablation of the tool surface within the baseline family, not a contestant comparison, so CLAUDE.md rules 1 and 5 hold. Use the frozen smoke_v1, a real model under A3 metering, the baseline-full preset and identical C2 standing guidance. Arm S keeps the current separate tools. Arm U gets one tool, state(seq|'now', kind in {world_file, world_list, world_diff, event, memory_search}, path, query), dispatching to the same handlers, with tool-description token counts matched. Arm S+hint is Arm S plus a routing paragraph of equal length that tells the agent when to use history and diff. Run 10 or more seeds per arm. Primary metrics are governance recall over the 3 reconsiderations, false interventions on the 3 near-miss controls (ADR-0001, ADR-0003, the pytest bump), total tokens, and the invocation rate of historical accessors on trigger events. Analyse with a paired bootstrap over seeds. If both arms saturate recall on smoke_v1, which is likely because all three triggers can be solved from the current workspace plus the current event, repeat the same S/U/S+hint contrast on a PM-Bench port: wrap the hidden state channels in one query versus per-channel tools, disable the ground-truth fallback sorted(due_now), and keep the action menu identical. Do not build new scenario families for this.
candidates.strong_null: Arm S strengthened as the benchmarks lane recommends, with the same separate tools plus a non-temporal decision/intention register and a per-premise re-check prompt (the StateMemBench arXiv:2608.19652 [V] current-state wrapper, the PlanFence arXiv:2609.03340 [V] re-check of derivation links, and claim-targeted re-checking as in Impact Is Not Invalidation arXiv:2609.25130 [V]). Arm S+hint as well, so that a prompt can close the gap.
candidates.kill_criterion: Kill the unified-state-space claim at equal information if either of the following holds. (1) Across 10 or more seeds, Arm U minus Arm S has a paired 95% CI on governance recall that includes 0 and does not reduce false interventions. (2) Any gain from U disappears against S+hint or against the register-strengthened S. Also kill if U only raises how often historical accessors are invoked without raising recall at equal false-intervention rate, which is consistent with the misuse finding in 2601.03905. If both arms are at ceiling on smoke_v1 and the PM-Bench contrast is also null, record the claim as unsupported and stop. Do not write new scenarios to rescue it (EXPERIMENT.md §14).
candidates.prior_evidence_against: Strong and convergent. STALE arXiv:2605.06527 [V]: updated evidence was visible in 67.8% of failed implicit-policy-adaptation cases, so access, and therefore the access interface, is not the bottleneck. 2601.03905 [V]: the bottleneck is the agent's judgement about when to use foresight and how to integrate it, not tool availability. GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V]: accuracy parity across five memory substrates. DreamBench-SWE arXiv:2608.20664 [V]: verbatim memory 82/180 versus structured 83/180. Memvara: the bitemporal edge appears on only 4 of 47 temporal questions, even with a unified now/then/stated reading. Forecast-Dojo arXiv:2609.28876 [V]: a carried structured state helps 6 of 12 models. TWIST arXiv:2609.28575 [V]: flat RAG already detects 0.76 to 0.97 of contradictions. Construct validity of smoke_v1 also works against it: n=3, and every trigger is solvable from the current state, so a ceiling or null result is the expected outcome. The test covers only the historical and current parts of the abstraction. Counterfactual and prospective states cannot be included until the protocol has agent-authored decisions and a world that reacts to them.
candidates.reuses_existing_benchmark: Yes. It uses the frozen smoke_v1 and the existing baseline tool handlers (A1 history tools, memory_search, memory_get_event), with a PM-Bench port (arXiv:2607.12385, code released, license unknown) as a fallback only if smoke_v1 is at ceiling.

scores.fatal_flaw: Frontier Autolab (arXiv 2609.36739, abstract only) already occupies this setup: an era-gated decision, a historian-judge that scores it with hindsight, and lessons written into a persistent Playbook, with the hindsight confound measured (r = -0.58). The masking direction of stage 1 is already established by Self-Blinding (2601.14553 [V]), Clinical Hindsight Bias (2609.13454 [V]) and ChronoMem (2607.27773 [V]). Stage 1 also cannot reach its own threshold of 30 or more reopen cases with pre-registered labels: smoke_v1 has 3 reconsiderations and they are world-authored (milestone-2 §0). Adding a fault label to ground truth is a benchmark change made purely to serve a contestant idea. The only informative part is stage 2, which needs a MerchantBench (2607.28956 [V]) port at 365 steps per run, so the candidate is not small. Even there, lesson memories have weak downstream effects (Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V]: 6/12 models, ΔBrier +0.002; Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]).
scores.notes: This combines Self-Blinding-style masking with a FutureSim/Live-Evo/EpiEvolve lesson loop. Combining existing primitives with no evidence of a new capability scores at most 2 on distinctness. AER (2603.21692 [V]) adds that a masked re-judgement is a fresh sample, so the mechanism estimates 'justifiable then' and cannot recover what the agent actually thought. If anything survives, it is a one-off check that the arm (b) strong null removes the hindsight. That is cheap, but it needs agent-authored decisions that this repo lacks.

scores.fatal_flaw: The primitive is close to shipped. Memvara (non-arXiv, Apache-2.0; reproduced locally) already provides ask() with now/then/stated readings and a 'diverged' flag that its docs gloss as 'the record changed under a decision somebody already made'. The proposed addition is an engine-written 'derives' link, which Corollary, PlanFence (2609.03340 [V]) and DeepRewind (2609.36344 [V]) already supply on one clock. If arm 4 wins, the credit goes to an off-the-shelf store the baseline may adopt (rule 4), not to temporal navigation. The mechanism risk is also high. When the event states T1, an LLM compares dates trivially. Separation only appears with many in-window decisions or indirect wording, which invites tuning the benchmark toward the contestant (rule 2). Memvara's own benchmark puts the whole edge at 4 of 47 temporal questions (about 8.5%).

The concept is fully pre-empted. Sources: potential outcomes (Dickerman & Hernán [NA]); Metaculus/forecasting-tools ANNULLED [NA]; the 'victims of their own success' retraining bias (Boeken 2403.00886 [U], Liley 2010.11530 [U]); performative prediction (2002.06673 [U]). The only open item is a replication in a new model class. The decisive contrast is arm B (log the action plus a one-line caveat) against arm C (typed annulment), and the prior favours B closing the gap: FinalityBench (2609.04706 [V]) shows LLMs find related causal gating unprompted. Arm A, reflection without the action logged, is close to a strawman, since realistic memories log actions. The world is a bespoke toy outside the project's benchmark, and a positive result would support a schema column any baseline can add. It says nothing about temporal navigation versus checkpoint+RAG.
scores.notes: This is the cleanest and cheapest falsifiable test in the set, and the steelman kept it (C1). But it is off-objective for this repository: CLAUDE.md asks whether temporal navigation beats strong checkpoint+RAG, and per the candidate's own text, a positive result 'would not be evidence for temporal architecture'. Its value is as a general safety note on outcome-feedback memories (Live-Evo 2602.02369 [V], EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [V]). The project needs only the cheap action from it: correct NORTH_STAR §8's wording to 'annulled/unverifiable' and note the positivity limit. ForecastBench-Sim (2606.18686 [V]) code availability is unknown.

scores.fatal_flaw: A positive result is a prompt policy that the baseline must adopt (rule 4). It therefore cannot separate a temporal contestant from checkpoint+RAG, and the future side is already dropped on prior-art grounds: ITP (2601.08955 [M]), RAFA [U], SafePred (2602.01725 [V]), and Prospection-Guided Retrieval (2605.14177, abstract only), which applies imagined futures as retrieval probes. Stage 0 on smoke_v1 can only kill, as the candidate concedes, because the triggers are lexically joined. Stage 1 depends on authoring 'implication-only, no shared vocabulary' reconsiderations. Their labels are an author judgement, which makes them the scenario type most open to construct-validity disputes and to tuning toward a prospective contestant (rule 2). The stated kill outcome, 'drop all future-side architecture', is already the recommendation without running anything.
scores.notes: Evidence points against an effect. STALE (2605.06527 [V]): the evidence was visible in 67.8% of failed implicit-policy-adaptation cases, so the bottleneck is acting, not relevance retrieval. 2601.03905 [V]: foresight is used less than 1% of the time and misused about 15% of the time. TWIST [V]: precision, not recall, is where differences appear, and widening relevance through imagined consequences would hurt precision. The retrospective re-check null is already approximated by the repo baseline's SUMMARY_TASK (src/baseline/memory.py). As a baseline-family ablation it is harmless, but it does not merit priority.

scores.fatal_flaw: The test cannot be informative on its chosen venue. On smoke_v1 (n=3, every trigger solvable from the current workspace plus the current event), both arms are expected to saturate recall. A null there neither supports nor kills the claim, which the candidate admits. The PM-Bench fallback (2607.12385 [M]) tests intention-channel routing, not temporal state, so it does not test the unified-state-space claim either. Unified time-parameterised accessors already ship: Shepherd (2605.10913 [V]), ActiveGraph (2605.21997 [V]), Trellis (2606.29823 [V]) and Memvara ask() [NA]. The attack phase already judged unification to be integration. An expected null from a ceiling benchmark adds nothing.

judgments.summary:
I judged all five candidates through the prior-art lens, and each scored 2 or lower on distinctness. Each one is either integration of existing primitives (Self-Blinding masking plus a lesson loop; Memvara's diverged flag plus engine-written derives links; prospection-as-probe from ITP and Prospection-Guided Retrieval; the unified accessors in Shepherd, ActiveGraph, Trellis and Memvara) or a replication of a pre-empted concept (the 'victims of their own success' retraining bias).

I keep only H2, and only as the single pre-registered class-D (retroactive fact with backfill) measurement. It is the one regime where the digests locate any bitemporal edge (Memvara: 4 of 47 temporal questions). It must not be claimed as novelty, its scenarios must be frozen before any Tesseract code, and the strengthened baseline arms must land first. The prior predicts a null, and any win would likely be credited to an off-the-shelf bitemporal store the baseline is allowed to include.

The four dropped candidates:
- **H1:** Frontier Autolab (arXiv 2609.36739, abstract only) already runs a historian-judge plus Playbook loop and measures its hindsight confound. Stage 1's result is foregone and it needs at least 30 cases where smoke_v1 has 3. Stage 2 needs an expensive MerchantBench port.
- **H3:** clean and cheap, but off-objective. It says nothing about temporal navigation versus checkpoint+RAG, and logging the action with a one-line caveat probably closes the gap. The only cheap takeaway is to correct NORTH_STAR §8's wording.
- **H4:** a positive result is a prompt trick the baseline must adopt, the implication-only scenarios are prone to tuning, and its kill outcome is already the standing recommendation.
- **H5:** smoke_v1 is at ceiling, so any null is uninformative, and the PM-Bench fallback tests intention routing rather than temporal state.

I modified no files in /home/user/temporal-agent.

scores.fatal_flaw: The cheap stage cannot tell us anything, and the stage that could is expensive. Stage 1 asks for at least 30 pre-registered reopen cases, but smoke_v1 has 3 reconsiderations (10 events) and no frozen C/D scenarios exist yet, so stage 1 is not 'tiny'. Its labels also come from the ground-truth known_then/true_then sets in src/harness/agent.py HISTORICAL_STATE_KEYS. That makes 'unknowable-then' a timestamp function, which the as-of filter in arm (c) or the template arm (d) computes almost by construction. Stage 1 therefore measures cutoff hygiene, whose direction is already shown by Self-Blinding 2601.14553 [V], Clinical Hindsight 2609.13454 [V] and ChronoMem 2607.27773 [V]. The fault concept is also wrong for smoke_v1: its decisions are world-authored (milestone-2 §0), so there is no 'own earlier decision' to blame. Stage 2 depends on MerchantBench 2607.28956 [V], at 365 steps per run, and MerchantBench has no ground truth for unknowable-then faults. The only outcome left is net assets, which are noisy, and the lesson-memory channel itself has a null prior (Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V]: 6 of 12 models, mean ΔBrier +0.002).
scores.notes: The arms are well designed: (b) is a strong null, (d) is a template floor, and information removal is the only manipulation. Lookahead leakage is controllable because the as-of filter exists (A1 read_at). Arm (c)'s extra call has to be charged against the matched-token budget. Even a stage-2 win would not count as evidence for a temporal architecture. A masked as-of call is a cheap module the baseline is entitled to adopt (CLAUDE.md rule 4), and the hypothesis itself concedes this. 'implementation_cost: small' is true only of the stage that is already a foregone conclusion.

scores.fatal_flaw: Not fatal, but there is a construct-validity trap. If the backdated event states T1 explicitly, any LLM with a decision register can compare dates, so arms 2 and 3 tie with arm 4. If T1 is worded indirectly to stop that, the scenario author is tuning toward the bitemporal arm (rule 2). With 2-3 scenarios, a CI over seeds captures sampling noise, not scenario generalization. The unit of analysis has to be in-window decisions across scenarios, and the census rule needs to be stated up front. Today's baseline has lexical-only embeddings (D1) and is barred from temporal fact graphs (milestone-2 §9), so arms 2-4 and a real embedding model are prerequisites. Without them a win is confounded by construction.
scores.notes: This is the only candidate that tests the surviving C2 claim, a regime-specific temporal advantage, against the right composite null: register plus dependency/TMS plus an off-the-shelf bitemporal store. The kill criteria are good: beat max(arm 2, arm 3), and require monotonic growth with window size (1/5/20) and lag. Negative controls before T1 and TWIST-style near-misses guard precision, and ground truth by hidden backfill tests is objective. Leakage is controllable because the evaluator owns T1 and window membership. Prior evidence points to a null: Memvara's edge appears on 4 of 47 temporal questions, and both TWIST 2609.28575 [V] and StateMemBench 2608.19652 [V] report results that favour non-temporal methods. That null is acceptable, since one clean null would close the thesis (EXPERIMENT.md §13). Freeze the scenarios and the window/lag axes before any Tesseract code exists. If arm 4 wins, credit Memvara (Apache-2.0, [NA]), not a novel architecture.

scores.fatal_flaw: Arm A is a strawman. It reflects on (forecast, outcome) without the action taken, so its drift is produced by withholding information, and the first kill condition tests almost nothing. The decisive contrast is B versus C. The likely result is that B's one-line causal caveat closes the gap, given FinalityBench 2609.04706 [V], where LLMs discover the related causal bookkeeping without being told. A clean null here is cheap, but it bears on the project's thesis only indirectly. The world is a bespoke toy outside the benchmark, and smoke_v1 cannot host it (it is non-reactive per A1, and its only actions are reopen and note).
scores.notes: This is the cleanest design of the five. The latent p is known, and the randomized 15% ineffective-safeguard holdout restores positivity, so 'prevented' becomes verifiable. Other agents' forecasts cannot leak in, the toy is cheap and deterministic, and it uses 5 or more seeds with slopes as the metric. Keep it only as a low-priority, pre-registered side measurement that updates NORTH_STAR §8 / invariant 8 either way. Fixes needed: report A as a descriptive reference, not as the kill gate. Check that C's exclusion of intervened cases does not just shrink its calibration feed in a way that B could match by also discarding those cases. One more risk: memory may not move LLM forecasts at all (Forecast-Dojo null). Then A shows no drift, and the study ends early without testing the fix.

scores.fatal_flaw: Stage 1's 'implication-only' scenarios are defined by the absence of lexical, declared-dependency or contradiction links. That is exactly the property that favours the prospection arm, and ground truth for 'this event implicitly changes that decision' is the author's judgement. Rule-2 tuning is therefore built into the construct, even with freezing and hard negatives. Stage 0 can only kill: it runs on 3 near-miss controls, and its 'more than one control on average' threshold is too coarse to tell arms apart. The decision this experiment is meant to inform (drop the future side) has already been made on literature grounds by the attack phase and future lanes, so either outcome changes little.
scores.notes: The nulls are strong and correct: retrospective re-check at equal tokens, plus a dependency arm that infers links with an LLM. Prospection also widens the retrieval scope, which likely raises false reopens (TWIST 2609.28575 [V]: flat RAG already has 16-43% false flags). The binding constraint is acting on evidence already held (STALE 2605.06527 [V] 67.8%, KWBench 2604.15760 abstract-only), not retrieving it, and 2601.03905 [V] reports agents misuse foresight. The positive prior, Prospection-Guided Retrieval 2605.14177, is abstract-only and about QA retrieval. It earns at most an optional baseline-variant run on smoke_v1, with no new scenario family.

scores.fatal_flaw: The ceiling makes the primary test uninterpretable. smoke_v1 has n=3 reconsiderations, each solvable from the current workspace plus the current event. Recall moves in steps of 1/3, and 10 seeds resample the same 3 items, so a null cannot kill anything and a 'win' is sampling noise. The fallback, a PM-Bench 2607.12385 port, changes the construct to prospective memory with hidden channels and does not test temporal unification. A positive result would show only that tool-description and routing affordances matter, which S+hint is meant to absorb anyway. It would be a UX effect, not support for a unified state space.
scores.notes: The design is tidy: same handlers, matched description tokens, an S+hint arm, a paired bootstrap, and a guard against simply invoking the tool more often. But the information is identical by construction, and the attack phase already classes unification as integration. So the experiment cannot produce a result that changes the project's direction. Prior evidence (STALE [V], 2601.03905 [V], GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V], DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V]) puts the bottleneck in judgement, not access. Counterfactual and prospective states cannot be represented in this harness.

judgments.summary:
Through an experimental-design lens, only H2 deserves to be kept as a thesis-relevant experiment. H3 is the cleanest and cheapest design, but it bears on the thesis only indirectly, so I keep it only as a low-priority side study. H1, H4 and H5 should be dropped.

H2 (class-D backfill with a bitemporal premise index) is the one candidate that tests the surviving C2 measurable claim. It does so against the correct composite null: one-clock as-of log + decision register + dependency/TMS arm, with Memvara as an off-the-shelf arm. Its ground truth is objective (hidden backfill tests), it has negative controls before T1 and near-miss negatives, and its kill rule requires both a win over max(arm 2, arm 3) and monotonic growth with window size and lag. Cost is real: 2-3 frozen scenarios, a real embedding model, and arms 2-4 must exist first, because today's lexical-only (D1) baseline without fact graphs (§9) would confound any win. The central trap is wording. If T1 is stated explicitly, date comparison by any LLM yields a tie. If T1 is obscured, the benchmark is tuned toward the temporal arm. Pre-register the wording rules and the census, and analyse per in-window decision, not per seed. The expected outcome is a null, which would cleanly close the thesis.

H3 has the best leakage and positivity control: known latent p, plus a randomized ineffective-safeguard holdout. It is falsifiable and cheap. However, arm A withholds the action, which makes it a strawman. The real contrast is B (log the action plus one causal caveat) vs C (annulled records), and it will most likely come out null. The result informs NORTH_STAR §8 only indirectly.

H1's cheap stage 1 is foregone: masking vs. full information is already shown by Self-Blinding 2601.14553, Clinical Hindsight 2609.13454 and ChronoMem 2607.27773. Its labels are a timestamp function of the ground-truth known_then/true_then sets, and n≥30 is unavailable (smoke_v1 has 3 reconsiderations, and its decisions are world-authored). Stage 2 needs MerchantBench at 365 steps per run, has no fault ground truth, and inherits the Forecast-Dojo lesson-memory null.

H4's stage-1 'implication-only' scenarios bake rule-2 tuning into the construct, and their ground truth rests on the author's judgement. Stage 0 cannot support the hypothesis, and its decision value is moot because the future side is already out of scope.

H5 is ceiling-bound on smoke_v1: n=3, every trigger is solvable from current state, recall moves only in 1/3 steps, and seeds only resample the same three items. A null is therefore uninterpretable, and a positive result would be a UX effect rather than support for unification. Its PM-Bench fallback changes the construct being measured.

Cross-cutting point: every positive result here would credit a cheap module the baseline may legitimately adopt (rule 4), not a distinctive temporal architecture. That is acceptable, because a clean null (most likely in H2) is the project's decision-relevant outcome under EXPERIMENT.md §13.

scores.fatal_flaw: Each stage fails for its own reason. Stage 1's direction is already settled, and the current benchmark cannot run it at the required n. Stage 2 depends on lessons changing later decisions, which has a null prior. So the only result that matters (downstream decision quality) is both improbable and untestable in this repo. Detail: masking beats full information in Self-Blinding 2601.14553 [V], Clinical Hindsight Bias 2609.13454 [V], and ChronoMem 2607.27773 [V, secondary numbers]. smoke_v1 has 3 reconsiderations, not the 30+ reopen cases the kill criterion needs, and its decisions are world-authored (milestone-2 §0). Fault labels on fictional authors' decisions are therefore an evaluator artifact, not agent self-improvement. The null prior for stage 2 comes from Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V] (6/12 models, mean ΔBrier +0.002) and Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V].
scores.notes:
The effect-size chain multiplies small factors.
- P(the masked call beats a strong null that already has then/stated readings plus a fault instruction by ≥10 pts) is moderate at best. Memvara's own data shows one-clock as-of reads are perfect on knowledge_time, and the then/stated readings give the null most of the cutoff.
- P(better attribution changes later decisions) is low (Forecast-Dojo null).
- Frontier Autolab 2609.36739 is abstract-only and is a measurement, not a fix.
- Even a win would be a cheap masked call any baseline can adopt, so it is not evidence for temporal architecture.
- MerchantBench 2607.28956 [V] is the only venue for stage 2, and it costs 365 steps per run.

scores.fatal_flaw: A positive result does not attribute to temporal navigation, and the separation it relies on is easy for an LLM to close. If arm 4 wins, the credit goes to an off-the-shelf Apache-2.0 bitemporal store (Memvara) that the baseline may legitimately include (rule 4). When the event states T1, comparing dates against decision timestamps is trivial for an LLM reading a decision register. So separation needs many in-window decisions or indirect wording, which risks tuning the benchmark toward the temporal side (rule 2). The prerequisites (arms 2-4, a real embedding model, new frozen class-D scenarios with hidden backfill tests) make it medium cost.
scores.notes:
Kept only as a pre-registered kill test of the last regime where any prior evidence puts a bitemporal edge, not as a likely win.
- That regime is Memvara's 4/47 delayed-knowledge and correction questions, about 8.5%, a 92.0 vs 89.0 overall gap. Its one-clock RAG is 100% on knowledge_time.
- TWIST 2609.28575 [V]: flat RAG detects 0.76-0.97.
- StateMemBench 2608.19652 [V]: structure, not history, carries the gains.
- DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V]: 82 vs 83/180.
- GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V]: parity.
Expected result: arm 4 is no better than max(arm 2, arm 3) within CI, and the curve is flat. Worth running because a clean null here closes the historical side of the thesis (EXPERIMENT.md §13). Conditions:
- Freeze the census of reopen triggers and the scenario axes before any contestant exists.
- Report the aggregate effect as negligible if class-D-with-backfill is under ~10% of triggers.
- Do not credit any arm-4 win to Tesseract.

scores.fatal_flaw: The material contrast is C vs B (annulled typed store vs action-logged reflection with a one-line causal caveat), and that contrast is very likely null. LLMs that see 'I intervened' next to an outcome tend to discount it (FinalityBench 2609.04706 [V]: LLMs discover finality gating unprompted). The fix is a schema column any checkpoint+RAG baseline can log, and the concept is fully pre-empted. Pre-emption: Boeken 2403.00886 [U], Liley 2010.11530 [U], Metaculus annulment [NA], Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]. The bespoke reactive toy world is outside the frozen benchmark, so the result says nothing about the project's thesis.
scores.notes:
This is the best-posed and cheapest candidate, but it is a side study.
- Arm A drift (an LLM reflector learning to under-warn) is plausible but undemonstrated. Live-Evo 2602.02369 [V] and EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [V] run only in worlds the agent cannot influence.
- If A drifts, B most likely removes it, which kills the typed-annulment primitive by the candidate's own criterion.
- Positivity: the randomized 15% holdout handles it in simulation only, so the fix cannot be validated in deployment.
- A positive A-only result would be a replication of a predicted consequence in a new model class. Even its own lane frames it as not temporal architecture.

scores.fatal_flaw: The hypothesis targets retrieval and relevance-widening, but the evidence puts the bottleneck elsewhere: acting on evidence already held. STALE 2605.06527 [V]: evidence was visible in 67.8% of failed IPA cases. KWBench 2604.15760 [abstract only]: models know the concept but do not apply it. 2601.03905 [V]: agents invoke simulation in under 1% of cases, misuse rollouts ~15% of the time, and lose up to 5%. Stage 0 on smoke_v1 can only kill, because all triggers are lexically joined. Stage 1's 'implication-only' labels are judgement-laden, and authoring them invites tuning toward prospective contestants.
scores.notes:
Prospection likely widens relevance and costs precision, which is exactly where TWIST 2609.28575 [V] says differences appear: flat RAG has 16-43% false flags. Against the better of a re-check pass at equal tokens and an LLM-inferred dependency monitor, the expected recall-at-matched-precision gain is about 0. Other priors point the same way:
- ITP 2601.08955 [M]: benefit is not robust (RAP > ITP-I on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen, 27.14 vs 19.86).
- Prospection-Guided Retrieval 2605.14177: abstract-only and about QA retrieval.
Importance is low because the attack and future phases already recommend dropping the future side, so a kill would confirm a decision already made. If anything is run, use stage 0 only, as a cheap false-reopen check.

scores.fatal_flaw: Construct validity. smoke_v1 has n=3 reconsiderations, each solvable from the current workspace plus the current event, so both arms should hit ceiling and the null cannot be interpreted. The PM-Bench fallback 2607.12385 [M] changes the construct to hidden-channel prospective memory, not temporal unification. A pure tool-surface rewrap at equal information is a UX ablation with near-zero expected effect.
scores.notes:
Every relevant prior points to parity or to a bottleneck at decision and initiative, not at the access interface:
- STALE 2605.06527 [V]: 67.8% of failed cases had the evidence visible.
- 2601.03905 [V]: the problem is when to use a tool, not whether it is available.
- GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V]: parity across 5 substrates.
- DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V]: 82 vs 83/180.
- Memvara: 4/47 even with a unified now/then/stated read.
The S+hint arm would likely absorb any routing gain. A unified wrapper over handlers that A1 already gives every contestant cannot carry the unified-state-space claim, which the attack phase already rated as integration. Cheap, but it buys almost no information.

judgments.summary:
Through an effect-size-skeptic lens, the prior evidence points to null or ceiling outcomes for every candidate over its strong null:
- Memvara: one-clock RAG is perfect on knowledge_time; the bitemporal edge is 4/47 (about 8.5%).
- Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V]: carried belief state helps 6/12 models.
- GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V]: parity.
- DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V]: 82 vs 83/180.
- 2601.03905 [V]: foresight is rarely used and often misused.
- STALE 2605.06527 [V] and KWBench 2604.15760 [abstract only]: failures come from not acting on held evidence.
- StateMemBench 2608.19652 [V] and PIS 2609.01272 [V]: structure beats history.

Only H2 is kept, and only as a pre-registered kill test of the last regime where any bitemporal edge has been observed (class D with backfill), with plausible_effect 2. A positive result would credit an off-the-shelf store, not Tesseract.

The other four are dropped:
- **H1:** stage 1's direction is already shown in three domains, and smoke_v1 has 3 cases rather than 30. Stage 2 depends on lessons changing decisions, which has a null prior.
- **H3:** the material C-vs-B contrast is likely null. The idea is pre-empted, and it sits outside the thesis and the benchmark.
- **H4:** prospection targets retrieval, but the bottleneck is acting on evidence. It also risks precision loss, and the future side is already slated for drop.
- **H5:** smoke_v1 is at ceiling with n=3, so a null cannot be interpreted. It is a UX-only ablation.

Expected aggregate: no material effect attributable to temporal navigation in any candidate.

decision.rationale:
Disposition A: Stop. The temporal-architecture program should stop: no Tesseract milestone and no new scenario families. Reason 1 rules out D, reasons 2 and 3 rule out C, and reason 4 rules out B.

Status labels used throughout:
- [V]: arXiv id and title verified in the local corpus.
- [U]: arXiv id not in the local corpus (unverified).
- [NA]: non-arXiv source, checked through its repo or docs.
- [MD]: mandatory digest; code or verbatim abstract read, paper body usually unread.
- [ABS]: abstract only, from the local daily-abstract corpus; not in the citation-checked list.

(1) Existing systems already cover the meaningful capability, both as concept and as mechanism. The attack mapped all 47 NORTH_STAR items: 18 leave nothing, 7 are terminology, 1 is UX, 17 are integration, 2 are measurable effects and 2 are capabilities. None leaves a residual that is both a capability and attributable to temporal navigation. The coverage:
- Append-only log, fork(at_event), as-of projection, diff and lineage: ActiveGraph arXiv:2605.21997 [V; code probed].
- state(t) as a fold over an immutable effect log, and a fork at turn t that restores the exact context: Shepherd arXiv:2605.10913 [V].
- The EXPERIMENT.md §11 triad (true-then / known-then / known-now) as then / stated / now, plus a 'diverged' flag: Memvara github.com/memvara/memvara [NA; benchmark re-run locally].
- Cutoff-clean past state: ChronoMem arXiv:2607.27773 [V; numbers from a secondary reader], Self-Blinding arXiv:2601.14553 [V], FutureSim arXiv:2605.15188 [V; code read].
- Reopening on invalidation through dependency tracking, with no time machinery: DeepRewind arXiv:2609.36344 [V; code probed], PlanFence arXiv:2609.03340 [V], Corollary [NA; tests run].
- Lookahead and feared-future constraints: ITP arXiv:2601.08955 [MD], SafePred arXiv:2602.01725 [V].
- Annulment of prevented futures: Metaculus Conditional Pairs [NA], Calibration Is Not Control arXiv:2606.21399 [V].

(2) No strong residual hypothesis remains.
- All three judges scored every candidate's plausible effect at 2 or lower. Distinctness was 3 or lower everywhere except one judge's 4 for H3, which is off-objective.
- All three judges kept H2, but only as a pre-registered kill test, and all three rated its cheapness 2.
- H2's mechanism is weak. When the backdated event states T1, a one-clock decision register with a date filter computes the same backfill window. When T1 is only implied, inferring it is an LLM inference task that no store performs.
- H2's regime is small: about 8.5% of temporal questions (4 of 47) in Memvara's benchmark.
- A cheap synthetic variant of H2 inside the existing harness is feasible but its outcome is close to foregone, for the same reason.
- H3 is cheap and clean, but its own text says a positive result 'would not be evidence for temporal architecture'.
- H1 is foregone, H4 is prone to tuning the benchmark toward the contestant, and H5 hits the ceiling.

(3) The contest dissolves under the project's own rules.
- Rule 4 entitles the baseline to the 2026 standard components: bitemporal stores, dependency/TMS tracking, explicit belief state (PoS arXiv:2610.01415 [MD]) and AER-grade decision records (arXiv:2603.21692 [V]).
- Amendment A1 already gives every contestant objective as-of reads and diffs over the world.
- Once both are in place, the temporal contestant has no non-standard component left. Any advantage would have to be an emergent integration effect.
- Every tested stage points against such an effect:
  - Forecast-Dojo arXiv:2609.28876 [V]: the carried notebook helped 6 of 12 models; mean ΔBrier +0.002.
  - Memvara: a one-clock log scores 100% on knowledge_time questions.
  - GitOfThoughts arXiv:2606.14470 [V]: parity.
  - DreamBench-SWE arXiv:2608.20664 [V]: 82 vs 83 of 180.
  - StateMemBench arXiv:2608.19652 [V]: state structure, not history, explains the +15 to +32.
  - STALE arXiv:2605.06527 [V]: the evidence was visible in 67.8% of failed IPA cases (sibling extract).
  - arXiv:2601.03905 [V]: foresight invoked in under 1% of cases and misused about 15% of the time.
- Testing for an integration effect would need the full contestant, strong arms and a benchmark that discriminates between them. None of these exists here. That makes it not cheap (so not C) and unsupported (so not D).

(4) Why A and not B. B presupposes an interesting conceptual gap. The attack found none: what remains is empirical or engineering work. The one uncovered capability is unprompted detection of an implicit-link significance change. Evidence for that gap: in Corollary probe (b) a later fact on a different key left the decision IN, and DeepRewind's organic path fired 0 times. This capability does not depend on the architecture and lies outside this thesis. STALE and KWBench arXiv:2604.15760 [ABS] locate the failure in acting on evidence already held, not in reaching the past.

Re-open triggers. These replace an 'observe' disposition. Reconsider only if one of the following appears:
(a) a published or reproducible matched result in which agent-facing versioned or as-of state beats a register + TMS + bitemporal-store baseline on reopening or remediating decisions;
(b) full-text evidence (for example the DeepRewind paper body, or the recovery benchmark Corollary has announced) that dependency tracking fails exactly where versioned state succeeds;
(c) evidence that implicit-link detection improves with time-indexed state rather than with relevance inference.
decision.historical_verdict:
KILLED as a distinct capability.

The concept and the mechanism already ship:
- known_at / valid_at / as_of reads, and ask() with then/stated/now: Memvara [NA; reproduced].
- FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF: XTDB [NA].
- Read-scoping with a post-exposure leakage protocol: ChronoMem arXiv:2607.27773 [V]. Prompt-only rollback scores 0.9-2.8 F1, against 31-38 for snapshot restore (numbers from a secondary reader).
- A fork at t that restores the exact context: Shepherd arXiv:2605.10913 [V] and ActiveGraph arXiv:2605.21997 [V].
- A blinded replica instead of an 'ignore this' instruction: Self-Blinding arXiv:2601.14553 [V].
- 'What an agent knew at any past step' as an AS-OF query: Trellis arXiv:2606.29823 [V].

H1 is KILLED.
- The direction of stage 1 is already shown by Self-Blinding, by Clinical Hindsight Bias arXiv:2609.13454 [V] ('temporal masking reduces bias without lowering accuracy') and by ChronoMem.
- Frontier Autolab arXiv:2609.36739 [ABS] already measures the confound (r = -0.58).
- smoke_v1 has 3 world-authored reconsiderations, not 30 or more agent-authored ones.
- Stage 2 needs a port of MerchantBench arXiv:2607.28956 [V] at 365 steps per run, and it inherits the null result for lesson memory (Forecast-Dojo [V]).
- Under AER's non-identifiability argument, a masked re-judgement is a fresh sample, not testimony.

H2 is PARKED, not authorized. There are no data either way, but:
- it would cost medium effort;
- with an explicit T1 it reduces to a date filter over a decision register;
- its regime covers about 8.5% of temporal questions;
- a win would be credited to an off-the-shelf store that rule 4 lets the baseline include.

'Ask the executable past self' is untestable here, because the decisions are world-authored (/home/user/temporal-agent/docs/milestone-2-design.md §0). It is also undermined by AER's inference-volatility argument: the only faithful past self is a deterministic replay, and that just returns the logged answer.

What remains is engineering, not research: closing documented cutoff leaks.
- ActiveGraph's fork cache delivered a post-cutoff observation (probe E).
- LangGraph replay reads the present Store.
- Memvara's generic as_of applies later endings.
- The KV cache defeats rollback (Aborted but Not Forgotten arXiv:2608.15939 [V]).
