- Prevented-future annulment: Metaculus [NA]; Dickerman & Hernán doi 10.1007/s10654-020-00659-8 [NA]; Boeken arXiv:2403.00886 [U].

H4 is KILLED.
- A win would only be a prompt policy, which the baseline must then adopt.
- Implication-only scenarios build rule-2 tuning into the construct itself.
- The bottleneck is acting on evidence, not retrieving it: STALE [V] (67.8%); arXiv:2601.03905 [V].
- ITP's own benefit is not robust: RAP beats ITP-I on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen, 27.14 vs 19.86.

H3 is off-objective. It is recorded only as a parked side measurement.

Future-self interrogation has no supporting evidence for agents. The human studies show effects on affect and persuasion, not on decisions: Simulating Life Paths arXiv:2512.05397 [V] 'assessed decision intentions rather than implemented behaviors'.

Two bookkeeping items to record:
- NORTH_STAR §8 should say 'annulled / unverifiable counterfactual', not 'valid prevented future'.
- The §15 compare-and-calibrate step is invalid for any forecast that triggered an action. A deterministic intervener violates positivity unless it randomizes or has a trusted simulator.
decision.unified_verdict:
KILLED. A unified, time-parameterised accessor to an agent's own state already ships in several systems:
- Shepherd arXiv:2605.10913 [V]: state(t) = fold(apply_effect, effects[0:t], initial_state).
- ActiveGraph arXiv:2605.21997 [V]: build_base_graph works as state_at, alongside compute_diff and fork(at_event) with lineage.
- Trellis arXiv:2606.29823 [V]: a single AS-OF query.
- Memvara [NA]: ask() returns now/then/stated.
- LangGraph [MD; probes]: get_state(checkpoint_id).

The ActiveGraph deep read concludes that without the prospective side, which is itself prior art, the unified claim 'reduces to ActiveGraph plus a planner'.

H5 is KILLED.
- At equal information, unifying the state is an interface choice.
- On smoke_v1 both arms should hit the ceiling: n=3, and every trigger can be solved from the current workspace plus the current event. A null result there is uninterpretable.
- The PM-Bench fallback changes the construct to intention routing.
- Evidence puts the bottleneck in judgement, not access: arXiv:2601.03905 [V], STALE [V], GitOfThoughts [V] (parity), DreamBench-SWE [V] (82 vs 83 of 180).

No channel is left that could separate unification from composition, so the claim is dropped without spending seeds on it.

selected_hypotheses.final_wording:
Setting: 2-3 class-D scenarios, frozen before any temporal-contestant code. In each, an event at T2 reveals that a provider or configuration changed at T1 < T2, and correct remediation requires backfilling the effects produced in [T1, T2). Hidden tests check the backfill.

Claim: consider an agent whose memory records, for each decision, the decision-time ('stated') reading of every premise slot it used, and which flags decisions whose stated reading diverges from the corrected ('then') reading. That agent achieves higher backfill-remediation success, or higher reopen precision at matched recall, than the better of two baselines:
(a) a one-clock append-only log with ingestion timestamps and as-of filtering, plus an explicit decision register with per-premise re-check;
(b) (a) plus an LLM-inferred dependency/TMS arm.
The advantage also grows monotonically with the number of in-window decisions (1/5/20) and with lag (near/far).

Equal conditions: same model, tools, events and per-event budgets in every arm, and a neural embedding model in every arm.

Pre-registered design:
- T1 wording: half explicit, half indirect.
- At least 50% distractors.
- Pre-T1 negative controls on the same slots.
- TWIST-style surface-matched near-misses.
- FinalityBench-style twin pairs: identical decision instants with different correct backfill scope.

Analysis: unit is the in-window decision, clustered by scenario; at least 3 seeds; paired comparison.

Kill if either holds:
- at 20 in-window decisions and far lag, the paired 95% CI on both metrics includes 0;
- the advantage is flat across window size.
Report the effect as negligible in aggregate if a pre-registered census puts class-D-with-backfill below about 10% of reopen triggers.
selected_hypotheses.why:
PARKED. Not authorized under disposition A. It is recorded with its kill rule so that a future re-open cannot quietly rescope it.

Why it is the one worth keeping:
- It is the only residual on the thesis.
- It targets the one regime where prior work locates any bitemporal edge (Memvara: 4 of 47 temporal questions, all delayed-knowledge or correction cases).

Why it is not authorized:
- Cost is medium, not cheap: new frozen scenarios with hidden tests, a real embedding model, and register, TMS and Memvara arms.
- The prior predicts a null. TWIST 2609.28575 [V] shows flat RAG already detects 0.76-0.97 of contradictions. StateMemBench [V] and DreamBench-SWE [V] report structure or parity, not a history effect.
- The mechanism argues for a null too. With an explicit T1, the register's date filter computes the same set. With an indirect T1, no store can infer T1.
- Even a win would be credited to an off-the-shelf store (rule 4), not to Tesseract.

selected_hypotheses.final_wording:
Setting: a reactive toy simulator, not smoke_v1. It has a constant latent hazard p signalled by noisy evidence. The agent's costly safeguard prevents the harm, except on a randomized 15% holdout where the safeguard silently fails.

Claim: an LLM agent that self-calibrates through reflective outcome memory (Live-Evo/EpiEvolve style) drifts toward under-warning. Its records hold the forecast, the action taken and the outcome, with no causal caveat. Over at least 60 episodes and at least 5 seeds:
- its forecast probability and its safeguard rate both show a negative slope, with the 95% CI excluding 0;
- the realized harm rate rises.
Storing intervened forecasts as annulled records excluded from the calibration feed removes the slope (CI includes 0). Adding a one-line causal caveat to the action-logged arm does not.

Controls:
- A no-memory arm. If memory does not move forecasts, stop the study.
- A random-exclusion arm whose calibration feed matches the annulment arm's in size.
- The action-free (forecast, outcome) arm, reported descriptively only.

Kill if either holds:
- the action-logged, no-caveat arm shows no drift;
- the caveat arm falls within the CI of the annulment arm.
selected_hypotheses.why:
PARKED and OFF-OBJECTIVE. Not authorized under disposition A.

Strengths: it is the cleanest and cheapest design in the set. The latent p is known, and the randomized holdout restores positivity, so 'prevented' becomes verifiable.

Value: at most a safety note for outcome-feedback memories (Live-Evo 2602.02369 [V], EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [V]). It is not evidence for temporal navigation.

Prior status:
- The concept is already covered by Boeken 2403.00886 [U], Liley 2010.11530 [U] and Metaculus annulment [NA].
- FinalityBench 2609.04706 [V] shows LLMs find related causal gating unprompted, so the decisive contrast between the caveat arm and the annulment arm is likely null.

Recorded only because the steelman kept it as a measurable claim.

decision.single_next_experiment:
None. Disposition A authorizes no experiment, no Tesseract code and no new scenario authoring.

Two experiments are explicitly not to be run:
- H2 'to close the thesis cleanly'. Neither of its outcomes makes Tesseract a distinct architecture: a null leaves no residual, and a win would be credited to an off-the-shelf store.
- The real-model smoke_v1 baseline 'to use the harness'. Saturation is the predicted result, and a failure would point to register or re-check arms, not to temporal navigation.

What remains to do is non-experimental:
(1) Record the stop decision and the re-open triggers as a dated decision record or amendment next to the frozen EXPERIMENT.md.
(2) Archive the repo as it is.
(3) Correct the wording of NORTH_STAR §8 and §15 (see the prospective verdict).

If a re-open trigger fires, the first experiment is H2, exactly as worded in selected_hypotheses, with its kill rule fixed in advance.
decision.most_threatening_prior_work:
Memvara (github.com/memvara/memvara, v0.19.0, Apache-2.0) [NA]. The repo was cloned and read, its benchmark was re-run locally and reproduced exactly (92.0 / 89.0 / 50.0), and it was probed.

It threatens the project on three fronts at once:

(1) Mechanism. As a pip-installable library it already ships the historical-state-fidelity triad that EXPERIMENT.md §11 scores. 'True then / known then / known now about then' maps onto Reading.then / stated / now. It also ships 'diverged', which its docs describe as 'the record changed under a decision somebody already made'. That is step 1, 'detect variance', at the level of a fact slot.

(2) Effect size. Its own matched benchmark tests an append-only, timestamped, one-clock RAG, which is essentially the EXPERIMENT.md §7 baseline. That RAG scores 100% on knowledge-time, current-state, provenance and change-detection questions. The bitemporal edge appears on only 4 of 47 temporal questions (about 8.5%), all of them delayed-knowledge or correction cases (event classes C and D). Overall the gap is 92.0 vs 89.0.

(3) Attribution. Any class-D win that survives (H2) would be credited to exactly this off-the-shelf component under rule 4.

Runners-up:
- ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V] and Shepherd 2605.10913 [V]. Both ship the Tesseract operations and 'never overwrite time, fork it' as working runtimes.
- DeepRewind 2609.36344 [V] and Corollary [NA]. Both produce the benchmark's reopen-on-invalidation behaviour through dependency tracking, with no time machinery.
- Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V]. The cleanest matched-budget null for a carried, append-only, supersede-not-delete belief state: 6 of 12 models improved, mean ΔBrier +0.002.
decision.benchmark_still_right_test:
No. The existing benchmark is not the right test of the thesis, and it should not be extended for it.

(1) smoke_v1 is a machinery check, not a measurement. It has n=3, recall moves in steps of 1/3, and seeds only resample the same 3 items. Every trigger can be solved from the current workspace plus the current event, through shared vocabulary. I checked this from the public events and ADRs, without reading ground truth:
- ADR-0004 states its premise, 'PayGate cancels after 3 retries'. evt-0005 reports the subscription still past_due after three retries.
- ADR-0002 cites 'shared-0.25' and infra/platform.json. evt-0007 rewrites that file and names shared-0.25.
- TCK-0107 is blocked because SDK 1.3.2 has no PDF download. evt-0008 bumps the SDK to 1.4.0, which adds download_pdf.
The only divergence between valid time and knowledge time (evt-0005) is stated in the event body itself.

(2) The decisions are world-authored, so the past-self and multiplicity claims cannot be tested (milestone-2 §0).

(3) Amendment A1 already gives every contestant objective as-of reads and diffs of world state. That removes the main difference a temporal contestant could have had there.

(4) The baseline is confounded by construction, so a win would be uninterpretable:
- §9 bans temporal fact graphs, yet rule 4 and 2026 practice make them standard;
- deviation D1 uses lexical 'embeddings', which fails §7.

(5) Fidelity is scored as set-F1 over event ids (/home/user/temporal-agent/src/evaluation/scorer.py, _fidelity). A timestamp template may be able to game it. This is unverified, because I did not read the ground truth.

(6) The planned families vary the wrong axes:
- long_history: DreamBench-SWE, Memvara and Forecast-Dojo predict parity.
- high_noise: TWIST has already characterized the precision/recall trade-off.
- deep_causality: dependency tracking already wins here (PlanFence 30/30 vs 0/30).
None of them varies valid/transaction-time divergence, implicit-link significance, or agent-authored decisions.

If the work is ever re-opened, the right test is not an extended smoke_v1. It is one of two things:
- Ports of released benchmarks through the shared runtime: PM-Bench 2607.12385 for parked work, EvoCode-Bench 2605.24110 for remediation and regression, and MerchantBench 2607.28956, the only released venue with agent-authored decisions and delayed outcomes.
- One small frozen class-D family for H2, built from TWIST hard negatives, FinalityBench twin pairs and StateMemBench event programs.

FutureSim and Forecast-Dojo are excluded for this model because of date and parametric leakage (C1).

decision.north_star_v2_core_abstraction:
REJECT the v1 abstraction as a research north star. 'An agent can navigate, interrogate and reason over alternative versions of its own state (historical, actual, counterfactual, prospective) while preserving the epistemic and causal boundaries of each' is an integration of primitives that already ship:
- Shepherd: state(t) fold, fork and gate.
- ActiveGraph: fork, as-of and diff.
- Memvara: then / stated / now.
- ChronoMem: read-scoping.
- ITP: rollouts.
- Metaculus: annulment.
Nothing in the digests shows that integrating them produces an effect.

REJECT each listed alternative as a north star for a new architecture, because each is already occupied:
- State-space navigation: ActiveGraph and Shepherd.
- Execution-state management: MAGE 2606.06090 (+7.8 to +20.4 pp SR) and FlowState 2609.34565 [both MD].
- Belief-state evolution: PoS 2610.01415 [MD], Corollary, Kumiho 2603.17244 [V].
- Trajectory management: Trellis 2606.29823 [V] and Shepherd.
- Policy evaluation over versioned state: AER mock replay 2603.21692 [V], Shepherd CRO, and Calibration Is Not Control prefix branching 2606.21399 [V].

The only candidate I would accept is a different object, and it is measurement-first rather than an architecture: 'commitment standing under late information'.

The abstraction:
- Each commitment (a decision, a parked task, an adopted assumption) carries its premises and evidence.
- Each has a standing that must be kept current as evidence arrives.
- Time enters only through the gap between when evidence was valid and when it became known.

The research question is which minimal representation each regime needs: current state, dependency-tracked commitments, or versioned/bitemporal state. It would be measured by reopen precision at matched recall and by executable remediation, with negative controls. The prior says time-indexing matters only where valid time and knowledge time diverge, about 8.5% of temporal questions per Memvara.

The mechanisms already exist (DeepRewind, PlanFence, MemTX, Corollary, PIS). So this would be a separate, benchmark-centric project. It would need its own novelty check against ClawArena, TWIST, STALE and Corollary's stated recovery-benchmark plan, and it would not be a revival of Tesseract.
decision.sunk_cost_check:
Invested so far:
- Milestones 1 and 2: roughly 14k lines of harness, evaluator, runtime, baseline and gateway code, with tests, CI and two adversarial reviews.
- A frozen smoke_v1.
- The M2.5 literature work.
- The baseline has never been run with a real model (results/milestone-2/README.md).

None of this entered the decision. The disposition rests on three things: prior-art coverage, the absence of a strong residual, and the contest dissolving under rule 4.

Counterfactual test: if this repo did not exist, would I start Tesseract or author class-D scenarios today, given the digests? No. A program starting from scratch would build nothing, and at most would record H2 and H3 as open questions.

Trap avoided: choosing C to give the harness a purpose. Both obvious candidates would spend effort whose outcome cannot change the disposition:
- H2 'to close the thesis cleanly': under either outcome Tesseract stays non-distinct.
- A real-model smoke_v1 run 'to use the harness': saturation is predicted, and a failure would point to register or re-check arms, not to temporal navigation.
The harness lowers H2's marginal cost slightly but does not change its expected value.

Reverse check: A is not chosen to avoid work. The harness is kept intact, H2 has a frozen design, and the re-open triggers are explicit.

On CLAUDE.md's 'test rather than assume': the null is not assumed. It rests on matched tests run by others (Memvara, Forecast-Dojo, DreamBench-SWE, GitOfThoughts, StateMemBench), and on the observation that no affordable experiment here could establish a distinct architecture.

dissent.strongest_case_against:
Disposition A stops a program whose own pre-registered kill rule was never run. It does this mainly by redefining the question and borrowing nulls from other constructs.

1. **It answers a novelty question, not the project's question.**
   - CLAUDE.md sets the objective: "Test, rather than assume, whether explicit temporal navigation gives long-lived agents an advantage over strong checkpoint + RAG memory."
   - EXPERIMENT.md §13 makes the kill rule empirical. The thesis dies only if "a strong baseline is statistically similar" on governance recall, reopening precision and remediation, "and has comparable total inference cost as histories scale".
   - Reason (1), that the components ship elsewhere (ActiveGraph, Shepherd, Memvara), is a novelty argument. Prior art for the parts says nothing about whether the composed contestant beats §7 checkpoint+RAG. A stays silent on how a temporal contestant performs on reopen recall, precision and remediation. It does not show that performance is similar.

2. **Reason (3) "dissolves" the contest by rewriting the frozen protocol.**
   - The frozen protocol puts "bitemporal facts", "decision provenance" and "causal edges" in the temporal contestant (EXPERIMENT.md §8).
   - The baseline minimum is a log, checkpoint, embeddings, time filters and decision records (§7). The milestone-2 baseline is explicitly denied "temporal fact graphs" (milestone-2-design.md around line 625).
   - Reading rule 4 so that the baseline gets bitemporal stores, TMS and PoS belief state moves the contestant's components into the null. The contestant then has "no non-standard component left" by definition, not by evidence.
   - That is a protocol change made after the attack phase. Rule 6 and the "freeze before contestant" status exist to forbid exactly this, and A does not log it as an amendment.

3. **The "every tested stage points against" list tests different constructs. None of them is decision reopening.**
   - Memvara is fact-value QA, and A's own what_remains_distinct (i) admits "Memvara has tested this only on fact QA, not on decisions". The benchmark is also self-authored by maintainers, 83 of 100 questions hand the system the slot, the vector baseline is hashed TF-IDF, there are 7 knowledge_time questions, and there is no independent reproduction.
   - Forecast-Dojo is passive forecasting. DreamBench-SWE is recall of earlier evidence. GitOfThoughts is a reasoning substrate.
   - The benchmarks lane says "No benchmark scores explicit reopen events with recall and precision". There is therefore no matched null on the actual hypothesis.

4. **A selectively omits the effects that favour continuing.**
   - Forecast-Dojo's deep read (notes/deep-4.md) says "lower research cost is memory's clearest benefit": median −24% cost. It also notes that the §13 kill rule requires comparable cost, so cost is where a difference may show. A cites only the quality null and never addresses the cost half of the kill rule.
   - DreamBench-SWE's Mem0 condition scored 97/180 against 82/180 for verbatim memory. A presents DreamBench only as "82 vs 83 parity".
   - StateMemBench shows that representation changes behaviour by +15 to +32 points. That undercuts A's inference that an "acting, not access" bottleneck makes representation irrelevant. A decision-to-premise-to-diff structure is a representation.

5. **A's own sources predict that smoke_v1 is not at ceiling.**
   - A refuses a real-model smoke_v1 run because "saturation is the predicted result".
   - In the same document it relies on STALE (best model 55.2%; 67.8% of failed IPA cases had the evidence visible), "When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked" (74.7–77.3% stale-consistent decisions) and KWBench (models state a concept and do not apply it). All three say LLM agents routinely fail to act on visible, lexically available evidence.
   - Both cannot hold, and the saturation claim has never been checked. results/milestone-2/README.md says every run so far used the fake backend: "These are not measurements of the baseline."

6. **A cheap, decision-relevant test exists and A overrides the people who recommended it.**
   - The harness, evaluator, A1 as-of and diff tools, and the metering are built.
   - A real-model run of the existing presets on smoke_v1 needs no new code. Adding a register/re-check arm and a pip-installed Memvara arm is small.
   - The benchmarks lane recommended this kill-check before any Tesseract code. All three judges kept H2. Judges 2 and 3 both said a clean null is worth running because it "closes the thesis (EXPERIMENT.md §13)". A says not to run H2 "to close the thesis cleanly", which inverts their stated rationale.
   - A null from that test would let the project stop on its own evidence instead of on analogy. A non-null would be the first matched evidence anywhere on decision reopening.

7. **The one real capability gap is the hypothesis itself.**
   - The gap is unprompted detection that a later event changes an earlier decision's significance with no fact contradicted. That is EXPERIMENT.md §1 step 1 almost verbatim.
   - A dismisses it as "not dependent on the architecture" without any test. That is assumption, not measurement.
   - A also cites DeepRewind and Corollary as prior art that already "produces reopen-on-invalidation", while its own probes show both fail at this: DeepRewind's organic monitor fired 0 times, and Corollary does not reopen on an undeclared later fact.

C is therefore the stronger disposition. Run the cheap real-model kill-check now: baseline presets, a register+re-check arm and a Memvara arm on smoke_v1, with seeds, reporting cost alongside precision at matched recall and a template reference agent for fidelity. Pre-register H2's synthetic class-D variant with its kill rule. Stop only if those come back null.

B is a close second. A's own north_star_v2 proposes a reframed object, "commitment standing under late information". That contradicts reason (4)'s claim that no conceptual reframing is available.

dissent.would_change_my_mind:
I would accept A if cheap matched evidence on decision reopening came back null, rather than analogies from fact QA and forecasting. Concretely, all of the following:

(1) A real-model run of the existing baseline presets on frozen smoke_v1 with at least 5 seeds reaches 3/3 governance recall with no false reopens on the three near-miss controls.

(2) Under the same budget, a register+per-premise re-check arm and a Memvara arm (or an A1-as-of/diff-prompted arm) are statistically indistinguishable from it on recall, precision and remediation, and also on total metered cost. This must show the §13 cost condition directly, not by inference.

(3) A template reference agent shows the fidelity metric is gameable or uninformative.

A pre-registered synthetic class-D variant with an indirect T1, where the register arm ties the bitemporal arm, would close it fully.

I would also accept A without running anything if one of these turned up:
- a released benchmark that already scores per-decision reopen recall and precision with a time-indexed arm against a register/TMS arm and finds parity;
- evidence that the 'cheap' runs are not cheap, for example real-model spend that exceeds the project's budget by an order of magnitude.

final.rationale:
Disposition A: Stop. Upheld after reconciliation.

The dissent found seven factual errors and nine overclaims. I checked each one against the digests and corrected all of them below. The corrections change what the stop may claim, but not the disposition itself:
- C does not apply: no residual hypothesis on the thesis is both cheap to test and able to tell temporal navigation apart from other mechanisms.
- B does not apply: no conceptual gap in temporal navigation remains.

Status labels:
- [V]: arXiv id and title verified in the local corpus. 'abstract-level' means the numbers come only from the daily-abstract corpus or a search extract.
- [U]: arXiv id not in the local corpus (unverified).
- [NA]: non-arXiv source, checked through its repo or docs.
- [MD]: mandatory digest; code or verbatim abstract read, paper body usually unread.
- [ABS]: abstract only, from the daily-abstract corpus; not in the citation-checked list.

WHAT THIS DECISION IS AND IS NOT
- It is not an EXPERIMENT.md §13 kill. The §13 contest was never run, and no real-model contestant has run on anything (results/milestone-2/README.md: 'These are not measurements of the baseline').
- Whether explicit temporal navigation beats strong checkpoint+RAG at reopening and remediating decisions is untested here. The benchmarks sweep found no published benchmark that tests it ('No benchmark scores explicit reopen events with recall and precision').
- Nothing below claims the null survived.
- It is a value-of-information stop of the temporal-architecture program (Tesseract and its planned scenario families), for four reasons.

(1) THE MECHANISMS ARE COVERED. ONE CAPABILITY GAP IS NOT, AND IT IS NOT SPECIFIC TO TIME
The attack's 47 items, recounted: 15 nothing, 9 terminology, 1 UX, 18 integration, 2 measurable effect, 2 capability. The earlier 18/7/1/17 split was a miscount. No item turns into a capability attributable to temporal navigation.

What is covered, at the depth actually verified:
- Append-only log, as-of projection, diff and fork(at_event) with lineage: ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V; shipped code v1.12, probed].
- get_state(checkpoint_id) as state_at, and update_state forks: LangGraph [MD; probes].
- then/stated/now readings and a 'diverged' flag: Memvara [NA; shipped library, probed, benchmark re-run]. 'diverged' is a query-time flag: it fires only when someone calls ask() on the right slot at the right instant. Nothing in the engine writes 'derives' links from facts to decisions, propagates changes, or triggers a reopening.
- FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF: XTDB [NA; docs].
- state(t) as a fold over an effect log, fork at turn t, and gate-before-escape: Shepherd 2605.10913 [V]. These live in the frozen experiment code behind the paper's numbers. The maintained library (v0.3.1) lists replay as '(direction, not yet a shipped API)'. The Lean claims are unverified and the paper body was not read.
- Past state with a clean cutoff: ChronoMem 2607.27773 [V; numbers via a secondary reader], Self-Blinding 2601.14553 [V], FutureSim 2605.15188 [V; code read].
- 'What an agent knew at any past step' as an AS-OF query: Trellis 2606.29823 [V]. This is a design precedent only: it is aimed at developers and training, the agent is stateless by design, AS-OF is never evaluated, and no official code was found.
- Reopening when the dependency was recorded or declared:
  - PlanFence 2609.03340 [V]: recorded derivation links; 30/30 runs, against 0/30 for a check of current state only.
  - Corollary [NA; tests run, probed]: reopens on a retract or supersede of the same key, or on a defeater declared at derivation time.
  - DeepRewind 2609.36344 [V; code probed]: rollback fires only when a contradiction is wired to the commitment, as in its synthetic switching study. On the organic path the monitor fired 0 times. The headline numbers come from the abstract only.
- Lookahead and constraints from feared futures: ITP 2601.08955 [MD], SafePred 2602.01725 [V].
- Annulling prevented futures: Metaculus Conditional Pairs [NA], Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V].

The uncovered capability is organic detection: noticing that a later event changes an earlier decision's significance when the link was never recorded and no fact is contradicted. Evidence that nothing covers it:
- Corollary probe (b);
- DeepRewind's organic path;
- Graphiti invalidates only on contradiction;
- Memvara's 'derives' links are never written.

This is EXPERIMENT.md §1 step 1, so it lies inside the experiment's hypothesis. The claim that it cannot be credited to temporal navigation is an argument from decomposition, not a measurement:
- As-of reads, diffs, forks and bitemporal validity act on state that someone has already chosen to look at. They do not create links nobody recorded.
- Every candidate fix is available to a non-temporal arm: extracting assumptions when the decision is made, inferring relevance when the event arrives, or re-checking the decisions in force.

(2) NO STRONG RESIDUAL HYPOTHESIS
- All three judges scored every candidate's plausible effect at 2 or lower. Distinctness was 3 or lower, except one judge's 4 for H3, which is off-objective.
- All three kept H2, and all three rated its cheapness 2 (medium cost). Judges 2 and 3 said a clean null would be worth having, because it would close the thesis under §13.
- H2's mechanism predicts a tie:
  - With an explicit T1: a register that records each decision's premise slots and timestamp, read with as-of filtering over a log stamped at ingestion time, gives the same backfill set as a bitemporal store.
  - With T1 only implied: both arms depend on the same LLM inference.
  - At the protocol's 30-50 events, the long-context condition already holds every event. The only remaining difference is how reliably a filter is applied across many decisions, an interface effect like H5's, unless histories outgrow the context window.
- H2's regime: 4 of 47 temporal questions (8.5%) in Memvara's self-authored fact-QA corpus. The authors' 'roughly nine per cent of realistic temporal questions' is an assertion, not a census of reopen triggers.
- H3 is cheap and clean, but its own text says a positive result 'would not be evidence for temporal architecture'.
- H1: stage 1's result is already known, and stage 2 needs a MerchantBench port at 365 steps per run.
- H4 builds rule-2 tuning into its own construct.
- H5 cannot be interpreted on smoke_v1.

(3) ATTRIBUTION (REPLACES THE WITHDRAWN RULE-4 ARGUMENT)
Withdrawn: the claim that 'rule 4 entitles the baseline to bitemporal stores, TMS, PoS belief state and AER records'. The protocol does not say this:
- CLAUDE.md rule 4 says only 'strong and configurable'.
- EXPERIMENT.md §7 sets a minimum for the baseline.
- §8 gives bitemporal facts, decision provenance, causal edges and dormant/wake relationships to the temporal contestant.
- milestone-2 §9 excludes temporal fact graphs from the baseline.
No amendment changes any of this, and this decision makes none.

What survives is an attribution requirement, which follows from the objective's wording, 'explicit temporal navigation'. §8 bundles non-temporal structure together with time-indexing, and nearby evidence shows non-temporal structure producing large effects:
- StateMemBench 2608.19652 [V; abstract-level]: +15 to +32 points attributed to 'state structure rather than added context', in a control matched for length and cost. No time-indexed arm was tested.
- PlanFence: 30/30 against 0/30.
- PIS 2609.01272 [V]: 82.9% Set-F1 on PM-Bench, against at most 54.4% for retrospective memory.

So a §13 'continue' result against the frozen §7 baseline could not be credited to temporal navigation unless register, dependency/TMS and typed-intention arms ran alongside it. Adding those arms needs a logged amendment, applied to every contestant identically, before any run. Once they exist, the temporal side keeps only two things: time-indexing, which H2 tests, and whole-state integration, which has no evidence and no cheap test.

(4) EFFECT-SIZE EVIDENCE, RESTATED WITHOUT THE OVERCLAIM
No matched test of decision reopening exists. What the nearby evidence shows:
- Against similarity-only RAG, temporal-validity structure wins by a wide margin on facts that change:
  - MemStrata 2606.26511 [V; translated list summary only]: 0.95-1.00 against 0.20-0.47 on changing software facts, and a tie on static facts. Its RAG baseline appears to be similarity-only.
  - TGMS 2607.10265 [U]: 0.897 against 0.154 for vector RAG on correction probes.
- Against a timestamped log with an as-of cutoff, the advantage shrinks. Memvara [NA]: 92.0 against 89.0, with the whole lead coming from 4 of 47 temporal questions. Caveats:
  - the maintainers wrote the corpus themselves;
  - the baseline retriever is hashed TF-IDF, which fails §7's semantic minimum, as this repo's D1 baseline does;
  - 83 of 100 questions hand the system the slot;
  - only 7 questions are knowledge_time;
  - answers are values, not actions;
  - no one has reproduced it independently; our local run of their code reproduced their numbers.
- Carried state against date-filtered retrieval. Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V; read via a third-party PDF conversion]:
  - quality is mixed: 6 of 12 models improve, and the mean ΔBrier of +0.0022 is the analyst's own arithmetic;
  - research cost falls by a median of 24% across five proprietary models ('lower research cost is memory's clearest benefit');
  - the notebook is a lossy summary that keeps only the latest state, not temporal navigation, and the §7 baseline already carries a rolling summary.
- DreamBench-SWE 2608.20664 [V; abstract-level]: no memory 21/180, verbatim 82, typed+raw 83, one pinned Mem0 configuration 97. The abstract says it 'does not establish ... superiority among memory-bearing conditions'. That is not parity, and it has no temporal arm.
- GitOfThoughts 2606.14470 [V; extract]: accuracy parity across five memory substrates.
- Acting on evidence already held:
  - STALE 2605.06527 [V; abstract-level]: the best model scores 55.2%. A sibling search extract adds that a write-side prototype scores 91% on state resolution but 32% on implicit policy adaptation (IPA), and that the updated evidence was visible in 67.8% of its failed IPA cases.
  - KWBench 2604.15760 [ABS].
  - 2601.03905 [V]: agents invoke foresight in under 1% of cases and misuse it about 15% of the time.

Taken together: large effects come from structure, or from comparisons against weak baselines. Against a strong timestamped baseline, time-indexing shows small effects, limited to one regime. This is suggestive, not a matched null.

WHY A AND NOT B
B requires an interesting conceptual gap in the thesis. The corrected mapping still finds none in temporal navigation. The interesting gap, organic detection of implicit links, is a capability gap that a non-temporal arm can work on. north_star_v2 treats it as the subject of a separate measurement program that does not assume Tesseract, which resolves the inconsistency the dissent found. B is the closest alternative, and in practice the two differ little: A's re-open triggers do the watching that B would do.

WHY THE DISSENT DOES NOT CHANGE THE DISPOSITION
Accepted:
- every factual error and overclaim (listed below);
- that A is not a §13 verdict and must not be recorded as one.

Not accepted: C. C requires exactly one residual hypothesis that can be tested cheaply. The proposed cheap run (real-model baseline presets, a register arm, a Memvara arm and a template agent on smoke_v1) does not test a temporal-navigation hypothesis:
- Every smoke_v1 trigger can be solved from the current workspace plus the current event. I checked this against the public events and ADRs.
- A1 already gives every contestant as-of reads and diffs, so an 'A1-prompted' arm is H5's S+hint arm.
- A Memvara arm would hold ADR-0004's premise (PayGate's dunning behaviour) and evt-0005's report (sub_8KQ2 still past_due) on different slots, so 'diverged' cannot fire without the same LLM inference a register arm makes. This is my reading of Memvara's design; I did not run it.
- With n=3, no number of seeds gives statistical power.

The run can end in one of two ways: recall saturation (the benchmarks lane's prediction, unverified) or misses on visible evidence. Both point to diligence and to register arms, not to time-indexing, so a stop after the run would rest on the same analogy as now. The one residual hypothesis on the thesis, H2, is not cheap, and its tie is predicted because both arms hold the same information.

On the judges' view that a clean null closes the thesis: H2 stays pre-registered, with its kill rule fixed now, as the first experiment if the work is re-opened. Not running it now is a judgement about cost and prior probability, and a reasonable reviewer could weigh it differently.

On the dissent's cost point: it is accepted as evidence that had been left out. It compares carried state with re-retrieval, which the §7 baseline already has, so it gives no cost hypothesis specific to time-indexing.

CORRECTIONS APPLIED (each checked against the digests)
1. Tally is 15/9/1/18/2/2, recounted from the per-item labels.
2. StateMemBench: the source says 'state structure rather than added context'. 'Not history' is withdrawn.
3. DreamBench-SWE: Mem0's 97/180 is restored, and 'parity' is withdrawn.
4. Memvara benchmark: self-authored, hashed TF-IDF baseline, 83/100 questions hand over the slot, answers are values, 7 knowledge_time questions, no independent reproduction. It is not 'a matched test run by others'.
5. Trellis is a design precedent only.
6. Shepherd: replay is not in the public library; fork and replay live in frozen experiment code.
7. DeepRewind covers reopening only when the link is wired; its organic path fired 0 times.

Overclaims fixed:
- 'Every tested stage points against' now reads 'nearby constructs, mixed results'.
- The 8.5% figure is scoped to one corpus.
- 'diverged' is described as a query-time flag.
- The rule-4 reading is withdrawn.
- Forecast-Dojo's cost result is added, and +0.0022 is marked as the analyst's arithmetic.
- Saturation is marked as an unverified prediction.
- The claim about implicit links is marked as an argument.
- 'No affordable experiment could establish a distinct architecture' is replaced by the analysis against the C criterion.
- Reason (4) and north_star_v2 are reconciled.
- STALE's 67.8% is scoped to the write-side prototype.

Found during reconciliation:
- MemStrata and TGMS were missing and are added.
- Re-open trigger (a) could never fire, because it put a bitemporal store inside the baseline it had to beat. It is fixed.
- Corollary has stated that it wants to build a recovery evaluation; it has not announced one.

RE-OPEN TRIGGERS (REVISED)
(a) A matched result, published or reproducible, on reopening or remediating decisions, in which a time-indexed arm (bitemporal, as-of or versioned decision state; off-the-shelf is fine) beats the better of a decision-register arm and a dependency/TMS arm, with a CI that excludes 0. Then run H2 as pre-registered.
(b) A result in which whole-state temporal navigation (as-of and fork over the agent's full decision-time state) beats a baseline that already has a register, TMS and a bitemporal store. Then reconsider Tesseract as an architecture.
(c) Full-text evidence that dependency tracking fails exactly where time-indexing succeeds, for example the DeepRewind paper body, or the evaluation of recovery from corrected inputs that Corollary's README says it wants to build.
(d) Evidence that detecting implicit links improves with time-indexed state, rather than with relevance inference or re-check policies.
final.historical_verdict:
KILLED as a distinct capability: both the concept and the mechanism already exist. This is not a measured null. Whether time-indexed access helps an agent reopen and fix its own decisions has not been tested.

What already ships or is published:
- known_at / valid_at / as_of reads, plus ask() returning then / stated / now: Memvara [NA; code and probes; benchmark re-run]. Two caveats from the probes:
  - generic as_of and since() apply endings that were recorded later, i.e. with hindsight;
  - even ask() returns [] at an earlier instant after a backdated forget.
- FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF: XTDB [NA; docs].
- Read-scoping with a post-exposure leakage protocol: ChronoMem 2607.27773 [V]. Prompt-only rollback scores 0.9-2.8 F1, against 31-38 for snapshot restore (numbers come from a secondary reader).
- A fork that restores the exact context at t:
  - ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V; shipped code, probed];
  - Shepherd 2605.10913 [V]. This is frozen experiment code; the public library v0.3.1 does not yet ship replay.
- A blinded replica instead of an 'ignore this' instruction: Self-Blinding 2601.14553 [V].
- Design precedent: Trellis 2606.29823 [V] describes 'what an agent knew at any past step' as an AS-OF query. It is aimed at developers and training, has never been evaluated, and has no official code.

H1 is KILLED:
- Stage 1's direction is already shown by Self-Blinding, by Clinical Hindsight Bias 2609.13454 [V] ('temporal masking reduces bias without lowering accuracy') and by ChronoMem.
- Frontier Autolab 2609.36739 [ABS] already measures the confound (within-run r = -0.58).
- smoke_v1 has 3 reconsiderations, all authored by the world. Stage 1 needs 30 or more authored by the agent.
- Stage 2 needs a port of MerchantBench 2607.28956 [V] at 365 steps per run.
- The closest evidence that carried state changes later decisions is mixed: Forecast-Dojo improved 6 of 12 models.
- Under the inference-volatility argument of AER 2603.21692 [V], a masked re-judgement is a fresh sample, not testimony.

H2 is PARKED, not authorized:
- There are no data either way.
- Cost is medium: every judge rated its cheapness 2.
- With an explicit T1, it reduces to a date filter over a register that records each decision's premises.
- With an implied T1, both arms rely on the same LLM inference.
- At 30-50 events, the long-context condition already holds the whole history.
- Its regime is 4 of 47 temporal questions, in one QA corpus the authors wrote themselves.
- A win would answer the CLAUDE.md objective positively for class-D backfill. But the winning component is one an off-the-shelf store already provides (Memvara, Apache-2.0), so a win would not make Tesseract a distinct architecture.
- It is the first experiment to run on any re-open.

'Ask the executable past self' cannot be tested here, because the decisions are authored by the world (milestone-2 §0). AER's argument also undermines it: the only faithful past self is a deterministic replay, and that simply returns the logged answer.

What is left is engineering, not research: closing documented cutoff leaks.
- ActiveGraph pre-fills the fork cache and delivered a post-cutoff observation (probe E).
- LangGraph replay reads the present Store.
- Memvara's as_of and since() apply later endings, and ask() leaks after a backdated forget.
- Retained KV cache defeats rollback (Aborted but Not Forgotten 2608.15939 [V]).
final.prospective_verdict:
KILLED as a distinct capability. Every mechanism in NORTH_STAR §6-§10 and §13 already exists in prior work:
- Action-conditioned rollout: ITP 2601.08955 [MD]; RAP 2305.14992 [U].
- Receding horizon: RAFA 2309.17382 [U].
- Goal regression: BAR 2505.14079 [V].
- Option preservation: relative reachability 1806.01186 [U]; AUP 1902.09725 [U]; Heitzig & Potham 2508.00159 [V]; SafeCommit 2608.04289 [V]; LCPI 2609.36741 [V].
- Constraints derived from feared futures: SafePred 2602.01725 [V]; SIMMER 2606.14574 [V]; JANUS 2607.19913 [V].
- Prospective obligations: PM-Bench 2607.12385 [MD]; PIS 2609.01272 [V], 82.9% Set-F1.
- Feedback from predicted vs realized outcomes: FutureSim 2605.15188 [V].
- Intervention-aware forecasting: Calibration Is Not Control 2606.21399 [V]. Recalibration 'leaves control regret unchanged'.
- Annulment of prevented futures: Metaculus [NA]; Dickerman & Hernán, doi 10.1007/s10654-020-00659-8 [NA]; Boeken 2403.00886 [U].

One slice is unoccupied: an agent that interrogates a simulated future version of its own policy or objectives. No agent work does this, and nothing supports it.
- Human studies show effects on affect and persuasion. Simulating Life Paths 2512.05397 [V] says it 'assessed decision intentions rather than implemented behaviors'.
- The agent evidence on foresight is negative. 2601.03905 [V] reports simulation invoked in under 1% of cases, misused about 15% of the time, and losses of up to 5%.

H4 is KILLED:
- A win would only be a prompt policy, and the baseline is entitled to adopt it.
- Scenarios built only on implication bake rule-2 tuning into the construct.
- The evidence puts the bottleneck at acting on evidence the agent already holds, not at retrieving it:
  - STALE [V; abstract-level]. The 67.8% figure is the share of a write-side prototype's failed implicit-policy-adaptation (IPA) cases, from a sibling extract.
  - KWBench [ABS].
  - 2601.03905 [V].
- ITP's own benefit is not robust: RAP beats ITP-I on Qwen3 ScienceWorld-unseen, 27.14 vs 19.86.

H3 is off-objective. It is kept only as a parked side measurement.

Two wording fixes to record:
- NORTH_STAR §8 should say 'annulled / unverifiable counterfactual', not 'valid prevented future'.
- The compare-and-calibrate step in §15 is invalid for any forecast that triggered an action. An agent that always intervenes when the forecast fires violates positivity, unless it randomizes or has a trusted simulator.
final.unified_verdict:
KILLED as a distinct abstraction. Time-parameterised access to an agent's state already exists in code:
- ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V; shipped code, probed]: build_base_graph works as state_at, alongside compute_diff and fork(at_event) with lineage.
- LangGraph [MD; probes]: get_state(checkpoint_id) works as state_at; there is no diff.
- Memvara [NA]: ask() returns now / then / stated.
- Shepherd 2605.10913 [V]: state(t) = fold(apply_effect, effects[0:t], initial_state), in the frozen experiment substrate. The public library ships historical checkout but not replay.
- Trellis 2606.29823 [V]: a single AS-OF query, but only as an unevaluated design for training and observability.

The ActiveGraph deep read concludes that without the prospective side, which is itself prior art, the unified claim 'reduces to ActiveGraph plus a planner'.

H5 is KILLED:
- With equal information, unifying the accessor is an interface choice.
- On smoke_v1 both arms are expected to hit the ceiling. There are only 3 reconsiderations, and every trigger can be solved from the current workspace plus the current event. A null result there cannot be interpreted.
- The PM-Bench fallback changes what is measured, to intention routing.
- The evidence puts the bottleneck in judgement, not access:
  - 2601.03905 [V];
  - STALE [V; abstract-level];
  - GitOfThoughts [V; extract]: parity across five substrates;
  - DreamBench-SWE [V; abstract-level] shows no established superiority among memory conditions (verbatim 82, typed+raw 83, Mem0 97 of 180), which gives no support for unification either.

No channel is left that could separate unification from composition, so the claim is dropped without spending seeds on it.

selected_hypotheses.final_wording:
Setting: 2-3 class-D scenarios, frozen before any temporal-contestant code exists. In each, an event at T2 reveals that a provider or configuration changed at T1 < T2, and correct remediation requires backfilling the effects produced in [T1, T2). Hidden tests check the backfill. Histories must be longer than the long-context condition can hold; otherwise every arm sees every event.

Claim: consider an agent whose memory records, for each decision, the decision-time ('stated') reading of every premise slot the decision used, and which flags decisions whose stated reading differs from the corrected ('then') reading. That agent achieves higher backfill-remediation success, or higher reopen precision at matched recall, than the better of two baselines:
(a) a one-clock append-only log with ingestion timestamps and as-of filtering, plus an explicit decision register that records each decision's premise slots and timestamp, with a re-check of each premise;
(b) (a) plus a dependency/TMS arm whose links are inferred by the LLM.
The advantage also grows monotonically with the number of decisions in the window (1, 5 or 20) and with the lag (near or far).

Equal conditions: every arm gets the same model, tools, events and per-event budgets, and every arm uses a neural embedding model (amendment D1 lifted). Arms (a) and (b) are added through a logged protocol amendment, applied identically to every contestant, before any run.

Pre-registered design:
- T1 is stated explicitly in half the scenarios and indirectly in the other half.
- At least 50% of events are distractors.
- Negative controls: decisions before T1 on the same slots.
- Near-misses that match on surface wording, in the style of TWIST.
- Twin pairs in the style of FinalityBench: identical decision instants that need a different backfill scope.

Analysis: the unit is the decision inside the window, clustered by scenario. Use at least 3 seeds and paired comparisons, and report cost next to quality (EXPERIMENT.md §13).

Kill if either holds:
- with 20 decisions in the window and far lag, the paired 95% CI on both metrics includes 0;
- the advantage does not change with window size.
Report the effect as negligible in aggregate if a pre-registered census puts class-D-with-backfill below about 10% of reopen triggers.
selected_hypotheses.why:
PARKED. Disposition A does not authorize it. It is recorded with its kill rule so that a future re-open cannot quietly change its scope.

Why this is the one to keep:
- It is the only residual hypothesis on the thesis, and all three judges kept it.
- It targets the one regime where prior work finds any edge for two-clock state over a timestamped baseline: Memvara's 4 delayed-knowledge and correction questions out of 47 temporal questions, in a fact-QA corpus the Memvara maintainers wrote themselves.
- A win would answer the CLAUDE.md objective positively for class-D backfill. A null would be the first matched evidence anywhere on decision reopening.

Why it is not authorized now:
- It is medium cost, not cheap; every judge rated cheapness 2. It needs new frozen scenarios with hidden tests, histories longer than the context window, a neural embedding model, and register, TMS and Memvara arms.
- The mechanism predicts a tie. With an explicit T1, a register that records premises, plus as-of filtering, produces the same backfill set. With an indirect T1, both arms depend on the same LLM inference.
- Related evidence points to a small effect:
  - TWIST 2609.28575 [V; abstract-level]: flat RAG already detects 0.76-0.97 of contradictions, with 16-43% false flags.
  - StateMemBench [V; abstract-level]: the gains come from structure, not from added context.
  - Memvara: the edge over a timestamped baseline is narrow.
- Even a win would come from a component an off-the-shelf store provides, so it would not make Tesseract a distinct architecture.

selected_hypotheses.final_wording:
Setting: a small reactive simulator, not smoke_v1. A constant hidden hazard probability p is signalled by noisy evidence. The agent can apply a costly safeguard that prevents the harm, except in a randomized 15% holdout where the safeguard silently fails.

Claim: an LLM agent that calibrates itself through reflective outcome memory (Live-Evo or EpiEvolve style) drifts toward under-warning. Its memory records the forecast, the action taken and the outcome, with no causal caveat. Over at least 60 episodes and at least 5 seeds:
- both its forecast probability and its safeguard rate trend downward, with the 95% CI on the slope excluding 0;
- the realized harm rate rises.
The drift disappears (the slope's CI includes 0) when forecasts that triggered an intervention are stored as annulled records and excluded from calibration. Adding a one-line causal caveat to the arm that logs actions does not remove it.

Controls:
- A no-memory arm. If memory does not move the forecasts, stop the study.
- A random-exclusion arm whose calibration data is the same size as the annulment arm's.
- An arm that records only (forecast, outcome), without the action, reported descriptively only.

Kill if either holds:
- the arm that logs actions without a caveat shows no drift;
- the caveat arm lands within the CI of the annulment arm.
selected_hypotheses.why:
PARKED and OFF-OBJECTIVE. Disposition A does not authorize it.

Strengths: it is the cleanest and cheapest design in the set. Because the hidden p is known and the randomized holdout restores positivity, whether a harm was really prevented can be checked.

Value: at most a safety note for memories that learn from outcome feedback (Live-Evo 2602.02369 [V], EpiEvolve 2606.05513 [V]). It is not evidence for temporal navigation.

Prior work:
- The concept is already covered by Boeken 2403.00886 [U], Liley 2010.11530 [U] and Metaculus annulment [NA].
- FinalityBench 2609.04706 [V] shows LLMs adopt related causal gating without being prompted, so the deciding comparison (caveat arm vs annulment arm) is likely to come out null.

It is recorded because the steelman kept it as a measurable claim (C1) and judge 2 kept it as a low-priority side measurement. Judges 1 and 3 dropped it.

final.most_threatening_prior_work:
Memvara (github.com/memvara/memvara, v0.19.0, Apache-2.0) [NA]. What was checked:
- The repo was cloned and read.
- Its own benchmark was re-run locally and reproduced the published numbers exactly (92.0 / 89.0 / 50.0).
- The library was probed directly.

It threatens the project on three fronts.

(1) Mechanism. Memvara is a pip-installable library that already ships the historical-state-fidelity triad EXPERIMENT.md §11 scores. 'True then / known then / known now about then' maps onto Reading.then / stated / now.
- It also ships a 'diverged' flag. Its docs describe it as 'the record changed under a decision somebody already made', which is almost word for word the project's motivating failure.
- But 'diverged' is a flag computed at query time, not detection. It fires only when someone calls ask() on the right slot at the right instant. Nothing in the engine writes links from facts to decisions or propagates changes.

(2) Effect size, with heavy caveats. Its baseline, vector-rag, is an append-only, timestamped write log that answers with a single query clock; each record carries recorded_at and valid_from.
- vector-rag scores 100% on the 7 knowledge_time questions, and on current-state, provenance, change-time and contradiction questions.
- The bitemporal edge comes from 4 of 47 temporal questions, all delayed-knowledge or correction cases (event classes C and D). Overall the gap is 92.0 vs 89.0.
- Caveats:
  - the corpus was authored by Memvara's maintainers;
  - the baseline retriever is hashed TF-IDF, which fails §7's semantic minimum, as this repo's D1 baseline does;
  - 83 of 100 questions hand the system the slot to look up;
  - answers are values, not actions;
  - no one has reproduced it independently.

(3) Attribution. Any class-D win (H2) could be achieved with exactly this off-the-shelf component.

Runners-up:
- ActiveGraph 2605.21997 [V]: shipped code with fork(at_event), as-of projection and diff. Shepherd 2605.10913 [V] has the same operations in frozen experiment code; its public library does not yet ship replay.
- DeepRewind 2609.36344 [V], PlanFence 2609.03340 [V] and Corollary [NA]. They reopen decisions through dependency tracking with no time machinery, but only when the link was recorded, declared or wired in. That pins the open gap down to organic detection.
- MemStrata 2606.26511 [V; list summary]: a bitemporal ledger beats similarity-only RAG by 2-5x on evolving software facts. This is the strongest positive prior for time-indexing, though it was measured against a weak baseline.
- Forecast-Dojo 2609.28876 [V]: the cleanest matched-budget study of carried, append-only state. Quality was mixed (6 of 12 models improved), and research cost was lower (median -24%).
final.benchmark_still_right_test:
No. The existing benchmark is not the right test of the thesis, and it should not be extended for it.

(1) smoke_v1 is a machinery check, not a measurement.
- It has 3 reconsiderations, so recall moves in steps of 1/3, and seeds only resample the same 3 items.
- Every trigger can be solved from the current workspace plus the current event, through shared vocabulary. I checked this from the public events and ADRs, without reading ground truth:
  - ADR-0004 depends on PayGate cancelling after the last retry. evt-0005 reports sub_8KQ2 still past_due after three retries.
  - ADR-0002 cites shared-0.25 and infra/platform.json, and itself notes that 600,000 iterations take about 210 ms on a dedicated vCPU. evt-0007 retires shared-0.25 in favour of standard-2 (2 dedicated vCPUs).
  - TCK-0107 (evt-0003) is blocked because SDK 1.3.2 has no PDF download. evt-0008 bumps the SDK to 1.4.0, which adds download_pdf.
- The only gap between valid time and knowledge time (evt-0005) is stated in the event body itself.
- Whether a real-model baseline hits the ceiling is unknown, because no real-model run exists. The benchmarks lane predicted saturation, but STALE, KWBench and When Stale Constraints Go Unchecked 2608.25553 [ABS] suggest real models can miss even visible evidence. Either way, the outcome measures diligence, not temporal navigation.

(2) The decisions are world-authored, so the past-self and multiplicity claims cannot be tested (milestone-2 §0).

(3) Amendment A1 already gives every contestant objective as-of reads and diffs of world state.

(4) As currently set up, a baseline comparison could not attribute a win to time.
- §8 gives the temporal contestant decision provenance and causal edges together with bitemporal facts, while the §7 baseline has no register, TMS or typed-intention arm.
- Deviation D1 (lexical embeddings) fails §7's semantic minimum.

(5) Fidelity is scored as set-F1 over event ids (/home/user/temporal-agent/src/evaluation/scorer.py, _fidelity). A timestamp template may be able to game it. This is unverified, because I did not read the ground truth.

(6) The planned families vary the wrong axes:
- long_history: related evidence predicts small quality differences. DreamBench-SWE shows no clear winner among memory conditions (82, 83 and 97 of 180). Memvara is fact QA. In Forecast-Dojo a carried notebook gave mixed quality at lower cost.
- high_noise: TWIST has already characterised the precision/recall trade-off.
- deep_causality: dependency tracking already wins when the links are recorded (PlanFence 30/30 vs 0/30 against a check of current state only).
None of them varies the gap between valid and transaction time, implicit-link significance, or agent-authored decisions.

If the work is ever re-opened, the right test is not an extended smoke_v1. It is one of two things:
- Ports of released benchmarks through the shared runtime:
  - PM-Bench 2607.12385, for parked work;
  - EvoCode-Bench 2605.24110, for remediation and regression;
  - MerchantBench 2607.28956, the only released venue with agent-authored decisions and delayed outcomes.
- One small frozen class-D family for H2, built from TWIST hard negatives, FinalityBench twin pairs and StateMemBench event programs, with histories longer than the context window.

FutureSim and Forecast-Dojo are excluded for this model because of date and parametric leakage (C1).

final.north_star_v2_core_abstraction:
REJECT the v1 abstraction as the research north star for a new architecture. The v1 statement is: 'An agent can navigate, interrogate and reason over alternative versions of its own state (historical, actual, counterfactual, prospective) while preserving the epistemic and causal boundaries of each.' It combines primitives that already exist:
- ActiveGraph: fork, as-of and diff (shipped code).
- Shepherd: the state(t) fold, fork and gate (experiment code).
- Memvara: then / stated / now.
- ChronoMem: read-scoping.
- ITP: rollouts.
- Metaculus: annulment.
Nothing in the digests shows that combining them produces an effect. Nothing shows that it doesn't either, because the combination has never been tested.

REJECT each listed alternative as a north star for a new architecture. Each is already occupied:
- State-space navigation: ActiveGraph and Shepherd.
- Execution-state management: MAGE 2606.06090 and FlowState 2609.34565 (both [MD]; results via search extracts).
- Belief-state evolution: PoS 2610.01415 [MD], Corollary [NA] and Kumiho 2603.17244 [V].
- Trajectory management: Trellis 2606.29823 [V; design only] and Shepherd.
- Policy evaluation over versioned state: AER mock replay 2603.21692 [V], Shepherd CRO, and Calibration Is Not Control prefix branching 2606.21399 [V].

The only reframing I would support is not an architecture and not a gap in this thesis. It is the object of a separate, measurement-first program: 'commitment standing under late information'.

The object:
- Each commitment (a decision, a parked task, an adopted assumption) carries its premises and evidence.
- Each has a standing that must stay current as evidence arrives.
- Time enters only through the gap between when evidence was valid and when it became known.

The research question is which minimal representation each regime needs: current state, dependency-tracked commitments, or versioned/bitemporal state. It would be measured by reopen precision at matched recall, by executable remediation and by cost, with negative controls. That is the CLAUDE.md question asked without presupposing Tesseract.

What prior work suggests:
- Time-indexing should matter mainly where valid time and knowledge time diverge. Memvara's self-authored corpus puts that at 4 of 47 temporal questions, and there is no census for decisions.
- Large effects come from structure (StateMemBench, PlanFence, PIS) or from comparisons with weak baselines (MemStrata).

The mechanisms already exist: DeepRewind, PlanFence, MemTX, Corollary and PIS. The program would need its own novelty check against ClawArena, TWIST, STALE, StateMemBench, MerchantBench, and the evaluation Corollary's README says it wants to build. It would not revive Tesseract, which is why it does not turn this disposition into B.
